> Machine-readable index of every page on https://axomexam.in. Each entry lists the canonical URL, page title, a short description and, for question-bank pages, the questions with their answers. ## Core pages

### axomexam | Assam Competitive Exams — Mock Tests, PYQs & PDF Notes
URL: https://axomexam.in/
Summary: Free bilingual (Assamese & English) Q&A, mock tests and PDF notes for Assam competitive exams — ADRE 2.0 & 3.0, APSC, Assam Police, SSC and Railway preparation.
Q: Is axomexam free to use?
A: Yes. axomexam is completely free. All mock tests, previous year solved papers and PDF notes are available without registration or payment.
Q: Which exams does axomexam cover?
A: axomexam covers Assam state exams such as ADRE (Assam Direct Recruitment Examination), APSC, Assam Police / SLPRB, DHS and DME/DTE, as well as central exams including SSC (CGL, CHSL, GD) and Railway (RRB NTPC, Group D).
Q: Are the questions available in Assamese as well as English?
A: Yes. Every question, answer and explanation on axomexam is bilingual, so you can practise in both Assamese and English.
Q: Does axomexam provide timed mock tests?
A: Yes. axomexam mock tests run on a live timer and follow the real exam pattern, with instant results and answer explanations.
Q: Can I download PDF notes and previous year papers?
A: Yes. PDF study notes, e-books and previous year solved papers can be downloaded for offline practice.
Q: Do I need an account to practise on axomexam?
A: No. You can start practising mock tests and questions immediately without creating an account.

### Tenses | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/english/grammar/tenses/
Summary: English tenses - present, past and future forms with time markers and common errors asked in Assam competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'She ___ to school every day.'
A: (A) goes — 'Every day' shows a habit, so we use the simple present. With 'she' we add 's/es'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The sun ___ in the east.'
A: (A) rises — A universal truth is always in the simple present tense.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'Look! It ___ (rain) now.'
A: (A) is raining — An action happening now uses the present continuous (is + ing).
Q: Fill in the blank: 'She ___ (cook) dinner at present.'
A: (A) is cooking — 'At present' indicates an action going on now, so present continuous.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I ___ (finish) my homework just now.'
A: (A) have finished — 'Just' suggests a recently completed action, so we use the present perfect.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'He ___ (live) here since 2005.'
A: (A) has lived — 'Since + a point of time' with an action still continuing takes the present perfect.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'They ___ (play) cricket for two hours.'
A: (A) have been playing — 'For + a period' with an action started in the past and still going on takes the present perfect continuous.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I ___ (visit) my uncle last week.'
A: (A) visited — 'Last week' is a finished past time, so we use the simple past.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The baby ___ (cry) when I came in.'
A: (A) was crying — An action going on when another past action happened uses the past continuous.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The train ___ (leave) before we reached the station.'
A: (A) had left — An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'He ___ (work) for three hours before the boss came.'
A: (A) had been working — An action continuing up to a past point uses the past perfect continuous.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I ___ (call) you tomorrow.'
A: (A) will call — 'Tomorrow' indicates a future action, so we use 'will + verb'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'She ___ (finish) the work by evening.'
A: (A) will have finished — 'By + a future time' showing completion takes the future perfect.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'This time next week I ___ (travel) to Delhi.'
A: (A) will be travelling — An action in progress at a certain future time uses the future continuous.
Q: 'Since morning' is a marker mainly used with which tense?
A: (A) Present perfect continuous — 'Since + a starting point' is typical of the present perfect / present perfect continuous tense.
Q: 'Yesterday' is a marker mainly used with which tense?
A: (A) Simple past — 'Yesterday' points to a finished past time, so the simple past is used.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I met him two days ___.'
A: (A) ago — 'Ago' is used with a past time and the simple past tense.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'She has been working here ___ 2019.'
A: (A) since — A point of time (2019) takes 'since' in the present perfect.
Q: Which verb does not take the continuous form?
A: (A) know — 'Know' is a stative verb (state, not action), so we say 'I know', not 'I am knowing'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'He ___ (know) the answer to this question.'
A: (A) knows — Stative verbs like 'know' are not used in the continuous form.
Q: 'Every day' is a marker mainly used with which tense?
A: (A) Simple present — 'Every day' shows a routine, so the simple present tense is used.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The earth ___ round the sun.'
A: (A) moves — Scientific truths are expressed in the simple present tense.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'I ___ (see) him yesterday.'
A: (A) saw — 'Yesterday' takes the simple past. The past of 'see' is 'saw'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'She ___ (not, go) to Guwahati last month.'
A: (A) did not go — The negative of the simple past is made with 'did not + base verb'.
Q: Fill in the blank: '___ you ___ (eat) your breakfast yet?'
A: (A) Have ... eaten — 'Yet' is used with the present perfect: 'Have + past participle'.

A: Yes. All 25 Tenses questions, answers and explanations on axomexam.in are completely free. No login or subscription is required.
Q: Are Tenses questions available in Assamese?
A: Yes. Every question and answer is bilingual, so you can practise the same content in both Assamese and English.
Q: Which exams benefit from Tenses questions?
A: Tenses is useful for ADRE 2.0 (Grade III & IV), Assam Police, APSC, Gauhati High Court, SSC and Railway exams.

### Parts of Speech | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/english/parts-of-speech/
Summary: Parts of speech (noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection, articles/determiners) with types, examples and common errors asked in Assam competitive exams (APSC, Assam Police, DME, etc.).
Q: Which of these is a proper noun?
A: (A) Brahmaputra — Brahmaputra is the name of a particular river, so it is a proper noun.
Q: Which word is a common noun?
A: (A) table — A common noun names any person, place or thing of the same class. 'Table' is a common noun.
Q: Which of these is a collective noun?
A: (A) crowd — A collective noun names a group. 'Crowd' means a group of people.
Q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'A ___ of cattle.'
A: (A) herd — A group of cattle is called a herd.
Q: Which of these is an abstract noun?
A: (A) kindness — An abstract noun names a quality or idea. 'Kindness' cannot be seen or touched.
Q: 'Wisdom' is what kind of noun?
A: (A) Abstract noun — Wisdom is an idea or quality, so it is an abstract noun.
Q: Which of these is a material noun?
A: (A) gold — A material noun names a substance or material. 'Gold' is a material.
Q: Which of these is a countable noun?
A: (A) book — 'Book' can be counted (one book, two books); the others are uncountable.
Q: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
A: (A) advice — 'Advice' is uncountable; we say 'some advice', not 'two advices'.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The news ___ good.'
A: (A) is — 'News' looks plural but is singular, so we use 'is'.
Q: Choose the correct plural of 'child'.
A: (A) children — The plural of 'child' is 'children'.
Q: Choose the correct plural of 'ox'.
A: (A) oxen — The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.
Q: Choose the correct plural of 'wife'.
A: (A) wives — Words ending in 'f'/'fe' often change to 'ves': wife → wives.
Q: Choose the correct plural of 'tooth'.
A: (A) teeth — Irregular plural: tooth → teeth.
Q: The plural of 'sheep' is ___
A: (A) sheep — 'Sheep' has the same form in singular and plural.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The scenery of Assam ___ beautiful.'
A: (A) is — 'Scenery' is uncountable and singular, so we use 'is'.
Q: What is the feminine of 'actor'?
A: (A) actress — The feminine of 'actor' is 'actress'.
Q: What is the feminine of 'tiger'?
A: (A) tigress — The feminine of 'tiger' is 'tigress'.
Q: The masculine of 'peahen' is ___
A: (A) peacock — A male peafowl is a peacock; the female is a peahen.
Q: Which noun is of common gender?
A: (A) doctor — 'Doctor' can refer to a male or a female, so it is common gender.
Q: Which noun is of neuter gender?
A: (A) table — Neuter gender is used for lifeless things. 'Table' is a lifeless object.
Q: What is the noun form of the verb 'speak'?
A: (A) speech — The noun form of 'speak' is 'speech'. 'Speaker' is the person who speaks.
Q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'A ___ of ships.'
A: (A) fleet — A group of ships is called a fleet.
Q: Fill in the blank: 'The police ___ caught the thief.'
A: (A) have — 'Police' is always used as a plural collective noun, so we use 'have'.
Q: Which word is a personal pronoun in 'She is my friend.'?
A: (A) She — 'She' stands for a person and is a personal pronoun.

### Ahom Dynasty Architecture | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/ahom-dynasty-architecture-assam/
Summary: Important questions on the architecture of the Ahom dynasty of Assam for competitive exams. Useful for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other Assam government exams.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom palace located at Garhgaon?
A: The Kareng Ghar (Gargaon Palace) is the famous Ahom palace at Garhgaon.
Q: Who built the Kareng Ghar at Gargaon?
A: The Kareng Ghar was originally built by Suklenmung (Garh Gayan) in 1540 and rebuilt by later kings.
Q: Which Ahom king shifted the capital from Gargaon to Rangpur?
A: Rudra Singha shifted the capital from Gargaon to Rangpur in the early 18th century.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom palace at Rangpur?
A: The Talatal Ghar at Rangpur is the famous Ahom palace built by Swargadeo Rudra Singha.
Q: Which is the largest and most impressive Ahom palace?
A: The Talatal Ghar is the largest and most impressive Ahom palace.
Q: What is the Talatal Ghar famous for architecturally?
A: The Talatal Ghar is famous for its underground tunnels and secret passages used for escape.
Q: Which is the famous Ahom amphitheatre at Rangpur?
A: The Rang Ghar is the famous two-storeyed Ahom amphitheatre at Rangpur.
Q: Who built the Rang Ghar?
A: The Rang Ghar was built by Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in 1746.
Q: What was the Rang Ghar used for?
A: The Rang Ghar was used as a royal pavilion for watching sports, elephant fights and cultural performances.
Q: Which is the emblem of the Assam government derived from Ahom architecture?
A: The Rang Ghar has been adopted as the emblem of the Government of Assam.
Q: Which Ahom king constructed the Kareng Ghar at Gargaon with bricks?
A: The brick construction of the Kareng Ghar was carried out by King Suklenmung.
Q: What is the name of the Ahom royal burial mounds?
A: The Ahom royal burial mounds are called 'Maidams'.
Q: Where are the royal maidams of the Ahom kings located?
A: The royal maidams are located at Charaideo, near Sivasagar.
Q: What was the Charaideo Maidam used for?
A: The Charaideo maidams were the royal burial grounds of the Ahom kings and queens.
Q: Which was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom in Assam?
A: Charaideo was the first capital of the Ahom kingdom established by Sukapha in 1253.
Q: Which style of construction is the Talatal Ghar?
A: The Talatal Ghar is an octagonal brick structure with a blend of Ahom and Mughal architectural styles.
Q: Which Ahom monument has underground storeys?
A: The Talatal Ghar has three underground storeys with secret tunnels.
Q: Which is the temple-like structure built by the Ahoms at Sivasagar?
A: The Shivdol, Joydol and Vishnudol temples at Sivasagar were built by the Ahom queen Ambika.
Q: Who built the Shivdol at Sivasagar?
A: The Shivdol was built by the Ahom queen Ambika, wife of Swargadeo Siva Singha, in 1734.
Q: Which is the tallest temple (Dol) in Assam?
A: The Shivdol at Sivasagar is the tallest temple in Assam.
Q: Which artificial tank was excavated by the Ahoms at Sivasagar?
A: The Sivasagar Tank (Borpukhuri) was excavated by the Ahom queen Ambika.
Q: Which Ahom king built the Tolatol Ghar?
A: The Tolatol Ghar is associated with the palace complex of Rangpur built by Rudra Singha.
Q: Which material was primarily used in the construction of Ahom monuments?
A: Bricks, stone and lime mortar were primarily used in Ahom construction.
Q: Which Ahom king built the Gargaon Palace with a 'multi-storeyed' design?
A: King Gadadhar Singha rebuilt the Gargaon Palace with a seven-storeyed (Kareng) design.
Q: What is the architectural style of the Rang Ghar?
A: The Rang Ghar is built in a unique style resembling a royal ship with a curved roof.
Q: Which Ahom capital was established by Sukapha?
A: Sukapha established the capital at Charaideo in 1253.
Q: What is the 'Sivasagar' also known as?
A: Sivasagar is also known as the 'City of Ahom' due to its rich Ahom monuments.
Q: Which Ahom monument resembles the shape of a 'Bengal tiger'?
A: The Rang Ghar is sometimes likened to a crouching tiger due to its shape.
Q: Which Ahom king built the 'Fakuwa Doul'?
A: The Fakuwa Doul at Sivasagar was built during the reign of the Ahom kings.
Q: Which is the main architectural legacy of the Ahoms in the Brahmaputra valley?
A: The palaces, maidams, tanks and temples at Gargaon, Rangpur and Sivasagar form the main legacy.
Q: Which Ahom monument is a World Heritage site (tentative)?
A: The Charaideo Maidams have been included in the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list and inscribed in 2024.
Q: What is the shape of the Kareng Ghar's central structure?
A: The Kareng Ghar has a rectangular, multi-tiered structure with arched doorways.
Q: Which Ahom king's reign saw the construction of many brick temples at Sivasagar?
A: The reign of Siva Singha and Queen Ambika saw the construction of many brick temples at Sivasagar.
Q: Which structure served as the royal pavilion for the Ahom kings during the Rongali Bihu?
A: The Rang Ghar served as the royal pavilion from which the Ahom kings watched games and celebrations.
Q: What is the construction material of the Talatal Ghar?
A: The Talatal Ghar is built of bricks and stone, with wooden beams in its interior.

### Assamese Literature & Historical Chronicles (Buranjis) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/assamese-literature-buranjis-culture/
Summary: Important questions on Assamese literature and the historical chronicles (Buranjis) for competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature?
A: The Charyapada, a collection of Buddhist mystical songs, is the earliest specimen of Assamese literature.
Q: Who is known as the father of Assamese literature?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva is known as the father of Assamese literature.
Q: Which is the most famous work of Sankardeva?
A: The Kirtan Ghosa is the most famous work of Sankardeva.
Q: Who wrote the 'Namghosa'?
A: The Namghosa was written by Mahapurusha Madhavdeva.
Q: Which is the first Assamese translation of the Ramayana?
A: The Saptakanda Ramayana by Madhava Kandali is the first Assamese translation of the Ramayana.
Q: Who wrote the 'Saptakanda Ramayana'?
A: Madhava Kandali wrote the Saptakanda Ramayana in the 14th century.
Q: What is a Buranji?
A: A Buranji is a historical chronicle or record maintained by the Ahom administration.
Q: In which language were the earliest Buranjis written?
A: The earliest Buranjis were written in the Tai (Ahom) language.
Q: Which Buranji is the most important for the reign of Sukapha?
A: The 'Assam Buranji' and the 'Chutiya Buranji' are important, with the Ahom Buranji covering early reigns.
Q: Who compiled the first systematic history of Assam in English?
A: Edward Gait wrote 'A History of Assam' (1905), the first systematic history of Assam.
Q: Who is the author of the 'Buranji Vivek Ratna'?
A: The 'Buranji Vivek Ratna' was written by the Ahom scholar Kasinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Which is the first Assamese newspaper?
A: The Orunodoi, published in 1846 by the American Baptist Mission, is the first Assamese periodical.
Q: Who is known as the 'Pioneer of Assamese Prose'?
A: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan is known as the pioneer of Assamese prose.
Q: Who wrote the famous 'Assam Buranji' in the early 19th century?
A: The 'Assam Buranji' was written by Kashinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Who is the author of 'Buranji Vivak Ratna'?
A: The 'Buranji Vivak Ratna' was authored by Kasinath Tamuli Phukan.
Q: Which Assamese writer is known as the 'Sahityarathi'?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is known as the 'Sahityarathi' (Charioteer of Literature).
Q: Who is the founder of the Assamese novel?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is regarded as the founder of the Assamese novel.
Q: Which is the first Assamese novel?
A: 'Mirijiyori' by Rajanikanta Bordoloi is considered the first Assamese novel (1894).
Q: Who is called the 'Bard of Brahmaputra'?
A: Bishnu Prasad Rabha is affectionately called the 'Bard of Brahmaputra'.
Q: Who is the first Assamese woman novelist?
A: Indira Goswami (Mamoni Raisom Goswami) is one of the most celebrated Assamese novelists.
Q: Which Assamese writer won the Jnanpith Award?
A: Indira Goswami won the Jnanpith Award in 2000 for her contribution to Assamese literature.
Q: Who is known as the 'Xatraiya Kabya' poet?
A: The early Vaishnavite poets like Sankardeva and Madhavdeva are known for devotional poetry.
Q: Who wrote the first Assamese grammar in Assamese?
A: The first Assamese grammar was written in the form of the 'Katha Gosha' by Bhattadeva, and later grammars by missionaries.
Q: Who is the father of Assamese prose?
A: Bhattadeva (Bhatta Dev) is considered the father of Assamese prose.
Q: Which work is Bhattadeva famous for?
A: Bhattadeva is famous for the 'Katha Bhagavat' and 'Katha Gita', early works of Assamese prose.
Q: Who wrote the 'Burhanjis' in the Ahom era?
A: The official chroniclers called 'Phukans' and the royal scribes wrote the Buranjis.
Q: Which is the longest poem of Assamese literature?
A: The 'Kirtan Ghosa' is considered one of the longest and most important devotional works.
Q: Who is the author of 'Khargosh' satire?
A: Lakshminath Bezbaroa is famous for his satirical essays in the 'Burhi Aair Xadhu' and other works.
Q: Which is the famous collection of folk tales by Lakshminath Bezbaroa?
A: The 'Burhi Aair Xadhu' is the famous collection of folk tales by Lakshminath Bezbaroa.
Q: Who is the first Assamese poet to write in free verse?
A: Amulya Barua is considered the first Assamese poet to write in free verse.
Q: Which Buranji records the battle of Saraighat?
A: The 'Purani Asom Buranji' and the Ahom Buranjis record the events including the battle of Saraighat.
Q: Who wrote the 'Deodhai Buranji'?
A: The 'Deodhai Buranji' was written by the royal astrologers and priests of the Ahom court.
Q: Which is the first drama of Assamese literature?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' of Sankardeva is the first drama of Assamese literature.
Q: Who is the author of 'Miri Jiyori'?
A: Rajanikanta Bordoloi wrote 'Miri Jiyori'.
Q: Which Assamese poet is known for the 'Xongkiar' or the bards of the Sattras?
A: The devotional poets of the Vaishnavite Sattras, beginning with Sankardeva, are known as the bardic poets.

### Major Festivals & Fairs of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/major-festivals-fairs-assam/
Summary: Important questions on the major festivals and fairs of Assam for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: How many Bihus are celebrated in Assam?
A: Three Bihus are celebrated — Bohag (Rongali), Kati (Kongali) and Magh (Bhogali).
Q: Which Bihu marks the Assamese New Year?
A: Bohag Bihu (Rongali Bihu), celebrated in mid-April, marks the Assamese New Year.
Q: Which Bihu is also called 'Kongali Bihu'?
A: Kati Bihu is also called 'Kongali Bihu' as it is observed during scarcity before harvest.
Q: Which Bihu is associated with the Uruka night?
A: The Uruka night, the eve of the last day of the month of Puh, is associated with Magh Bihu.
Q: What is the community bonfire lit during Magh Bihu called?
A: The community bonfire lit during Magh Bihu is called the 'Meji'.
Q: What is the temporary hut built during Magh Bihu called?
A: The temporary hut built during Magh Bihu is called 'Bhelaghar'.
Q: Which festival is celebrated by the Bodo community as their New Year?
A: The Bwisagu festival is celebrated by the Bodo community as their New Year.
Q: Which festival of the Bodo community is associated with the Bathou religion?
A: The Kherai festival is associated with the Bathou religion of the Bodo community.
Q: Which festival of the Mising community is related to agriculture?
A: The Ali-Ai-Ligang festival of the Mising community is related to sowing and agriculture.
Q: When is the Ali-Ai-Ligang festival celebrated?
A: The Ali-Ai-Ligang festival is celebrated in the month of Fagun (February-March).
Q: Which festival of the Karbi community is associated with the worship of the ancestral spirits?
A: The Chomangkan festival of the Karbi community is associated with the worship of ancestral spirits.
Q: What is the Chomangkan of the Karbi community?
A: Chomangkan is the Karbi festival of remembrance of the dead, marked by songs and dances.
Q: Which festival is celebrated by the Dimasa community?
A: The Bushu festival is celebrated by the Dimasa community.
Q: What is the Bushu festival associated with?
A: The Bushu festival of the Dimasa community is a harvest festival celebrated with dance and music.
Q: Which festival is celebrated by the tea tribe community of Assam?
A: The Karam Puja and Tusu festivals are celebrated by the tea tribe community of Assam.
Q: Which festival of the Deuri community is related to their animistic worship?
A: The 'Gija Puja' and 'Igu' festivals of the Deuri community are related to animistic worship.
Q: Which is the biggest religious fair of Assam held at the Kamakhya Temple?
A: The Ambubachi Mela is the biggest religious fair held at the Kamakhya Temple.
Q: When is the Ambubachi Mela held?
A: The Ambubachi Mela is held in the month of Asad (late June) during the annual menstruation of the goddess.
Q: What is the duration of the Ambubachi period?
A: The Ambubachi period lasts for three days, during which the temple remains closed.
Q: Which festival is celebrated at the Hayagriva Madhava Temple at Hajo?
A: The Doul (Holikotsav) and the Powa Mecca fair are celebrated at Hajo.
Q: What is the name of the fair held at the Barpeta Satra?
A: The 'Barpeta Doul Utsav' is the famous fair held at the Barpeta Satra.
Q: Which festival of Assam celebrates the spring season?
A: Bohag Bihu and the Holi (Doul) festival celebrate the spring season in Assam.
Q: Which is the festival of lights in Assam?
A: Kati Bihu involves lighting lamps (Saki) under the Tulsi plant and in the paddy fields.
Q: What is the 'Me-dam-me-phi' festival?
A: Me-dam-me-phi is the ancestral worship festival of the Ahom community.
Q: When is the Me-dam-me-phi festival celebrated?
A: Me-dam-me-phi is celebrated on 31 January every year.
Q: Which festival of the Ahoms is dedicated to the worship of ancestors?
A: The Me-dam-me-phi festival is dedicated to the worship of Ahom ancestors.
Q: Which is the harvest festival of the Rabha community?
A: The 'Baikho' festival is the harvest festival of the Rabha community.
Q: What is the 'Baikho' festival associated with?
A: The Baikho festival is associated with the worship of the deity for good harvest in the Rabha community.
Q: Which festival is celebrated by the Tiwa community?
A: The 'Nrikri' and 'Biswasing' festivals are celebrated by the Tiwa community.
Q: Which is the spring festival of the Tiwa community?
A: The 'Nrikri' festival is celebrated by the Tiwa community in the month of Fagun.
Q: Which is the popular cattle fair of Assam?
A: The 'Jonbeel Mela' is a famous fair where a traditional barter market and cattle fair is held.
Q: Where is the Jonbeel Mela held?
A: The Jonbeel Mela is held near the Jonbeel lake at Jagiroad in Morigaon district.
Q: What is unique about the Jonbeel Mela?
A: The Jonbeel Mela is India's oldest barter market where tribal communities exchange goods without money.
Q: When is the Jonbeel Mela held?
A: The Jonbeel Mela is held during the Magh Bihu season in January.
Q: Which festival is associated with the worship of Goddess Manasa?
A: The Manasa Puja (Maroi Puja) is associated with the worship of Goddess Manasa.

### Manuscript Paintings & Mask Making of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/manuscript-paintings-mask-making-assam/
Summary: Important questions on manuscript paintings and mask making of Assam for competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What is the traditional Assamese manuscript painting on bark called?
A: The traditional Assamese manuscript painting is called 'Sanchi Pat' painting.
Q: Which tree's bark is used to make the Sanchi Pat manuscript?
A: The bark of the Sanchi (Aquilaria) tree is used to make the manuscript pages.
Q: Which is the most famous illustrated manuscript of Assam?
A: The 'Chitra Bhagavat' is the most famous illustrated manuscript of Assam.
Q: Which Sattra preserves the famous 'Chitra Bhagavat' manuscript?
A: The Chitra Bhagavat is preserved at the Barpeta Sattra.
Q: What is the style of the manuscript paintings of Assam?
A: The Assamese manuscript paintings use bold lines, bright natural colours and depict religious themes.
Q: Which colours are traditionally used in Assamese manuscript paintings?
A: Natural colours like red (hingul), yellow, black (kola) and white are traditionally used.
Q: Who is considered the father of Assamese manuscript painting tradition?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva is considered the father of the Assamese manuscript painting tradition.
Q: Which of Sankardeva's works was illustrated with paintings?
A: The 'Bhagavat Purana' translated by Sankardeva was illustrated with manuscript paintings.
Q: Which is the traditional Assamese art of painting on the wall?
A: The traditional Assamese wall painting is seen in the Namghars and Satras, often as Pata paintings.
Q: What is the 'Pata' in Assamese art?
A: The Pata is a painted cloth or bark used as a backdrop or as an illustrated scroll in Assamese art.
Q: Which is the traditional Assamese art of mask making associated with the Satras?
A: The 'Mukha Shilpa' (mask craft) of the Satras, especially Samaguri Satra, is traditional mask making.
Q: Which Satra of Assam is internationally famous for mask making?
A: The Samaguri Satra in Nagaon district is internationally famous for mask making.
Q: Which materials are used to make the traditional masks of Assam?
A: Bamboo, cane, clay, cow dung, cloth and natural colours are used to make the masks.
Q: Which character is depicted in the biggest masks of the Samaguri Satra?
A: Demons and mythological characters like Bakasura, Narakasura and Ravana are depicted in the masks.
Q: What is the 'Mukha Nritya' of Assam?
A: The Mukha Nritya is the mask dance of the Sattras where performers wear large masks.
Q: Which festival of the Samaguri Satra showcases the mask dance?
A: The 'Ras' and 'Bhaona' festivals of the Samaguri Satra showcase the mask dance.
Q: Who is the renowned mask artist of the Samaguri Satra?
A: Sri Sri Pradip Kumar Goswami is the renowned mask artist of the Samaguri Satra.
Q: What is the significance of the mask in Assamese Bhaona?
A: Masks are used to depict supernatural beings, demons and gods, enhancing the dramatic effect.
Q: Which district is famous for the manufacture of masks in Assam?
A: Nagaon district is famous for the manufacture of masks in Assam.
Q: What is the traditional Assamese book of palm leaf?
A: The 'Tulapat' manuscript is the traditional palm leaf book used in ancient Assam.
Q: Which art form uses the 'Sanchi' bark for writing and painting?
A: The Sanchi Pat manuscript tradition uses the Sanchi bark for writing and painting.
Q: Which museum houses many Assamese manuscript paintings?
A: The Assam State Museum in Guwahati and the Kalakshetra museum house many manuscript paintings.
Q: Which is the traditional Assamese art of painting on silk?
A: The 'Patala' painting on silk is a traditional Assamese art form.
Q: What is the traditional Assamese scroll painting called?
A: The traditional Assamese scroll painting is called the 'Pata Chitra'.
Q: Which natural pigment gives the red colour in Assamese paintings?
A: Hingul (red vermilion) gives the red colour in Assamese paintings.
Q: Which is the black pigment traditionally used in Assamese manuscript painting?
A: The black pigment (Kola) is traditionally made from soot and gum.
Q: Which art of Assam received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag for mask making?
A: The Samaguri mask craft of Assam has received the GI tag.
Q: Which book of Sankardeva is famous for its illustrations?
A: The 'Bhagavat Purana' (Saptakanda) illustrated by Sankardeva is famous for its paintings.
Q: Which is the traditional Assamese art of making idols from bamboo?
A: The traditional bamboo idol-making is seen in the making of masks and puppets in Assam.
Q: What is the traditional Assamese painted border on the Sanchi manuscript called?
A: The decorative border of the Sanchi manuscript is called the 'Khol' or 'Kara' border.
Q: Which institution teaches traditional mask making in Assam?
A: The Samaguri Satra and its mask-making school teach the traditional mask craft.
Q: Which is the oldest preserved manuscript of Assam?

A: Floral motifs, creepers, geometric patterns and mythological scenes are painted on the borders.
Q: What material is traditionally used to make the ink for writing Sanchi manuscripts?
A: A paste of lamp black and natural gum, often mixed with herbal extracts, is used as ink.

### Traditional Music, Folk Songs & Musical Instruments of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/music-folk-instruments-assam/
Summary: Important questions on traditional music, folk songs and musical instruments of Assam for competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: Who composed the Borgeet (Great Songs) of Assam?
A: The Borgeets were composed by Srimanta Sankardeva and his disciple Mahapurusha Madhavdeva.
Q: What is the total number of Borgeets composed by Sankardeva and Madhavdeva?
A: Together they composed 240 Borgeets — 34 by Sankardeva and 206 by Madhavdeva.
Q: Which raga is the basis of most Borgeets?
A: Borgeets are set to classical ragas, largely derived from the Ragamala tradition.
Q: What is the main theme of the Borgeets?
A: Borgeets are devotional songs (Bhakti) dedicated to Lord Krishna and Lord Rama.
Q: Which folk song of Assam is associated with the Bihu festival?
A: The Bihu geet (Bihunam) is the folk song associated with the Bihu festival of Assam.
Q: Which musical instrument is played during the Bihu dance?
A: The Dhol (drum), Pepa (buffalo horn pipe) and Gogona (bamboo jaw harp) are played during Bihu.
Q: What is the Pepa made of?
A: The Pepa is a wind instrument made from the horn of a buffalo.
Q: What is the Gogona used for in Assamese music?
A: The Gogona is a bamboo jaw harp used mainly by women during Bihu dances.
Q: Which traditional narrative song form of Assam is performed by an Oja with palis?
A: Ojapali is the narrative song-drama form performed by an Oja (lead) with palis (assistants).
Q: Which epics are narrated in the Ojapali tradition?
A: The Ojapali tradition narrates stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and the Manasa legends.
Q: What are the two main types of Ojapali?
A: The two main types are Biyah (Maroi) Ojapali and Suknanni Ojapali.
Q: Which Assamese folk song is sung during the agricultural season?
A: The Tokari geet and the Kherkheriya geet are sung during the agricultural seasons.
Q: Which musical instrument accompanies the Tokari geet?
A: The Tokari, a one-stringed plucked instrument, accompanies the Tokari geet.
Q: Who is the famous exponent of Tokari geet of Assam?
A: Khagen Mahanta is the most famous exponent of Tokari geet and modern folk songs of Assam.
Q: Which folk song form is associated with the Goalpara region?
A: Goalpariya lokageet is the folk song form associated with the Goalpara region.
Q: What is the Zikir and Zari of Assam?
A: Zikir and Zari are devotional folk songs introduced by Azan Pir (Ajan Fakir) among the Muslim community.
Q: Who is the composer of the Zikir songs?
A: Azan Pir Shah Miran, popularly known as Ajan Fakir, composed the Zikir songs.
Q: Which is the traditional drum used in the Bhaona performances?
A: The Khol (a two-sided clay drum) is the traditional drum used in Bhaona performances.
Q: Which instrument is the Khol usually played with?
A: The Khol is played with the hands, accompanied by the Taal (cymbals) and Bhortal.
Q: What is the Bhortal?
A: Bhortal is a type of large cymbal used in Sattriya music and the Bhortal Nritya of Barpeta.
Q: Who is the founder of the Bhortal Nritya?
A: The Bhortal Nritya was introduced by Narahari Burha Bhakat of Barpeta.
Q: Which is the folk song of the Mising community?
A: The Mising community sings songs like 'O Nitom' and 'Ledum' during their festivals.
Q: What is the Kherai song associated with?
A: The Kherai song is associated with the Bathou religious festival of the Bodo community.
Q: Which instrument is the emblem of the Bodo community's music?
A: The Sifung, a long bamboo flute, is the emblem of Bodo music.
Q: What is the name of the traditional musical instrument of the Bodo community?
A: The Kham (drum), Sifung (flute), Serja (stringed instrument) and Thorkha are traditional Bodo instruments.
Q: Which instrument is used in the Kherai dance performance?
A: The Kham (drum) and Sifung (flute) are used in the Kherai dance performance.
Q: What is the Xutuli instrument?
A: Xutuli is a small earthen whistle used traditionally during Bihu, especially by women.
Q: Which song is sung during the marriage ceremonies of Assam?
A: Biyanam (wedding songs) are sung during Assamese marriage ceremonies.
Q: What is the name of the lullaby songs of Assam?
A: The lullaby songs of Assam are called 'Nisukoni geet' or 'Paduli geet'.
Q: Which song is sung by the women during paddy cultivation?
A: The 'Kherkheriya geet' and 'Gari ga geet' are sung by women during paddy cultivation.
Q: Which is the folk song associated with the cattle-herding community?
A: The 'Gorukhia geet' is the folk song associated with the cattle-herding community.
Q: Which musical instrument is a bamboo clapper used in Assamese folk music?
A: The Toka is a bamboo clapper used in Assamese folk music, especially in Deodhani performances.
Q: What is the name of the drum used by the tea garden community?
A: The tea garden community uses the 'Madal' (Mandal) drum in their Jhumur performances.
Q: Which traditional music form is used in the Namghar prayers?
A: The Namkirtan and the Borgeet are the traditional music forms used in Namghar prayers.
Q: Which instrument accompanies the recitation of the Borgeets in the Sattra?
A: The Khol, Taal and the Veena (string instrument) accompany the recitation of Borgeets.

### Sattras & Charaideo Maidams | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/sattras-charaideo-maidams-assam/
Summary: Important questions on the Sattras and Charaideo Maidams of Assam for competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What is a Sattra in Assamese Vaishnavism?
A: A Sattra is a Vaishnavite monastery-cum-institution established for religious, cultural and social activities.
Q: Who established the Sattra institutions in Assam?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva and his disciple Mahapurusha Madhavdeva established the Sattras.
Q: Who is the head of a Sattra called?
A: The head of a Sattra is called the 'Satradhikar'.
Q: What is the main prayer hall of a Sattra called?
A: The main prayer hall of a Sattra is called the 'Kirtan Ghar' or 'Namghar'.
Q: Which is the most famous Sattra centre of Assam?
A: The Majuli island is the most famous centre of Sattras, with many ancient Satras.
Q: Which river island of Assam is known for its Sattras?
A: Majuli, the largest river island in the world, is known for its Sattras.
Q: Which is the oldest Sattra of Assam?
A: The Dakhinpat Sattra and the Kamalabari Sattra are among the oldest Sattras of Assam.
Q: Which Sattra on Majuli is famous for the Ras Lila performance?
A: The Dakhinpat Sattra is famous for its grand Ras Lila performances.
Q: Which Sattra is known for the Paal Naam and manuscript art?
A: The Auniati Sattra is known for its Paal Naam, manuscripts and rich collection of artefacts.
Q: Which Sattra is associated with the royal patronage of the Ahom kings?
A: The Auniati Sattra received significant patronage from the Ahom kings.
Q: Which Sattra on Majuli is famous for mask making?
A: The Samaguri Sattra (near Majuli, at Nagaon) is famous for mask making, not on Majuli but in Nagaon.
Q: What is the annual event of the Sattras called?
A: The annual religious congregations of the Sattras are called 'Raas' or 'Palnaam' festivals.
Q: Which festival is celebrated with Ras Lila in the Sattras of Majuli?
A: The Ras Purnima (Raas Mahotsav) is celebrated with Ras Lila performances in the Sattras.
Q: What is the main scripture recited in the Sattras?
A: The Kirtan Ghosa and the Bhagavata Purana are the main scriptures recited in the Sattras.
Q: Who is the founder of the Vaishnavite Bhakti movement in Assam?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva is the founder of the Vaishnavite Bhakti movement in Assam.
Q: Which disciple of Sankardeva established many Sattras?
A: Mahapurusha Madhavdeva, the principal disciple of Sankardeva, established many Sattras.
Q: What is the Manikut of a Sattra?
A: The Manikut is the inner sanctum of the Sattra where the sacred scriptures and idol are kept.
Q: Which Sattra is located on the south bank of the Brahmaputra near Jorhat?
A: The Madhupur Sattra and the Garamur Sattra are located in the Majuli region.
Q: What is the role of the Sattras in Assamese society?
A: The Sattras preserved art, literature, dance and culture while promoting social reform and unity.
Q: Which Sattra at Barpeta is a major centre of Vaishnavism?
A: The Barpeta Sattra, founded by Madhavdeva, is a major centre of Vaishnavism.
Q: What is the Namghar in the Sattra system?
A: The Namghar is the community prayer house attached to the Sattra for congregational worship.
Q: What is the Charaideo Maidam?
A: Charaideo Maidam is the royal burial ground of the Ahom kings, with burial mounds known as Maidams.
Q: Where is Charaideo located?
A: Charaideo is located in the Charaideo district, near Sivasagar in upper Assam.
Q: Who was the first Ahom king buried at Charaideo?
A: Sukapha, the founder of the Ahom kingdom, was the first to be honoured at Charaideo.
Q: What is the architectural structure of a Maidam?
A: A Maidam is a vaulted mound of earth over a brick chamber containing the royal remains and treasures.
Q: Which site received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2024?
A: The Charaideo Moidam (Maidam) royal burial mounds received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2024.
Q: What is the meaning of 'Maidam' in the Tai-Ahom language?
A: 'Maidam' means a burial mound or a sacred repository of the departed in the Tai-Ahom tradition.
Q: Which dynasty built the Charaideo Maidams?
A: The Ahom dynasty built the Charaideo Maidams over several centuries.
Q: What is the significance of the maidams in Ahom culture?
A: The maidams reflect the Ahom belief in the afterlife and preserve the memory of the royal lineage.
Q: Which is the first capital and last resting place of the Ahom kings?
A: Charaideo was the first capital and the traditional last resting place of the Ahom kings.
Q: Which organisation has recognised the Charaideo maidams as a heritage site?
A: UNESCO has recognised the Charaideo maidams as a World Heritage site.
Q: Which Sattra is associated with the Kirtan Ghosa?
A: The Sattras of Majuli, especially the Kamalabari and Auniati Sattras, preserve the Kirtan Ghosa tradition.
Q: What is the 'Bhakats' role in the Sattra?
A: The Bhakats are the resident devotees who perform the daily prayers, dances and rituals of the Sattra.
Q: Which Sattra is known for the practice of 'Nirvana' style worship?
A: The Barpeta Sattra is known for its distinct 'Sravan' style of worship and the celebration of Doul.
Q: Which riverine island hosts the annual Raas festival of the Sattras?
A: Majuli hosts the annual Raas festival, drawing thousands of visitors.

### Traditional Theatre — Ankiya Naat & Bhaona | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/assam-art-culture-sec/theatre-ankiya-naat-bhaona-assam/
Summary: Important questions on Ankiya Naat and Bhaona theatre forms of Assam for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Who is the founder of Ankiya Naat, the traditional theatre form of Assam?
A: Srimanta Sankardeva founded the Ankiya Naat in the 16th century.
Q: What is the playhouse where Bhaona is performed called?
A: The playhouse for Bhaona is called 'Naatghar' or 'Bhaonaghar', attached to a Namghar or Satra.
Q: Which is the first drama written by Sankardeva?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' is the first drama written by Sankardeva.
Q: Which is the most famous Ankiya Naat of Sankardeva?
A: The 'Kaliya Daman' and 'Parijata Harana' are among the most famous Ankiya Naats of Sankardeva.
Q: What is the duration of a traditional Ankiya Naat performance?
A: An Ankiya Naat traditionally lasts for several hours, often a full night.
Q: Who is the main narrator-conductor in the Ankiya Naat?
A: The Sutradhar is the main narrator-conductor in the Ankiya Naat.
Q: What does the Sutradhar sing at the beginning of the Bhaona?
A: The Sutradhar sings a Mangalacharan (invocatory verse) and a Borgeet at the beginning.
Q: Which language is used in the dialogues of the Ankiya Naat?
A: The Ankiya Naat uses Brajavali, a literary language mixing Maithili and Assamese.
Q: What is the role of the Gayan-Bayan in Bhaona?
A: The Gayan-Bayan sing the introductory Ghosas and play the Khol and Taal during the Bhaona.
Q: Which mask (Mukha) is used to depict demons in the Bhaona?
A: Large painted masks, especially those of the Samaguri Satra, depict demons like Bakasura.
Q: Who traditionally performs the female roles in the Ankiya Naat?
A: In the traditional Sattriya Bhaona, male performers play the female roles.
Q: What is the closing verse or benediction of the Ankiya Naat called?
A: The closing benediction of the Ankiya Naat is called the 'Bharat Vakya'.
Q: Which is the first Ankiya Naat written by Madhavdeva?
A: The 'Arjun Bhanjan' is considered the first Ankiya Naat written by Madhavdeva.
Q: Which famous Ankiya Naat of Madhavdeva depicts the killing of Putana?
A: The 'Putana Badh' is the famous Ankiya Naat of Madhavdeva depicting the killing of Putana.
Q: What is the traditional backdrop or curtain used in the Bhaona stage called?
A: The painted backdrop of the Bhaona stage is called the 'Aarana' or 'Pata'.
Q: What is the function of the 'Nandi' in the Ankiya Naat?
A: The Nandi is the prologue that recites the benediction and introduces the play.
Q: In which month is the Bhaona usually performed in the Sattras?
A: Bhaona is usually performed during the festivals like Doul (Falguna) and other religious occasions.
Q: Which community was the traditional performer of the Bhaona in the Sattras?
A: The Bhakats (devotees) of the Sattras were the traditional performers of the Bhaona.
Q: What is the name of the costume worn by the performers of Bhaona?
A: The performers wear traditional costumes called 'Kopani' with dhoti, paguri (turban) and ornaments.
Q: Which instrument is played by the 'Bayan' in the Bhaona?
A: The Bayan plays the large cymbals (Bortal/Taal) while the Gayan plays the Khol.
Q: Which festival celebrates the creation of the first Bhaona by Sankardeva?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' day, commemorating Sankardeva's first drama, is celebrated by the devotees.
Q: What is the literary form of the Ankiya Naat written in?
A: Ankiya Naats are written in verse, mixing dialogue and song, in the Brajavali language.
Q: Which deity is the central theme of most Ankiya Naats?
A: Lord Krishna is the central theme of most Ankiya Naats.
Q: What is the 'Borgeet' in the context of Bhaona?
A: The Borgeet is the devotional song sung by the Sutradhar or Gayan before the Bhaona begins.
Q: Which district is famous for the traditional mask-making used in Bhaona?
A: The Samaguri Satra of Nagaon district is famous for mask-making used in Bhaona.
Q: What is the unique feature of the Bhaona performance at the Samaguri Satra?
A: The Samaguri Satra performs the famous 'Mukha Nritya' (mask dance) using elaborate masks.
Q: Who is the famous mask-making artist of the Samaguri Satra?
A: Sri Sri Pradip Kumar Goswami is the famous mask-making artist of the Samaguri Satra.
Q: What is the importance of the 'Pat' (backdrop) in the Bhaona?
A: The painted Pat serves as the visual backdrop depicting the scene, and is a traditional art form.
Q: Which traditional oil lamp is lit at the start of the Bhaona?
A: The 'Mukhbota' and traditional earthen lamps are lit to begin the Bhaona.
Q: Which literary work of Sankardeva is considered the first play with painted backdrop?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' is considered the first play with a painted backdrop by Sankardeva.
Q: What is the name of the traditional Assamese theatre movement that revived the Bhaona?
A: The modern Bhaona performances are part of the 'Ankiya Nat' revival movements led by Sattras and cultural bodies.
Q: Which role does the 'Oja' play in the traditional theatre forms?
A: The Oja is the lead performer who narrates and conducts the Ojapali song-drama.
Q: Which is the grand annual performance of the Ankiya Naat in the Sattras?
A: The 'Ras Utsav' and 'Doul Utsav' are the grand occasions for the performance of Ankiya Naats.
Q: What is the significance of the Bhaona in the propagation of Vaishnavism?
A: The Bhaona was used by Sankardeva as a medium to propagate the Bhakti movement and Vaishnavism.
Q: Which is considered the first Ankiya Naat written by Sankardeva?
A: The 'Chihna Yatra' is considered the first Ankiya Naat written by Sankardeva.

### Ancient, Cave & Temple Architecture | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/ancient-cave-temple-architecture-india/
Summary: Important questions on ancient, cave and temple architecture of India for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Which are the main styles of Hindu temple architecture?
A: The main styles are Nagara (north), Dravida (south) and Vesara (mixed).
Q: What is the 'Shikhara'?
A: The Shikhara is the curved or pyramidal tower above the sanctum of a temple, characteristic of Nagara architecture.
Q: What is the 'Vimana'?
A: The Vimana is the tower above the sanctum in Dravida (south Indian) temple architecture.
Q: Which temple is an example of Dravida architecture?
A: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur is an example of Dravida architecture.
Q: Which temple was built by Raja Raja Chola I?
A: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur was built by Raja Raja Chola I in the 11th century.
Q: Which caves are Buddhist rock-cut caves?
A: Ajanta, Ellora (partly), Karle, Bhaja and Nasik caves are Buddhist rock-cut caves.
Q: Which rock-cut temples are famous at Ellora?
A: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora is a famous rock-cut temple, carved from a single rock.
Q: Who built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora?
A: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century.
Q: Which temple is famous for the 'Sun Temple'?
A: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha is a famous Sun Temple, built by Narasimhadeva I.
Q: Which temple is known as the 'Black Pagoda'?
A: The Konark Sun Temple is known as the 'Black Pagoda'.
Q: Which is the largest Buddhist monument in the world?
A: The Borobudur Temple in Indonesia is the largest, but in India, the Sanchi Stupa is the largest ancient Buddhist structure.
Q: Who built the Sanchi Stupa?
A: The original Sanchi Stupa was built by Emperor Ashoka and later expanded by the Shungas and Satavahanas.
Q: What is a 'Stupa'?
A: A Stupa is a Buddhist mound-shaped monument containing relics, with a harmika and chhatra on top.
Q: Which temple in India is known for its 'Erotic Sculptures'?
A: The Khajuraho Temples are known for their erotic sculptures, built by the Chandela dynasty.
Q: Which temple is dedicated to the Sun God in Gujarat?
A: The Modhera Sun Temple in Gujarat is dedicated to the Sun God, built by Bhima I.
Q: Which is the oldest temple of South India?
A: The Mundeshwari Temple in Bihar is considered the oldest, but in South India, the Mahabalipuram temples are the oldest.
Q: Which site has the 'Five Rathas'?
A: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) in Tamil Nadu has the Pancha Rathas (five rathas), built by the Pallavas.
Q: Which temple is built in the 'Vesara' style?
A: The Hoysala temples, like Chennakesava at Belur, are examples of the Vesara (Karnata-Dravida) style.
Q: What is the 'Gopuram'?
A: The Gopuram is the monumental entrance tower of a Dravida temple.
Q: Which temple has the tallest gopuram?
A: The Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple at Srirangam has the tallest gopuram in India.
Q: Which rock-cut architecture is known as 'cave architecture'?
A: Rock-cut architecture, like the Ajanta and Ellora caves, is known as cave architecture.
Q: Which temple is at the hill station of Rishikesh?
A: Rishikesh has several temples; the Trimbakeshwar Temple at Nashik is a famous Jyotirlinga site.
Q: What is the 'Garbhagriha'?
A: The Garbhagriha is the inner sanctum of a temple where the main deity is placed.
Q: Which temple is at Amarkantak?
A: Amarkantak has the Narmada Udgam temple, marking the origin of the Narmada river.
Q: Which architectural style uses 'curvilinear towers'?
A: Nagara architecture uses curvilinear (curved) towers, like the Lingaraja Temple at Bhubaneswar.
Q: Which is the famous temple of Odisha?
A: The Jagannath Temple at Puri and the Lingaraja Temple at Bhubaneswar are the famous temples of Odisha.
Q: Which dynasty built the Kailasa temple?
A: The Rashtrakutas built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.
Q: What is the 'Nagara' style famous for?
A: The Nagara style is famous for its curvilinear shikhara and is found mainly in northern India.
Q: Which cave has the famous 'Trimurti'?
A: The Elephanta Caves have the famous Trimurti sculpture of Shiva.
Q: Which temple was built by the Pallavas?
A: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).

### Classical & Folk Dances | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/classical-folk-dances-india/
Summary: Important questions on Indian classical and folk dances for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: How many classical dances are officially recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
A: The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognizes eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.
Q: Which classical dance originated in Tamil Nadu?
A: Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu, evolving from the temple dances of the devadasis.
Q: Which dance form is associated with the Mughal courts and storytelling?
A: Kathak, a north Indian classical dance, is associated with the Mughal courts and features rhythmic footwork and storytelling.
Q: Which classical dance is famous for its eye movements and is from Kerala?
A: Kathakali from Kerala is famous for its elaborate eye movements (netra abhinaya) and stylized gestures.
Q: Kuchipudi is a classical dance of which state?
A: Kuchipudi is a classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi.
Q: Which classical dance originated in the temples of Odisha?
A: Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha and is known for its graceful, curvilinear movements.
Q: Manipuri dance is associated with which mythological theme?
A: Manipuri dance is associated with the Raas Lila of Lord Krishna and Radha, using gentle, flowing movements.
Q: Mohiniyattam is a solo dance form of which state?
A: Mohiniyattam is a solo classical dance of Kerala, characterized by graceful, feminine movements.
Q: Sattriya dance is associated with which state and saint?
A: Sattriya dance is associated with Assam and the saint Srimanta Sankardev, performed in the satras (monasteries).
Q: Which dance form is a combination of dance and martial arts from Kerala?
A: Kathakali combines elements of dance and martial arts like Kalaripayattu from Kerala.
Q: What is 'Bhava', 'Raga' and 'Tala' in classical dance?
A: Bhava (expression), Raga (melody) and Tala (rhythm) are the three basic elements of Indian classical dance.
Q: What does 'Natya Shastra' contain?
A: The 'Natya Shastra' of Bharata Muni contains the theory of Indian dance, music and drama.
Q: Who is known as the father of Indian classical dance theory?
A: Bharata Muni, author of the 'Natya Shastra', is considered the father of Indian classical dance theory.
Q: Which folk dance of Punjab is performed during harvest?
A: Bhangra and Giddha are the harvest folk dances of Punjab.
Q: Which folk dance is associated with Rajasthan?
A: Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Gair are folk dances of Rajasthan.
Q: What is 'Garba' and from which state?
A: Garba is a devotional folk dance of Gujarat performed during Navratri, revolving around a lamp or image of the goddess.
Q: Which dance is performed by the Santhal tribes of Bihar and Jharkhand?
A: Jhumar and Chhau are performed in tribal areas; the Santhals perform dances like 'Karma' and 'Sohrai'.
Q: Which dance form is a martial dance of Odisha?
A: Chhau, especially the Mayurbhanj Chhau, is a martial dance form of Odisha.
Q: Which folk dance is performed by the women of Mizoram?
A: Cheraw (bamboo dance) is a famous folk dance of Mizoram performed by women.
Q: What is 'Bihu' dance associated with?
A: Bihu is the folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bohag (Rongali) Bihu festival celebrating the Assamese new year.
Q: Which dance is associated with the Warli tribe?
A: The Warli tribe of Maharashtra is known for their folk dances like Tarpa dance, named after the tarpa instrument.
Q: Which folk dance of Kerala is performed by women holding lamps?
A: Kaikottikali (also called Thiruvathirakali) is a folk dance of Kerala performed by women around a lamp.
Q: Which dance form belongs to Sikkim and is performed during Pang Lhabsol?
A: Singhi Chham (snow lion dance) is performed in Sikkim during the Pang Lhabsol festival.
Q: Which dance form of Tamil Nadu is performed at the Aiyanar temple festivals?
A: Karagaattam (pot dance) and Devarattam are folk dances of Tamil Nadu performed at village festivals.
Q: What is the main instrument used in the Cheraw dance?
A: The Cheraw dance uses bamboo staves as the main instrument, tapping them in rhythm.
Q: Which classical dance uses the concept of 'lasya' and 'tandava'?
A: Most classical dances use lasya (graceful) and tandava (vigorous) styles; Bharatanatyam and Odissi distinguish these movements clearly.
Q: Who is credited with reviving Bharatanatyam in the modern era?
A: E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale are credited with reviving and popularizing Bharatanatyam.
Q: Which dance is known as the 'dance of the enchantress'?
A: Mohiniyattam is known as the dance of the enchantress, named after Mohini, the female form of Vishnu.
Q: Which dance form of West Bengal involves ornate costumes and masks?
A: Chhau dance of West Bengal (Purulia Chhau) uses elaborate costumes and masks.
Q: Which state is famous for the 'Lavani' folk dance?
A: Lavani is a folk dance of Maharashtra, known for its powerful rhythm and performed to dholki beats.

### Classical Languages & Literature | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/classical-languages-literature-india/
Summary: Important questions on Indian classical languages and literature for competitive exams. Useful for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other Assam government exams.
Q: How many classical languages are recognized in India?
A: India recognizes six classical languages: Tamil, Sanskrit, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam and Odia.
Q: Which was the first language to be given classical status in India?
A: Tamil was the first language to be given classical status in 2004.
Q: Which is the oldest language of India?
A: Tamil is considered the oldest classical language, while Sanskrit is the oldest language of the Indo-Aryan family.
Q: Which is the language of the Vedas?
A: The Vedas are composed in Vedic Sanskrit.
Q: Who composed the 'Ramayana'?
A: The 'Ramayana' was composed by Valmiki.
Q: Who composed the 'Mahabharata'?
A: The 'Mahabharata' was composed by Vyasa.
Q: What is the 'Bhagavad Gita'?
A: The Bhagavad Gita is a 700-verse part of the Mahabharata, a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.
Q: Who composed the 'Mudrarakshasa'?
A: The 'Mudrarakshasa' was composed by Vishakhadatta.
Q: Who composed the 'Raghuvamsa'?
A: The 'Raghuvamsa' was composed by Kalidasa.
Q: Who composed the 'Meghaduta'?
A: The 'Meghaduta' was composed by Kalidasa.
Q: Who is known as the 'Shakespeare of India'?
A: Kalidasa is known as the 'Shakespeare of India' for his Sanskrit dramas.
Q: Who wrote the 'Panchatantra'?
A: The 'Panchatantra' was written by Vishnu Sharma.
Q: Who wrote the 'Arthashastra'?
A: The 'Arthashastra' was written by Kautilya (Chanakya).
Q: Who composed the 'Ashtadhyayi'?
A: The 'Ashtadhyayi', a grammar of Sanskrit, was composed by Panini.
Q: Who wrote the 'Natyashastra'?
A: The 'Natyashastra' was written by Bharata Muni.
Q: Which is the oldest Tamil literature?
A: The 'Sangam' literature is the oldest Tamil literature, composed around 300 BCE to 300 CE.
Q: What is the 'Tolkappiyam'?
A: The 'Tolkappiyam' is an ancient Tamil grammar text, the earliest surviving Tamil literary work.
Q: Who wrote the 'Silappatikaram'?
A: The 'Silappatikaram', an epic Tamil poem, was written by Ilango Adigal.
Q: Who wrote the 'Manimekalai'?
A: The 'Manimekalai' was written by Sattanar (Kundalakesi).
Q: Who composed the 'Kural' (Tirukkural)?
A: The 'Tirukkural' was composed by Thiruvalluvar.
Q: Who wrote the 'Ashtavakra Gita'?
A: The 'Ashtavakra Gita' is attributed to Sage Ashtavakra, a discourse on Advaita Vedanta.
Q: Which is the 'Gita' of the Mahabharata?
A: The Bhagavad Gita is the Gita within the Mahabharata.
Q: Who wrote the 'Gitagovinda'?
A: The 'Gitagovinda' was written by Jayadeva in Sanskrit, depicting Radha and Krishna.
Q: What is the 'Abhijnanasakuntalam'?
A: The 'Abhijnanasakuntalam' is a famous Sanskrit drama by Kalidasa, based on Shakuntala and Dushyanta.
Q: Who wrote the 'Malavikagnimitram'?
A: The 'Malavikagnimitram' was written by Kalidasa.
Q: Which language is known as 'Devabhasha'?
A: Sanskrit is known as 'Devabhasha', the language of the gods.
Q: Who wrote the 'Buddhacharita'?
A: The 'Buddhacharita' was written by Ashvaghosha.
Q: Who wrote the 'Saundarananda'?
A: The 'Saundarananda' was written by Ashvaghosha.
Q: Which is the oldest classical language among the Dravidian languages?
A: Tamil is the oldest classical language among the Dravidian languages.

Q: What is the famous silk saree of Banaras called?

Q: Which saree is made of wild silk and is associated with Chhattisgarh?
A: Kosa sarees, made of Tussar (wild) silk, are associated with Chhattisgarh.
Q: Which state is famous for 'Pochampally' ikat sarees?

Q: What is 'Pashmina'?

Q: Which textile is known as 'Woven Air'?

Q: Which silk is known as 'golden silk'?
A: Muga silk of Assam is known as golden silk because of its natural golden color.
Q: What is the famous weaving of Karnataka?
A: Mysore silk sarees and Ilkal sarees are the famous weaves of Karnataka.

A: Kanjeevaram (Kanchipuram) silk sarees are famous in Tamil Nadu.

Q: Which traditional art of block printing is from Rajasthan?
A: Bagru and Sanganeri block printing are traditional textile arts of Rajasthan.
Q: What is 'Bandhani'?
A: Bandhani is a tie-and-dye textile technique of Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Q: Which craft is famous in Lucknow?
A: Chikankari, a delicate white embroidery, is the famous craft of Lucknow.
Q: What is 'Phulkari'?
A: Phulkari is a vibrant embroidery of Punjab, traditionally done on dupattas.
Q: Which craft is associated with Kashmir?
A: Kashmir is famous for its carpets, paper-maché and shawls.
Q: What is 'Zardozi'?

Q: Which craft is famous in Moradabad?

### Major Religions & Philosophical Schools | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/major-religions-philosophies-india/
Summary: Important questions on major Indian religions and philosophical schools for competitive exams. Covers ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: What are the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy?
A: The six orthodox (Astika) schools are Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa and Vedanta.
Q: Who is the founder of the Samkhya philosophy?
A: The Samkhya philosophy is attributed to Sage Kapila.
Q: What is the central text of the Yoga philosophy?
A: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali is the central text of the Yoga philosophy.
Q: Who composed the 'Yoga Sutra'?
A: The 'Yoga Sutra' was composed by Patanjali.
Q: What is the Nyaya philosophy known for?
A: Nyaya philosophy is known for its logical reasoning and epistemology.
Q: Who is the founder of the Nyaya school?
A: The Nyaya school was founded by Sage Gautama (Akshapada).
Q: What is the Vaisheshika philosophy about?
A: Vaisheshika is an atomistic philosophy founded by Sage Kanada, dealing with categories and atoms.
Q: What is Mimamsa philosophy?
A: Mimamsa is a school focusing on ritual and the interpretation of the Vedas, founded by Jaimini.
Q: Who founded the Vedanta philosophy?
A: Vedanta is based on the Upanishads; its chief exponent was Adi Shankaracharya.
Q: What is Advaita Vedanta?
A: Advaita Vedanta, propounded by Adi Shankaracharya, teaches the non-duality of the soul (Atman) and Brahman.
Q: Who founded the 'Dvaita' philosophy?
A: The Dvaita philosophy was founded by Madhvacharya.
Q: What is 'Vishishtadvaita'?
A: Vishishtadvaita is the qualified non-dualism taught by Ramanujacharya.
Q: Who founded the Buddhist religion?
A: Buddhism was founded by Gautama Buddha in the 6th century BCE.
Q: Who was the founder of Jainism?
A: Jainism was established by Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara.
Q: What are the 'Four Noble Truths'?
A: The Four Noble Truths are the core of Buddhism: suffering, its origin, its cessation and the path.
Q: What is the 'Eightfold Path' in Buddhism?
A: The Eightfold Path is the Buddhist path to liberation, including right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness and right concentration.
Q: What is 'Ahimsa'?
A: Ahimsa is the principle of non-violence, central to Jainism and Buddhism.
Q: Who founded Sikhism?
A: Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak in the 15th century.
Q: What is the holy book of Sikhism?
A: The holy book of Sikhism is the Guru Granth Sahib.
Q: What is the main text of Jainism?
A: The main texts of Jainism are the Agamas, and the Tattvartha Sutra is a key philosophical text.
Q: What are the 'Three Jewels' of Jainism?
A: The Three Jewels of Jainism are Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct.
Q: Who is the founder of the 'Sankhya' school?
A: Sage Kapila is the founder of the Sankhya school.
Q: What is the central concept of Sankhya?
A: Sankhya teaches the dualism of Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter).
Q: Who founded the 'Vaisheshika' school?
A: Sage Kanada founded the Vaisheshika school.
Q: What is the 'Charvaka' philosophy?
A: Charvaka is a materialistic and heterodox philosophy that rejects the Vedas and the supernatural.
Q: What is the 'Purana'?
A: Purana are ancient Hindu texts containing mythological stories, cosmology and legends; there are 18 major Puranas.
Q: Which is the longest epic in the world?
A: The Mahabharata is the longest epic in the world.
Q: Who is the author of the 'Mimamsa Sutras'?
A: The 'Mimamsa Sutras' were composed by Jaimini.
Q: What is 'Tantra'?
A: Tantra is a tradition of esoteric practices in Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism, focusing on rituals and meditation.
Q: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
A: Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) is considered the first Tirthankara of Jainism.

Q: Who built the Taj Mahal?
A: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
Q: Who designed the Taj Mahal?
A: The Taj Mahal was designed by the architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
Q: Which emperor built the Qutub Minar?
A: The Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

Q: What is the height of the Qutub Minar?
A: The Qutub Minar is about 72.5 meters (238 feet) tall.
Q: Who built the Red Fort in Delhi?
A: The Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan in 1648.
Q: Who built the Jama Masjid in Delhi?
A: The Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
Q: Who built the Agra Fort?
A: The Agra Fort was built by Akbar, with later additions by Shah Jahan.

Q: Who built the Golconda Fort?

Q: What is the 'Jantar Mantar'?
A: The Jantar Mantar is an astronomical observatory built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur.

A: The Hawa Mahal in Jaipur was built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in 1799.

A: The Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khalji in 1311.

A: The Taj-ul-Masajid at Bhopal is considered the largest mosque in India.

### Classical & Folk Music Traditions | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/music-traditions-classical-folk-india/
Summary: Important questions on Indian classical and folk music traditions for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: What are the two main traditions of Indian classical music?
A: The two main traditions are Hindustani (north Indian) and Carnatic (south Indian) classical music.
Q: Who is considered the father of Hindustani classical music?
A: Swami Haridas is often considered the father of Hindustani classical music, and Tansen was his disciple.
Q: Who is the famous musician in Akbar's court?
A: Miyan Tansen, one of the Navaratnas, was the famous musician in Akbar's court.
Q: What is the basic melodic framework of Indian classical music?
A: The Raga (melodic framework) is the basic structure of Indian classical music.
Q: What is the rhythmic cycle in Indian classical music called?
A: The rhythmic cycle is called Tala, measured in beats called matras.
Q: Which instrument is considered the national instrument of India?
A: The sitar, popularized globally by Pandit Ravi Shankar, is often regarded as the national instrument of India.
Q: Who introduced the sitar to the West?
A: Pandit Ravi Shankar introduced the sitar to the West, collaborating with musicians like George Harrison.
Q: Who is known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
A: Sarojini Naidu, the poetess, is known as the 'Nightingale of India', but in music, Lata Mangeshkar is also called the nightingale.
Q: Which musician is known as the 'Queen of Thumri'?
A: Girija Devi is known as the 'Queen of Thumri', a semi-classical Hindustani vocal style.
Q: What is 'Thumri'?
A: Thumri is a semi-classical vocal genre of Hindustani music, known for its romantic and devotional lyrics.
Q: What is the difference between Khayal and Dhrupad?
A: Dhrupad is the older, austere form while Khayal is more flexible and ornamented; both are Hindustani vocal genres.
Q: Who is the author of the music treatise 'Sangeet Ratnakar'?
A: 'Sangeet Ratnakar' was written by Sarangadeva in the 13th century.
Q: Which instrument is associated with Ravi Shankar?
A: The sitar is associated with Pandit Ravi Shankar.
Q: Which classical singer is known for the 'Mewati Gharana'?
A: Pandit Jasraj was a renowned exponent of the Mewati Gharana.
Q: What is the origin of Carnatic music?
A: Carnatic music developed in the southern states of India, with the Trinity of Carnatic music being Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.
Q: Who are the Trinity of Carnatic music?
A: The Trinity of Carnatic music are Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.
Q: What is 'Kriti' in Carnatic music?
A: Kriti is the main compositional form of Carnatic music, developed by the Trinity.
Q: Which instrument did M.S. Subbulakshmi play?
A: M.S. Subbulakshmi was a vocalist, not an instrumentalist; she sang Carnatic music.
Q: What is the folk music of Assam called?
A: The folk songs of Assam include Bihu Geet, Borgeet (devotional) and Ojapali.
Q: What is 'Borgeet'?
A: Borgeet are devotional songs composed by Sankardev and Madhavdev in Assamese.
Q: Which is the folk music form of Rajasthan performed by the Kalbelia community?
A: Kalbelia folk songs and dances, practiced by the Kalbelia community, are recognized as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO.
Q: What is the folk music of Punjab called?
A: The folk music of Punjab includes Tappa, Mahiya and songs sung with the tumbi and dhol.
Q: What is 'Baul' music?
A: Baul is a mystic folk music of Bengal, performed by Baul singers using the ektara.
Q: Which instrument is used in Baul music?
A: The ektara (one-stringed instrument) is used in Baul music.
Q: What is the origin of the 'Gharana' system in Hindustani music?
A: The Gharana system originated in the court traditions of north India, with gharanas like Gwalior, Agra, Kirana and Jaipur.
Q: Who composed the 'Tarannum' style of singing?
A: Amir Khusrau is credited with creating the Tarannum, a style using Persian syllables in Hindustani music.
Q: Who is known as the 'Queen of Qawwali'?
A: Abida Parveen is known as the 'Queen of Qawwali', a Sufi devotional music form.
Q: Which dance-drama music is known as 'Bhagavata Mela'?
A: Bhagavata Mela is a classical dance-drama tradition of Tamil Nadu based on Krishna themes.
Q: What is 'Sugam Sangeet'?
A: Sugam Sangeet refers to light music or semi-classical music of India, distinct from pure classical forms.
Q: Which folk music is associated with the harvest festival of Assam?
A: Bihu Geet is associated with the harvest festivals of Assam, sung during Rongali Bihu.

### Paintings: Murals & Miniatures | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/art-culture/india-art-culture-sec/paintings-murals-miniatures-india/
Summary: Important questions on Indian murals and miniature paintings for competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Which is the oldest painting tradition in India?
A: Rock paintings of Bhimbetka, dating to the Mesolithic period, are among the oldest paintings in India.
Q: Where is Bhimbetka located?
A: Bhimbetka is located in Madhya Pradesh, near Bhopal, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Q: Which site is famous for Ajanta murals?
A: The Ajanta Caves in Maharashtra are famous for their Buddhist murals.
Q: What are the themes of Ajanta paintings?
A: The Ajanta paintings depict the life of Buddha and the Jataka tales.
Q: Which cave paintings depict the life of Lord Krishna?
A: The Bagh Caves in Madhya Pradesh and the murals of the Krishna Mandapa in Hampi depict Krishna themes.
Q: What is 'Pattachitra'?
A: Pattachitra is a cloth-based scroll painting tradition of Odisha and Bengal, depicting mythological themes.
Q: Which state is famous for Madhubani painting?
A: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is famous in Bihar.
Q: What is the unique feature of Madhubani painting?
A: Madhubani paintings use natural dyes, geometric patterns and bold outlines, traditionally done on walls and floors.
Q: Which painting style is associated with the miniature paintings of Rajasthan?
A: Rajput painting, including the Mewar, Bundi and Kishangarh schools, is the miniature style of Rajasthan.
Q: Which Mughal emperor patronized the most famous miniature paintings?
A: Emperor Akbar established the Mughal miniature painting tradition, which reached its peak under Jahangir.
Q: What is the distinctive feature of the Kangra painting style?
A: Kangra paintings are known for their delicate, lyrical depiction of nature, especially the Radha-Krishna theme.
Q: Which school of Pahari painting is known for the 'Bani Thani'?
A: The Kishangarh school of Rajput painting is known for the iconic 'Bani Thani' portrait.
Q: What is 'Warli' painting?
A: Warli painting is a tribal art form of Maharashtra, using simple geometric shapes, white pigment on mud walls.
Q: Which tribal painting uses dots and is from Madhya Pradesh?
A: Gond painting from Madhya Pradesh is characterized by dots and dashes, depicting nature and mythology.
Q: What is 'Kalighat' painting?
A: Kalighat painting is a folk art of Bengal that developed near the Kalighat temple in Kolkata in the 19th century.
Q: Which painting tradition of Kerala uses natural pigments on walls?
A: Kerala mural painting is known for its vibrant natural pigments and mythological themes, such as in the Mattancherry Palace.
Q: What is the 'Tanjaur' painting?
A: Thanjavur (Tanjaur) painting is a classical South Indian style characterized by rich colors, gold foil and the use of semiprecious stones.
Q: Which miniature school is famous for the depiction of Ragamala paintings?
A: The Bundi and Kotah schools of Rajasthan are famous for Ragamala paintings.
Q: What is 'Phad' painting?
A: Phad is a scroll painting tradition of Rajasthan depicting folk deities, performed with narration called 'Phad Bhopa'.
Q: Which painting style belongs to Odisha and uses palm leaves?
A: Palm leaf Pattachitra of Odisha uses dried palm leaves as the canvas.
Q: What is the 'Basohli' painting style?
A: Basohli is an early Pahari miniature school of Jammu, known for bold colors and vigorous forms.
Q: Which Mughal painting school is associated with Persian influence?
A: The Mughal miniature school, started under Humayun with Persian artists, blended Persian and Indian styles.
Q: Which site has the famous 'Sittanavasal' paintings?

Q: What is 'Kalamkari'?

Q: Which miniature paintings are known for the 'Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan'?
A: Rajput and Kangra miniatures frequently depict Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan.
Q: What is 'Company School' painting?
A: Company School painting was an Indo-European style that developed under the British East India Company in the 18th-19th centuries.
Q: Which state is famous for the 'Manjusha' paintings?
A: Manjusha art is a folk painting style of Bihar, associated with the Bishahari Puja.
Q: What is 'Pithora' painting?
A: Pithora is a ritual wall painting of the Rathwa-Bhilala community of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
Q: Which painting is done by women of Mithila during festivals?
A: Mithila (Madhubani) painting is traditionally done by women during festivals and ceremonies.
Q: Which folk painting of Andhra Pradesh is done on festival occasions?
A: Cheriyal scroll painting, done on cloth with natural colors, is a folk painting of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

Q: Which civilization is famous for the 'Dancing Girl' statue?
A: The Harappan (Indus Valley) civilization is famous for the bronze 'Dancing Girl' statue found at Mohenjo-daro.

A: The 'Dancing Girl' was created by the unknown artisans of the Harappan civilization around 2500 BCE.
Q: What is the 'Priest-King' statue?
A: The 'Priest-King' is a famous steatite (soapstone) sculpture of the Harappan civilization found at Mohenjo-daro.
Q: Which is the famous bronze sculpture of the Chola period?
A: The Nataraja bronze sculpture, depicting Lord Shiva as the cosmic dancer, is the famous Chola period bronze.
Q: What is the 'Nataraja' symbol?
A: Nataraja symbolizes the cosmic dance of Shiva, representing creation, preservation and destruction.
Q: Which site is famous for the lion capital of Ashoka?
A: Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh is famous for the Lion Capital of Ashoka, the national emblem of India.
Q: What does the Lion Capital symbolize?
