### Manufacturing, MSME & Handloom of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-manufacturing-msme-handloom/
Summary: Important questions on Assam manufacturing, MSME and handloom sector for Assam competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: Which is the premier state agency for industrial development in Assam?
A: The Assam Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) is the premier agency for industrial development.
Q: When was the Assam Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) established?
A: AIDC was established in 1962 to promote industrial development in Assam.
Q: What is the primary role of AIDC in the industrial sector?
A: AIDC provides term loans, equity participation and financial assistance to medium and large industries.
Q: Which scheme promotes micro and small enterprises in Assam through financial support?
A: The PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme) promotes micro and small enterprises with subsidy.
Q: Which handloom village of Assam is known as the 'Manchester of Assam' for silk weaving?
A: Sualkuchi in Kamrup district is known as the 'Manchester of Assam' for its silk weaving industry.
Q: Which type of silk produced in Assam is the rarest and unique in the world?
A: Muga silk, produced only in Assam, is the rarest and unique golden-coloured silk in the world.
Q: Which is the most widely produced silk in Assam?
A: Eri silk is the most widely produced silk in Assam, mostly spun from castor-fed eri worms.
Q: Which silk is also called 'Endi' or 'Errandi' silk in Assam?
A: Eri silk is also known as 'Endi' or 'Errandi' silk in Assam.
Q: Which variety of mulberry silk is produced in Assam?
A: The 'Pat' (mulberry) silk variety is produced in Assam, mainly in Kamrup and adjacent areas.
Q: Which government body promotes sericulture and handloom development in Assam?
A: The Directorate of Sericulture and the Directorate of Handloom and Textiles promote these sectors in Assam.
Q: Which organisation is the apex agency for sericulture development in India?
A: The Central Silk Board (CSB) is the apex agency for sericulture development in India.
Q: Which traditional Assamese handloom product is an inseparable part of Assamese culture?
A: The Gamosa, a white rectangular cotton cloth with red borders, is an inseparable part of Assamese culture.
Q: Which fabric is used to make the traditional Assamese 'Mekhela Chador'?
A: The Mekhela Chador is traditionally woven from mulberry (pat) or muga silk.
Q: Which scheme provides financial assistance to handloom weavers in Assam?
A: Schemes like the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and Yarn Supply Scheme assist weavers.
Q: What is the approximate number of handloom weavers in Assam?
A: Assam has over 12 lakh handloom weavers, making it one of the largest handloom states in India.
Q: Which is the major industrial estate of Assam located near Guwahati?
A: The Amingaon Industrial Estate near Guwahati is a major industrial estate in Assam.
Q: Which agency develops industrial areas and estates in Assam?
A: The Assam Small Industries Development Corporation (ASIDC) develops industrial estates and areas.
Q: Which Assam government scheme provides seed capital to young entrepreneurs?
A: The Swami Vivekananda Assam Youth Empowerment Scheme (SVAYEM) provides seed capital to young entrepreneurs.
Q: What is the full form of the scheme PMEGP?
A: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme.
Q: Which organization implements PMEGP in Assam?
A: The KVIC (Khadi and Village Industries Commission) and state KVIB implement PMEGP.
Q: Which Assam-based refinery company was set up as a subsidiary of OIL?
A: Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) was set up as a subsidiary of Oil India Limited.
Q: Which fertilizer plant of Assam is located at Namrup?
A: The Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer Corporation (BVFCL) plant is located at Namrup.
Q: Which cement plant is located at Bokajan in Assam?
A: The Cement Corporation of India (CCI) plant is located at Bokajan in Karbi Anglong.
Q: What is the major jute processing centre of Assam?
A: The jute mills are mainly located in the Barak valley, especially around Silchar and Karimganj.
Q: Which industrial policy of Assam was launched in 2019?
A: The Assam Industrial Policy 2019 was launched to promote investment and industrial growth.
Q: Which scheme of Assam offers incentives for setting up new industrial units?
A: The Assam Industrial Policy 2019 provides incentives like capital subsidy, interest subsidy and power subsidy.
Q: Which industry is the largest agro-based industry in Assam?
A: The tea industry is the largest agro-based industry in Assam.
Q: What is the role of the Assam State Co-operative Marketing Society (ASCM) in the economy?
A: ASCM markets agricultural and co-operative products, facilitating trade for farmers.
Q: Which bamboo-based industry is being promoted under the North East bamboo policy?
A: Bamboo furniture, handicrafts, flooring and bamboo shoot processing industries are being promoted.
Q: Which organisation provides financial support to MSMEs in Assam?
A: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and state financial corporations support MSMEs.
Q: What is the target of the 'Make in Assam' initiative?
A: The 'Make in Assam' initiative aims to boost local manufacturing and attract investment in the state.
Q: Which Assam textile park was approved for muga silk processing?
A: The proposed Assam Silk Textile Park aims to develop the muga and eri silk value chain.
Q: Which agency is responsible for skill development for industry in Assam?
A: The Assam Skill Development Mission (ASDM) provides skill training aligned with industry needs.
Q: What is the significance of the 'Assam Silk' GI tag?
A: The GI tag protects the unique identity and quality of Assam's muga, eri and pat silk products.
Q: Which is the oldest textile mill of Assam?
A: The Assam Silk Mills at Gohpur is one of the oldest textile units of Assam.

### Minerals, Oil & Natural Gas of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-minerals-oil-gas-coal/
Summary: Important questions on minerals, oil and natural gas of Assam for Assam competitive exams. Useful for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other Assam government exams.
Q: Which town of Assam is known as the birthplace of the oil industry in Asia?
A: Digboi, where the first oil well of Asia was drilled in 1889 and production began in 1901.
Q: In which year was the first oil well in Asia drilled at Digboi?
A: In 1889, and commercial production started in 1901.
Q: Which is the oldest operating oil refinery in Asia?
A: The Digboi Refinery, which was established in 1901 and is still operational.
Q: Which company, with headquarters at Duliajan, is a major oil producer in Assam?
A: Oil India Limited (OIL), which was founded in 1889 as the Assam Oil Company's successor and nationalised in 1961.
Q: In which year was Oil India Limited (OIL) nationalised and made a public sector company?
A: In 1961, when the Government of India took over the company with headquarters at Duliajan, Assam.
Q: Which oilfield of Assam is the oldest producing field?
A: The Digboi oilfield, which began production in 1901.
Q: Which town in Assam is the headquarters of ONGC's eastern region assets?
A: Sivasagar (and its nearby areas like Nazira), where ONGC has its eastern region operational headquarters.
Q: Which company discovered the Naharkatia oilfield in 1953?
A: The Assam Oil Company, with the Naharkatia field later being developed by Oil India Limited.
Q: Which district of Assam contains the Moran oilfield?
A: The Moran oilfield is located in the Dibrugarh district (near Moranhat).
Q: Which is the oldest oilfield of Assam discovered in 1889 by the Assam Railway and Trading Company?
A: The Digboi oilfield, discovered in 1889 and brought into production in 1901.
Q: Where is the headquarters of ONGC in Assam located?
A: ONGC's eastern region headquarters is at Nazira near Sivasagar, with its corporate presence in Guwahati.
Q: Which refinery of Assam is the largest in terms of installed capacity?
A: The Numaligarh Refinery (NRL), with a capacity of 3 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA).
Q: In which district is the Numaligarh Refinery located?
A: In Golaghat district, near Numaligarh town on the banks of the Dhansiri river.
Q: When was the Numaligarh Refinery commissioned?
A: The Numaligarh Refinery was commissioned in 1999.
Q: Which company owns the Numaligarh Refinery?
A: Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL), a subsidiary of Oil India Limited.
Q: Which refinery of Assam is located in the Barak valley?
A: There is a refinery at Silchar (Cachar Refinery under NRL); the main Bongaigaon refinery is in the Brahmaputra valley.
Q: Which refinery of Assam was established in collaboration with IOC and is known for petrochemical production?
A: The Bongaigaon Refinery and Petrochemicals (BRPL), now owned by Indian Oil Corporation.
Q: In which year was the Bongaigaon Refinery commissioned?
A: The Bongaigaon Refinery was commissioned in 1979.
Q: Which refinery of Assam was the first to be established by Indian Oil Corporation?
A: The Guwahati Refinery, commissioned in 1962, was the first refinery of Indian Oil Corporation in the North-East.
Q: In which district is the Guwahati Refinery located?
A: In Kamrup Metropolitan district, at Noonmati in Guwahati.
Q: Which PSU is the major producer of crude oil in Assam?
A: ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is the largest crude oil producer, followed by Oil India Limited.
Q: Which company of India is responsible for refining Assam's crude oil?
A: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) operates the Guwahati and Bongaigaon refineries, and NRL the Numaligarh refinery.
Q: What is the name of the company formed to distribute natural gas in Assam?
A: Assam Gas Company Limited (AGCL), which distributes natural gas for industrial and domestic use in the state.
Q: Which town of Assam has a major natural gas-based power plant?
A: The Lakwa and Amguri gas-based power plants (in Sivasagar district) are major natural gas power stations of the state.
Q: Which mineral coal reserve of Assam is the largest and most important?
A: The Makum coalfield in Tinsukia district is the largest and most important coal field of Assam.
Q: Which district of Assam has large deposits of limestone?
A: Karbi Anglong district has large limestone deposits, which supply raw material for cement manufacturing.
Q: Which company operates the cement plant at Bokajan in Karbi Anglong using local limestone?
A: The Cement Corporation of India (CCI) operates the Bokajan cement plant.
Q: Which other minerals found in Assam include high-grade iron ore?
A: Assam has iron ore deposits in the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao regions, though not commercially exploited at scale.
Q: What is the approximate share of Assam in India's total crude oil production?
A: Assam contributes about 3-4% of India's total crude oil production.
Q: Which pipeline transports crude oil from Assam to the Barauni refinery?
A: The Naharkatia-Nunmati-Barauni (NNB) crude oil pipeline, the first major cross-country pipeline of India.
Q: When was the Naharkatia-Nunmati-Barauni pipeline commissioned?
A: It was commissioned in 1963-64 as India's first major oil pipeline.
Q: Which gas field of Assam is the largest onshore gas field in India?
A: The Geleky field (in Sivasagar district) was historically among the largest onshore gas fields of India.
Q: Which oilfield near Digboi is famous for producing the lightest grade of crude oil in India?
A: The Digboi and Naharkatia oilfields produce lighter grades of crude compared to other Indian fields.
Q: True or False: The Digboi refinery is the first refinery established in India.
A: True. The Digboi refinery (1901) is the first and oldest refinery in India and Asia.
Q: Which natural gas pipeline connects Assam to the rest of North-East India and the national grid?
A: The Jagiroad gas network and the North-East Gas Grid project connect Assam's gas fields to consumers and the national grid.

### Assam Power & Energy | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-power-energy-sector/
Summary: Important questions on Assam power and energy sector for Assam competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Which is the largest hydroelectric project in Assam?
A: The Lower Subansiri Hydroelectric Project (2000 MW), located on the Subansiri river, is the largest.
Q: When was the Assam State Electricity Board (ASEB) established?
A: The Assam State Electricity Board was established in 1958 under the Electricity (Supply) Act 1948.
Q: In which year was the ASEB unbundled into separate generation, transmission and distribution companies?
A: The ASEB was unbundled in 2003, creating APGCL, AEGCL and APDCL.
Q: What does APDCL stand for in the Assam power sector?
A: APDCL stands for Assam Power Distribution Company Limited.
Q: Which company handles electricity generation in Assam after unbundling?
A: Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL) handles electricity generation.
Q: Which company is responsible for electricity transmission in Assam?
A: Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited (AEGCL) is responsible for transmission.
Q: On which river is the Kopili Hydroelectric Project located?
A: The Kopili Hydroelectric Project is located on the Kopili river, a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
Q: Which project supplies power to the Kopili system from Meghalaya?
A: The Khandong and Umiam (Barapani) projects of Meghalaya supply power to the Kopili system.
Q: What is the installed hydroelectric capacity of the Kopili project?
A: The Kopili project has an installed capacity of about 150 MW (Kopili-I and Kopili-II).
Q: Where is the Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station located?
A: The Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station is located at Salakati near Bongaigaon in western Assam.
Q: What is the installed capacity of the Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station?
A: It has an installed capacity of 250 MW (3 units of 60 MW and 1 unit of 70 MW).
Q: Which is the only thermal power station owned by APGCL?
A: The Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station at Salakati is the only thermal plant owned by APGCL.
Q: On which river is the Lower Subansiri Hydroelectric Project located?
A: It is located on the Subansiri river at the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border near Gerukamukh.
Q: Who is developing the Lower Subansiri Hydroelectric Project?
A: The National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) is developing the project.
Q: Which river project is the Karbi Langpi Hydroelectric Project associated with?
A: The Karbi Langpi project is associated with the Borpani (Karbi Langpi) river in Karbi Anglong district.
Q: Which commission regulates electricity tariffs in Assam?
A: The Assam Electricity Regulatory Commission (AERC) regulates electricity tariffs.
Q: In which year was the AERC established?
A: The Assam Electricity Regulatory Commission was established in 2001.
Q: Which scheme aims to provide free electricity connections to households under the rural electrification drive?
A: Under schemes like Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) and Saubhagya, households get free electricity connections.
Q: Which agency implemented rural electrification under DDUGJY in Assam?
A: APDCL implemented rural electrification under DDUGJY in Assam.
Q: What is the approximate installed power generation capacity of Assam (including state, central and private)?
A: Assam's total installed power capacity is roughly around 1500-2000 MW, with a large share coming from central sector projects.
Q: Which organisation generates electricity from natural gas in Assam?
A: The Assam Power Generation Company and central utilities like NTPC use natural gas to generate power in Assam.
Q: Which gas-based power project is located at Kathalguri in Assam?
A: The Kathalguri Gas-based Combined Cycle Power Project of NTPC (291 MW) is located there.
Q: Which state-owned company markets natural gas in Assam?
A: Assam Gas Company Limited (AGCL), a joint venture of the state government, markets natural gas.
Q: What is the share of hydroelectric power in Assam's state-owned generation?
A: Hydroelectric power forms the majority share of APGCL's generation capacity.
Q: Which ministry is responsible for the Ministry of Development of North East Region?
A: The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) is responsible for NE development including power projects.
Q: Which national scheme focuses on strengthening power transmission in the North East region?
A: The North Eastern Region Power System Improvement Project (NERPSIP) focuses on strengthening NE transmission.
Q: Which organisation owns the Umrangso thermal power station in Assam?
A: The Umrangso thermal power station is a captive plant of the cement industry, owned by private companies.
Q: What is the key objective of the Saubhagya scheme implemented in Assam?
A: Saubhagya aims to provide electricity connections to all households including rural areas by 2019.
Q: Which renewable energy source is being promoted by Assam's solar policy?
A: Solar energy is being promoted under the Assam Solar Power Policy and PM-KUSUM.
Q: What is the peak power demand situation of Assam generally referred to as?
A: Assam generally faces a power deficit during peak demand periods, leading to load shedding.
Q: Which institute manages the North Eastern Regional Load Despatch Centre (NERLDC)?
A: The Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCIL) operates the NERLDC at Shillong.
Q: Which river in Assam is the site of the proposed Tipaimukh/Palchen multi-purpose project debate?
A: The proposed Palchen multi-purpose project is on the Barak river, while Tipaimukh is on the Barak basin in Manipur.
Q: Which central PSU commissioned the 120 MW Lower Kopili project in Assam?
A: The Lower Kopili Hydroelectric Project (120 MW) was commissioned by NHPC.
Q: What is the role of the State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC) in Assam?
A: The SLDC coordinates and controls the real-time operation of the state grid for reliable power supply.
Q: Which scheme provides subsidy-free electricity for agriculture pumps in Assam?
A: PM-KUSUM provides solarised agriculture pumps with subsidy, reducing dependence on grid electricity.

### Tea Industry & Sericulture of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-tea-sericulture/
Summary: Important questions on tea industry and sericulture of Assam for Assam competitive exams. Useful for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other Assam government exams.
Q: What share of India's total tea production does Assam contribute?
A: Assam produces over half (about 50-55%) of India's total tea output, making it the largest tea-producing state of the country.
Q: In which valley of Assam are the majority of tea gardens located?
A: The Brahmaputra Valley (upper Assam in particular), where the climate and soil favour tea cultivation.
Q: Which district of Assam is called the 'Tea Capital of the World'?
A: Dibrugarh district is often referred to as the 'Tea City of India' or 'Tea Capital of the World'.
Q: Who was the first British officer to establish a tea garden in Assam by clearing forest near Chabua?
A: C.A. Bruce, who established the first tea garden in Assam near Chabua in 1836.
Q: In which year was the first commercial tea garden of Assam established?
A: In 1837, when the East India Company established the first tea garden near Chabua; exports to London began soon after.
Q: Which town is known as the headquarters of the tea industry in Assam?
A: Jorhat, which houses the Tea Research Association and its headquarters (Tocklai Tea Research Institute).
Q: What is the difference between CTC and orthodox tea?
A: CTC (Crush, Tear, Curl) is machine-processed into small granular pellets suited for strong milk tea, while orthodox tea is rolled leaf tea with a delicate flavour.
Q: Which variety of tea is exclusively produced in large quantities in Assam and known for its strong malty flavour?
A: Assam black tea (Assamica), known for its brisk, malty and strong-bodied liquor.
Q: Which institute in Assam is Asia's first and the world's oldest tea research institute?
A: The Tocklai Tea Research Institute at Jorhat, established in 1911.
Q: How many workers does the tea industry of Assam employ approximately?
A: The tea industry directly and indirectly employs over 10 lakh (about 10-12 lakh) workers, mostly women from tea garden communities.
Q: Which port is traditionally used for exporting Assam tea?
A: The Kolkata port (and earlier through the Kolkata auction centre) is the traditional export channel for Assam tea.
Q: Which river was historically used as the main waterway for transporting tea from upper Assam to Kolkata?
A: The Brahmaputra river, along which tea chests were ferried downstream to the port of Kolkata.
Q: Which is the largest tea auction centre of Assam?
A: The Guwahati Tea Auction Centre (GTAC), one of the largest tea auction centres in the world.
Q: In which year did the first tea auction take place in Guwahati?
A: In 1970, when the Guwahati Tea Auction Centre was established.
Q: Which silk variety is unique to Assam and produced nowhere else in the world?
A: Muga silk, which is golden-yellow in colour and has been granted a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.
Q: Which silkworm produces muga silk, and what is its host plant?
A: The Antheraea assamensis silkworm, which feeds primarily on the Som (Machilus bombycina) and Soalu (Litsaea polyantha) plants.
Q: Which silk of Assam is white/off-white and produced mainly in the Brahmaputra valley from the eri silkworm?
A: Eri silk, which is known as the 'peace silk' because the pupae are not killed during extraction.
Q: Which mulberry silk variety is produced in Assam, mainly in the Goalpara and Barpeta belt?
A: Mulberry silk (from the Bombyx mori silkworm), which is produced on a smaller scale in the state.
Q: Which silk variety is also known as 'endangered silk' and is produced in parts of North-East India besides Assam?
A: Muga silk, whose production is restricted to Assam and parts of the adjoining North-Eastern states.
Q: Which town of Assam is famous as the 'Manchester of the East' for its silk weaving industry?
A: Sualkuchi, located on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Kamrup district, famous for its handloom silk weaving.
Q: Which department/body of the Government of Assam is responsible for the development of sericulture in the state?
A: The Directorate of Sericulture, under the Department of Handloom, Textiles and Sericulture of Assam.
Q: What is the name of the Assam government agency that promotes the marketing of Assam silk?
A: The Assam Silk Outreach Mission and the Assam Silk Mark Organisation, along with AINSTTM (Assam Institute of Silk and Textile Technology Management).
Q: Which silk of Assam received the GI tag in the same year as the Bhut Jolokia (2008)?
A: Muga silk received the GI tag in 2008; subsequently, Eri and Mulberry silk also received GI tags.
Q: Which silk variety of Assam is used to make the traditional Assamese mekhela chador?
A: Muga silk is the most prized for the traditional mekhela chador, followed by Eri and Mulberry silks.
Q: In which region of Assam is muga rearing concentrated?
A: Muga rearing is concentrated in upper Assam districts like Sivasagar, Jorhat, Golaghat and Lakhimpur.
Q: True or False: Eri silk is produced only in Assam and nowhere else in the world.
A: False. Eri silk is also produced in other states like Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland and West Bengal, though Assam is a major producer.
Q: Which scheme of the Government of India promotes the integrated development of the silk sector?
A: The Central Silk Board's scheme under the 'Silk Samagra' programme.
Q: What is the common name of the golden silk obtained from the muga silkworm?
A: Golden silk or Muga silk, renowned for its natural golden-yellow lustre that improves with age.
Q: Which institute at Kokrajhar deals with the training and research in sericulture for the Bodo region?
A: The Regional Sericulture Research Station and training institutes in Kokrajhar serve the region's sericulture development.
Q: Which district of Assam is the largest producer of tea in terms of total area under tea gardens?
A: Dibrugarh district has the largest area under tea gardens in Assam.
Q: What is the name of the festival celebrated by the tea garden workers of Assam in the Assamese month of Bohag (mid-April)?
A: The Rongali Bihu festival is celebrated; tea garden communities also celebrate with their own traditional dance and music.
Q: Which company of the Tata group owns several tea estates in Assam?
A: Tata Consumer Products (Tata Tea) owns several estates in Assam through its subsidiary Amalgamated Plantations.
Q: What is the approximate annual tea production of Assam?
A: Assam produces around 700-750 million kg of tea annually, the highest among Indian states.
Q: Which national institute for tea and coffee (located in Assam) imparts training for the tea industry?
A: The National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM) has a tea-related presence; specifically, the Tea Research Association's Tocklai at Jorhat is the main R&D body.
Q: True or False: The Brahmaputra valley produces more tea than the Barak valley of Assam.
A: True. The Brahmaputra valley accounts for the overwhelming majority of Assam's tea output, with only a few gardens in the Barak valley.

Q: Kaziranga National Park lies on which bank of the Brahmaputra river?

Q: Hojai is famous for which industry?
A: The agarbati (incense stick) manufacturing industry.

A: Nagaon district.

A: Guwahati.

Q: Which town of Assam is known as the 'Tea City of India'?
A: Dibrugarh.

A: Upper Assam, especially Jorhat, Dibrugarh and Tinsukia districts.
Q: The State Bank of India's North East circle head office is located in which city?
A: Guwahati.
Q: Which bank is the sponsor bank of Assam Gramin Vikash Bank?

A: The Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
Q: Assam State Cooperative Apex Bank was established in which year?

Q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched in which year?

A: RuPay debit card.

A: On 1 July 1982, as the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

A: Guwahati.
Q: True or False: The credit-deposit ratio of banks in Assam is generally lower than the national average.
A: True. Assam's credit-deposit ratio is generally lower than the national average, reflecting lower credit offtake in the state.

Q: What is the length of the National Waterway-2 (Brahmaputra) in Assam?

Q: Which authority maintains National Waterways in India?
A: The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) maintains the National Waterways.
Q: Which is the longest bridge in India, located on the Brahmaputra in Assam?

Q: Which bridge connects Guwahati and North Guwahati?

Q: In which year was the Saraighat Bridge commissioned?

Q: Which is the airport in Assam serving international flights?

Q: Which is the second international airport in Assam, located in the Barak valley?

Q: Which railway zone covers the railway network of Assam?

Q: What is the gauge of most railway lines in Assam?

A: The luxury cruise MV Mahabaahu and MV Ganga Vilas routes operate on the Brahmaputra.

A: The State Highways and Major District Roads network connects all district headquarters of Assam.

A: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and PWD (NH wing) construct and maintain national highways.

Q: Which organisation runs the city bus service in Guwahati?
A: The Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC) and the Guwahati Smart City initiative run city bus services.

### Unemployment & Industrial Lag of Assam | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/assam-economy-sec/assam-unemployment-industrial-lag/
Summary: Important questions on unemployment and industrial lag of Assam for Assam competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What is the approximate unemployment rate in Assam compared to the national average?
A: Assam's unemployment rate is generally higher than the national average, especially among educated youth.
Q: What is the main cause of educated unemployment in Assam?
A: Limited industrial base, lack of job-oriented skill training and low private sector investment are the main causes.
Q: Which scheme of Assam provides employment-oriented skill training to youth?
A: The Assam Skill Development Mission (ASDM) under the State Skill Development policy provides skill training.
Q: Which national scheme provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in rural Assam?
A: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provides 100 days of work.
Q: What is 'industrial lag' in the context of Assam's economy?
A: Industrial lag refers to Assam's slow industrialisation compared to other states, with low manufacturing share in GSDP.
Q: Which historical factor contributed to Assam's industrial lag?
A: The partition of 1947 cut off Assam's natural markets and river communication routes to Bangladesh.
Q: Which factor restricts industrial investment in Assam due to its geography?
A: Being a landlocked state with limited access to ports and connectivity gaps restricts industrial investment.
Q: Which state sector has historically been the largest employer in Assam?
A: The agriculture and allied sectors have historically been the largest employers in Assam.
Q: What is the share of agriculture in Assam's workforce?
A: Around 40-45% of Assam's workforce is engaged in agriculture and allied activities.
Q: Which scheme provides free skill training and certification to Assam's youth?
A: The PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana and the ASDM schemes provide free skill training with certification.
Q: What is the trend of out-migration of youth from Assam?
A: Many educated and skilled youth migrate to metro cities and abroad in search of employment.
Q: Which industrial sectors show potential for growth in Assam?
A: Tea processing, oil and gas, food processing, tourism, bamboo and handloom show high growth potential.
Q: Which is the major hurdle in attracting large-scale industry to Assam?
A: Poor infrastructure, high logistics cost, insurgency legacy and limited power supply are major hurdles.
Q: What is the role of the Assam Start-up policy in employment generation?
A: The Assam Start-up Policy provides funding and support to startups, promoting self-employment.
Q: Which scheme of the Government of India supports young entrepreneurs in Assam with collateral-free loans?
A: The MUDRA scheme provides collateral-free micro loans to small entrepreneurs including in Assam.
Q: What is the employment scenario in the tea industry of Assam?
A: The tea industry is a major employer, providing direct employment to over 7-8 lakh workers.
Q: Which government initiative aims to make Assam a hub of food processing industries?
A: The Assam Agro-Industrial Policy and PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana promote food processing in Assam.
Q: What is the main challenge of skill development schemes in Assam?
A: Mismatch between training content and actual industry demand limits the success of skill schemes.
Q: Which is the largest private employer in Assam's organised sector?
A: The tea industry is the largest private employer in Assam's organised sector.
Q: What is the concept of 'hidden unemployment' relevant to Assam's rural areas?
A: Hidden (disguised) unemployment occurs when more people work on land than required, common in rural Assam.
Q: Which initiative of the Assam government provides financial assistance to job-seekers?
A: The Assam Job Portal and employment assistance schemes provide allowances and support to job-seekers.
Q: What is the contribution of the tertiary (services) sector to Assam's GSDP?
A: The services sector contributes around 50-55% of Assam's GSDP, being the largest sector.
Q: Why is industrialisation in Assam considered slower than in southern states?
A: Geographical isolation, historical neglect and poor infrastructure have slowed Assam's industrialisation.
Q: Which mega project of Assam is expected to boost employment in the power sector?
A: The Lower Subansiri Hydroelectric Project and related transmission projects are expected to create jobs.
Q: What is the role of the North East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS) 2017?
A: NEIDS 2017 provides incentives to industries in the North East, including Assam, to promote investment.
Q: Which is the biggest challenge of the employment sector in the Barak valley?
A: Limited industrial development and connectivity with the rest of the state create employment challenges.
Q: What is the impact of floods on Assam's employment and economy?
A: Floods destroy crops, infrastructure and disrupt livelihoods, increasing rural unemployment and poverty.
Q: Which organisation provides employment data for Assam?
A: The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) and DES Assam provide data.
Q: Which is the fastest-growing employment sector in Assam in recent years?
A: The services sector, including IT, tourism, healthcare and education, is growing fastest.
Q: What is the main objective of the Assam skill development policy?
A: To skill and upskill the workforce to meet industry demand and reduce unemployment.
Q: Which factor has been identified as the biggest deterrent for FDI in Assam?
A: Infrastructure bottlenecks and connectivity deficits are identified as the biggest deterrents for FDI.
Q: Which scheme of Assam provides grants to youth for self-employment ventures?
A: The SVAYEM scheme provides seed capital grants to youth for self-employment ventures.
Q: What is the expected outcome of the 'Act East' policy on Assam's employment?
A: Improved connectivity and trade are expected to create new jobs in logistics, tourism and services.
Q: Which is the major hindrance to the growth of the IT sector in Assam?
A: Lack of adequate digital infrastructure, skilled manpower and private investment hinder IT growth.

### Balance of Payments & Foreign Exchange | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/bop-forex-reserves-india/
Summary: Important questions on Balance of Payments and foreign exchange for Indian economy competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What are the two main components of the Balance of Payments?
A: The two main components of the Balance of Payments are the Current Account and the Capital Account.
Q: Which account of the Balance of Payments records trade in goods and services?
A: The Current Account records trade in goods and services, income and current transfers.
Q: What is Current Account Deficit (CAD)?
A: Current Account Deficit occurs when the value of imports of goods, services and transfers exceeds exports and receipts.
Q: What is Balance of Trade?
A: Balance of Trade is the difference between the value of merchandise exports and imports of a country.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Current Account — Remittances, FDI inflows, Service exports, or Interest payments?
A: FDI inflows are recorded in the Capital Account, not the Current Account.
Q: What are the four components of India's foreign exchange reserves?
A: India's forex reserves consist of Foreign Currency Assets, Gold, SDRs and the Reserve Tranche Position in the IMF.
Q: Which institution manages India's foreign exchange reserves?
A: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) manages India's foreign exchange reserves.
Q: In which type of exchange rate system is the rupee exchange rate determined by market forces?
A: In a floating exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by market forces of demand and supply.
Q: Which exchange rate system does India currently follow?
A: India follows a managed floating exchange rate system since 1993.
Q: What is the difference between devaluation and depreciation of currency?
A: Devaluation is an official reduction of the currency value in a fixed rate system, while depreciation is the market-driven fall in a floating system.
Q: What does a fall in the value of the rupee against the dollar indicate?
A: A fall in the rupee value indicates rupee depreciation, making imports costlier and exports cheaper.
Q: Which account of the rupee is fully convertible in India as per the Tarapore Committee?
A: The Current Account of the rupee is fully convertible; Capital Account convertibility is only partial in India.
Q: Which Act replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) in 1999?
A: The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999 replaced FERA.
Q: FEMA was enacted in which year?
A: FEMA was enacted in 1999 and came into force on 1 June 2000.
Q: Who administers FEMA in India?
A: The RBI administers FEMA, and enforcement cases are handled by the Directorate of Enforcement.
Q: Rupee depreciation makes Indian exports more competitive. True or false?
A: True, rupee depreciation makes Indian exports cheaper in foreign markets and more competitive.
Q: Who introduced the concept of current account convertibility in India?
A: Current account convertibility was adopted in India in 1994 based on the Tarapore Committee recommendations.
Q: What is LIBOR?
A: LIBOR (London Interbank Offered Rate) was the benchmark interest rate at which major global banks lent to each other.
Q: Which currency is known as a hard currency?
A: The US Dollar is a hard currency because of its stability and wide international acceptance.
Q: What is SDR?
A: SDR (Special Drawing Rights) is an international reserve asset created by the IMF to supplement member countries' reserves.
Q: Which institution issues SDRs?
A: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) issues SDRs.
Q: The Asian Financial Crisis occurred in which year?
A: The Asian Financial Crisis occurred in 1997.
Q: Which currency came under severe pressure during the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis?
A: The Thai Baht came under severe pressure, triggering the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis.
Q: What is a Current Account Surplus?
A: A Current Account Surplus occurs when exports and receipts exceed imports and payments on the current account.
Q: Invisibles in the Current Account include services, income and what?
A: Invisibles include services, income and current transfers such as remittances.
Q: Which of the following is a capital account inflow — Remittances, Export earnings, FDI, or Software earnings?
A: FDI is a capital account inflow; the others are current account receipts.
Q: What is the impact of rupee depreciation on India's import bill?
A: Rupee depreciation makes imports costlier, thereby increasing India's import bill in rupee terms.
Q: Which institution decides the reference rate of the rupee in India?
A: The RBI announces the reference rate of the rupee based on market conditions.
Q: What is the full form of CAD in the Balance of Payments context?
A: CAD stands for Current Account Deficit.
Q: A fixed exchange rate system is also called which kind of exchange rate?
A: A fixed exchange rate system is also called a pegged exchange rate system.
Q: Under the gold standard, currency value was fixed in terms of what?
A: Under the gold standard, currency value was fixed in terms of a fixed quantity of gold.
Q: What is the external commercial borrowing (ECB)?
A: ECB is a loan raised by Indian companies from foreign lenders, recorded in the capital account.
Q: Remittances from Indians working abroad are recorded in which account of the BoP?
A: Remittances are recorded in the Current Account under current transfers.
Q: Which country's currency, the yen, is a widely traded international currency?
A: The yen is the currency of Japan.
Q: In which year did India face a severe BoP crisis leading to economic reforms?
A: India faced a severe BoP crisis in 1991, which led to the economic liberalisation reforms of 1991.

### Capital & Money Markets | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/capital-money-markets-sebi/
Summary: Important questions on capital and money markets for Indian economy competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: When was SEBI established?
A: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) was established in 1988 as a non-statutory body and was given statutory powers in 1992.
Q: In which year did SEBI become a statutory body?
A: SEBI became a statutory body in 1992 under the SEBI Act, 1992.
Q: What is the role of SEBI?
A: SEBI is the regulator of the securities market in India, protecting the interests of investors and regulating stock exchanges, brokers and market intermediaries.
Q: When was the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) established?
A: The BSE was established in 1875 and is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.
Q: When was the National Stock Exchange (NSE) established?
A: The NSE was established in 1992 and started its operations in 1994.
Q: What is the Sensex?
A: Sensex is the benchmark stock index of the Bombay Stock Exchange, comprising 30 leading companies, with base year 1978-79 taken as 100.
Q: What is the Nifty 50?
A: Nifty 50 is the benchmark index of the National Stock Exchange, comprising 50 diversified stocks, with base year 1995 taken as 1000.
Q: What is the primary market?
A: The primary market is where new securities are issued and sold for the first time, such as through IPOs, to raise fresh capital.
Q: What is the secondary market?
A: The secondary market is where already-issued securities are bought and sold by investors, such as on stock exchanges.
Q: What is an IPO?
A: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is the process by which a company offers its shares to the public for the first time to raise capital.
Q: What is an FPO?
A: An FPO (Follow-on Public Offer) is an offering of shares by an already-listed company to raise additional capital from the public.
Q: What is a debenture?
A: A debenture is a debt instrument through which a company borrows money from the public, carrying a fixed rate of interest and a promise to repay.
Q: Name two instruments of the money market.
A: Treasury Bills, call money, repos, Commercial Paper and Certificates of Deposit are the main instruments of the money market.
Q: What are Treasury Bills?
A: Treasury Bills are short-term (up to one year) borrowing instruments of the government, issued by the RBI at a discount and redeemed at face value.
Q: What are the maturity periods of Treasury Bills issued in India?
A: Treasury Bills are issued in India with maturities of 91 days, 182 days and 364 days.
Q: What is call money?
A: Call money is money lent or borrowed between banks for a very short period, usually one day, at an agreed rate of interest.
Q: What is a repo in the money market?
A: A repo (repurchase agreement) is an agreement where securities are sold with a promise to repurchase them later, used for short-term borrowing.
Q: What is a Commercial Paper?
A: A Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term promissory note issued by companies to raise funds for a short period, usually 7 to 365 days.
Q: What is a Certificate of Deposit?
A: A Certificate of Deposit is a short-term negotiable deposit instrument issued by banks and financial institutions in dematerialised form.
Q: What is a Credit Default Swap (CDS)?
A: A Credit Default Swap is a credit derivative contract in which one party buys protection against the default of a borrower in exchange for regular payments.
Q: How many stocks does the Nifty 50 index comprise?
A: The Nifty 50 index comprises 50 stocks selected from different sectors of the Indian economy.
Q: What are derivatives?
A: Derivatives are financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying asset, such as futures and options.
Q: What is insider trading and why is it banned?
A: Insider trading is trading in securities based on unpublished price-sensitive information, and it is banned under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations to ensure fairness.
Q: What is a mutual fund?
A: A mutual fund is a pooled investment vehicle through which money from many investors is invested in a diversified portfolio of securities by an asset management company.
Q: What is AMFI?
A: AMFI, the Association of Mutual Funds in India, is the industry body of mutual fund companies that also conducts the AMFI certification exam for distributors.
Q: What are NSDL and CDSL?
A: NSDL and CDSL are the two depositories of India that hold securities in electronic (dematerialised) form on behalf of investors.
Q: Which was the first depository of India?
A: NSDL (National Securities Depository Ltd), established in 1996, was the first depository of India.
Q: What is DEMAT form of holding securities?
A: DEMAT means dematerialised form, in which securities are held electronically in a depository account instead of physical share certificates.
Q: What is the base year of the Sensex?
A: The base year of the Sensex is 1978-79, taken as 100.
Q: What is the base year of the Nifty 50?
A: The base year of the Nifty 50 is 1995, taken as 1000.
Q: Where is the headquarters of SEBI located?
A: The headquarters of SEBI is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
Q: Which institution regulates stock exchanges in India?
A: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) regulates the stock exchanges in India.
Q: What is FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment)?
A: FPI is investment by foreign investors in the financial assets of a country, such as stocks and bonds, without taking management control.
Q: What is the basic difference between a share and a debenture?
A: A share represents ownership in a company and gives dividends and voting rights, while a debenture is a debt instrument giving fixed interest without ownership or voting rights.
Q: Which is the oldest stock exchange in Asia?
A: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), established in 1875, is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.

A: Yes. Every question and answer in this topic is bilingual, so you can practise in Assamese and English.

### Commercial Banking, NPAs & Financial Inclusion | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/commercial-banking-npa-inclusion/
Summary: Important questions on commercial banking, NPAs and financial inclusion for Indian economy competitive exams. Covers ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: What are scheduled commercial banks?
A: Scheduled commercial banks are those banks included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, which makes them eligible for RBI facilities.
Q: When was the first round of nationalization of 14 major commercial banks carried out?
A: The first round of nationalization of 14 major commercial banks was carried out on 19 July 1969.
Q: How many banks were nationalized in the second round in 1980?
A: Six banks were nationalized in the second round in 1980.
Q: What was the total number of banks nationalized in 1969?
A: Fourteen banks were nationalized in 1969.
Q: In which year was the State Bank of India formed and from which bank was it created?
A: The State Bank of India was formed in 1955 from the nationalization of the Imperial Bank of India.
Q: In 2017, how many banks were merged into the State Bank of India?
A: In April 2017, five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged into SBI, making it six banks in all.
Q: What is a Non-Performing Asset (NPA)?
A: An NPA is a loan or advance whose interest or principal instalment remains overdue for a period of more than 90 days.
Q: After how many days of overdue does a loan become an NPA?
A: A loan becomes an NPA if the interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
Q: What is the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
A: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 empowers banks and financial institutions to recover non-performing assets by enforcing security interests without the intervention of courts.
Q: What is the main purpose of the SARFAESI Act?
A: The main purpose of the SARFAESI Act is to enable banks to recover bad loans quickly by selling the mortgaged assets of defaulters without court intervention.
Q: What is the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016?
A: The IBC, 2016 is the comprehensive law for time-bound resolution of insolvency and bankruptcy of companies, with a single unified framework.
Q: Which committee's recommendations led to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
A: The Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, chaired by T. K. Vishwanathan, submitted the report that led to the IBC, 2016.
Q: What is an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC)?
A: An ARC is a company that buys non-performing assets (bad loans) from banks at a discounted price and tries to recover them.
Q: What are Basel norms?
A: Basel norms are international banking standards on capital adequacy and risk management, set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision of the Bank for International Settlements.
Q: What is the minimum CRAR required for Indian banks under Basel norms?
A: The minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) required for Indian banks is 9 percent.
Q: What is capital adequacy in banking?
A: Capital adequacy is the ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-weighted assets, ensuring that the bank has enough capital to absorb potential losses.
Q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
A: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 as a national mission for financial inclusion.
Q: What is the slogan of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
A: The slogan of PMJDY is Mera Khata, Bhagya Vidhata.
Q: What are payment banks?
A: Payment banks are niche banks that accept demand deposits (up to a limit), provide payment services and remittances, but cannot lend money.
Q: Which was the first payment bank to start operations in India?
A: Airtel Payments Bank was the first payment bank to begin operations in India, starting in 2017.
Q: What are small finance banks?
A: Small finance banks are banks that focus on financial inclusion, providing loans and savings services primarily to small farmers, micro and small industries and unorganized sectors.
Q: What is BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System)?
A: BBPS is an integrated bill payment system launched by NPCI that provides interoperable and recurring bill payment services across India.
Q: What is financial literacy?
A: Financial literacy is the ability to understand and effectively use various financial skills, including budgeting, saving, investing and managing debt.
Q: What is the priority sector lending target for commercial banks in India?
A: Commercial banks have to lend 40 percent of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to the priority sector.
Q: Name two sectors that come under priority sector lending.
A: Agriculture, micro and small enterprises (MSME), education, housing and weaker sections are the main constituents of priority sector lending.
Q: What is the Lead Bank Scheme?
A: Under the Lead Bank Scheme, introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the Nariman Committee, one bank in each district takes the lead in coordinating credit and banking development.
Q: Under which Act were the Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) established?
A: Regional Rural Banks were established under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
Q: What was the first Regional Rural Bank of India?
A: Prathama Bank, sponsored by Syndicate Bank and set up on 2 October 1975, was the first RRB of India.
Q: In what proportion are Regional Rural Banks owned?
A: RRBs are jointly owned by the central government, the state government and the sponsor bank in the ratio of 50:15:35.
Q: What are cooperative banks?
A: Cooperative banks are banks organized on the cooperative principle, owned and operated by their members, mainly serving agriculture and rural areas.
Q: What is the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework of the RBI?
A: The PCA framework imposes financial and regulatory restrictions on banks with weak capital, high NPAs or poor profitability, to help them recover.
Q: What does scheduled status of a bank mean?
A: A scheduled bank is one included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, and hence eligible for RBI facilities and liquidity support.
Q: Who regulates urban cooperative banks in India?
A: Urban cooperative banks are regulated by the RBI, while rural cooperative banks are supervised mainly through NABARD and the state governments.
Q: What is NABARD?
A: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is the apex institution for rural credit in India, established in 1982.
Q: What is the maximum amount of deposit a payment bank can accept from an individual?
A: A payment bank can accept deposits up to ₹2 lakh from an individual customer.

### Demographics & Human Development (Census, HDI) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/demographics-hdi-census-india/
Summary: Important questions on demographics and human development for Indian economy competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: What was the total population of India as per the Census 2011?
A: The total population of India as per Census 2011 was 121.08 crore, often rounded to about 121 crore.
Q: Which ministry conducts the decennial Census in India?
A: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts the decennial Census.
Q: In which year was the first census of independent India conducted?
A: The first census of independent India was conducted in 1951.
Q: In which year was the first census in India conducted during British rule?
A: The first all-India census was conducted in 1872 during British rule, under the supervision of Lord Mayo.
Q: What is the term for the number of females per 1000 males in a population?
A: It is called the sex ratio, expressed as the number of females per 1000 males.
Q: As per Census 2011, what was the sex ratio of India?
A: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio of India was 943 females per 1000 males.
Q: What was the literacy rate of India as per Census 2011?
A: The overall literacy rate of India as per Census 2011 was 74.04 percent.
Q: Which state has the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011?
A: Kerala has the highest literacy rate of about 94 percent as per Census 2011.
Q: What is the population growth rate of India as per Census 2011 compared to the previous decade?
A: The decadal population growth rate of India during 2001-2011 was 17.70 percent, a decline from 21.54 percent in the previous decade.
Q: What is the term for the ratio of dependents (children and aged) to the working-age population?
A: It is called the dependency ratio, which measures the load on the working-age population.
Q: What does 'demographic dividend' refer to?
A: Demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential that results from a shift in the age structure towards a larger working-age population and smaller dependent population.
Q: What is the full form of HDI?
A: HDI stands for Human Development Index, published by the UNDP in its annual Human Development Report.
Q: Which organization publishes the Human Development Report?
A: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the annual Human Development Report.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index?
A: HDI is based on three components - health (life expectancy), education and income (GNI per capita); military expenditure is not a component.
Q: Health in the HDI is measured by which indicator?
A: Health in the HDI is measured by life expectancy at birth.
Q: Education in the HDI is measured by which indicators?
A: Education in HDI is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.
Q: Income in the HDI is measured by which indicator?
A: Income in HDI is measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, adjusted for purchasing power parity.
Q: As per the latest UNDP Human Development Report, India is placed in which category of human development?
A: India falls in the medium human development category as per the recent UNDP Human Development Report.
Q: Which country topped the UNDP Human Development Index for several recent years?
A: Switzerland has topped the UNDP Human Development Index in several recent reports.
Q: The HDI value ranges between which two numbers?
A: The HDI value ranges between 0 and 1.
Q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about India's age structure?
A: India has a young population with a large proportion in the working-age group, giving it a demographic dividend advantage.
Q: Which of the following indices is released by NITI Aayog to measure the progress of states towards the SDGs?
A: NITI Aayog releases the SDG India Index to measure the progress of states and Union Territories towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
Q: The Census 2021 in India was postponed primarily due to what reason?
A: The Census 2021 was postponed primarily due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Q: What is the term for the difference between the birth rate and the death rate of a population?
A: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate is called the natural growth rate of population.
Q: Which stage of the demographic transition theory is characterized by low birth rate and low death rate?
A: The third/late stage of the demographic transition is characterized by both low birth rate and low death rate, leading to near-stable population.
Q: As per Census 2011, which state has the highest population in India?
A: Uttar Pradesh has the highest population among Indian states as per Census 2011.
Q: Which state has the lowest population density among major states as per Census 2011?
A: Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest population density in India, with just 17 persons per square kilometre as per Census 2011.
Q: What is the national average population density of India as per Census 2011?
A: The national average population density of India as per Census 2011 was 382 persons per square kilometre.
Q: The population of India is projected to surpass which country to become the most populous nation?
A: India surpassed China to become the world's most populous nation in 2023.
Q: What is the sex ratio at birth (number of girls per 1000 boys) indicator used to measure in India?
A: The sex ratio at birth is used to detect gender imbalance, reflecting practices like female foeticide and skewed child sex ratio.
Q: Which institution publishes the 'National Family Health Survey' (NFHS) in India?
A: The National Family Health Survey is conducted by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Q: Which of the following is a consequence of a high dependency ratio in a country?
A: A high dependency ratio puts pressure on the working population to support more dependents, reducing per capita savings and growth.
Q: As per Census 2011, India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was how many girls per 1000 boys?
A: India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was 919 girls per 1000 boys as per Census 2011, the lowest since independence.
Q: Which of the following is the most densely populated state of India as per Census 2011?
A: Bihar is the most densely populated state of India as per Census 2011, with about 1106 persons per square kilometre.
Q: What is the full form of UNDP?
A: UNDP stands for the United Nations Development Programme, which publishes the Human Development Report.

### Digital Infrastructure & FinTech | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/digital-infrastructure-fintech-india/
Summary: Important questions on digital infrastructure and FinTech for Indian economy competitive exams. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: When was the Digital India programme launched?
A: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 by the Government of India.
Q: What is the vision of the Digital India programme?
A: The vision of Digital India is to transform India into a digitally empowered society and a knowledge economy.
Q: What is BharatNet?
A: BharatNet (earlier known as NOFN) is the flagship project of the Government of India to connect all gram panchayats with high-speed broadband network.
Q: Which ministry implements the BharatNet project?
A: The Department of Telecommunications under the Ministry of Communications implements BharatNet, with BSNL as a major executing agency.
Q: What is UPI?
A: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is an instant real-time payment system developed by NPCI that allows money transfer between any two bank accounts through a mobile platform.
Q: In which year was UPI launched in India?
A: UPI was launched on 11 April 2016 by the Reserve Bank of India and NPCI.
Q: What is the full form of NPCI?
A: NPCI stands for National Payments Corporation of India, the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India.
Q: When was NPCI established?
A: NPCI was established in 2008, with the approval of the Reserve Bank of India, to build a robust retail payments system.
Q: What is Aadhaar?
A: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number issued by the UIDAI to residents of India, based on their biometric and demographic data.
Q: Under which Act does Aadhaar get its legal backing?
A: Aadhaar gets its legal backing from the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.
Q: What is UIDAI?
A: UIDAI, the Unique Identification Authority of India, is the statutory body (established under the Aadhaar Act 2016) that issues Aadhaar numbers.
Q: What is India Stack?
A: India Stack is a set of open APIs and digital public infrastructure (Aadhaar, e-KYC, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC, etc.) that enables paperless, cashless and presence-less service delivery.
Q: What is e-KYC?
A: e-KYC is electronic Know Your Customer verification, which uses Aadhaar-based authentication to verify a customer's identity instantly for opening accounts and services.
Q: What is BHIM?
A: BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) is a UPI-based mobile app launched by NPCI in 2016 for easy digital payments and instant money transfer.
Q: What is RuPay and which organisation developed it?
A: RuPay is India's indigenous card payment network developed by NPCI and launched in 2012, providing an alternative to Visa and Mastercard.
Q: What is DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer)?
A: DBT is a scheme under which government subsidies and benefits are transferred directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries, eliminating middlemen.
Q: When was the Direct Benefit Transfer scheme launched?
A: The DBT scheme was launched on 1 January 2013 by the Government of India.
Q: What is the JAM trinity?
A: JAM trinity refers to the combination of Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and Mobile numbers, which together enable targeted delivery of subsidies through DBT.
Q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?
A: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 as a national mission for financial inclusion.
Q: What is DigiLocker?
A: DigiLocker is a cloud-based platform under Digital India where citizens can store, access and share their documents in digital form, issued by government agencies.
Q: Which ministry launched the DigiLocker platform?
A: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launched DigiLocker.
Q: How many pillars does the Digital India programme have?
A: The Digital India programme is built on nine pillars of growth areas.
Q: What is CERT-In?
A: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) is the national nodal agency responsible for cyber security, cyber incident response and cyber crisis management in India.
Q: Which is the nodal agency for cyber security in India?
A: CERT-In under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is the nodal agency for cyber security in India.
Q: What role does NPCI play in the UPI system?
A: NPCI operates and develops the UPI platform, facilitating interoperability between different banks and payment apps.
Q: Which of the following is a popular UPI-based payment app in India: PhonePe, Western Union, SWIFT?
A: PhonePe is a popular UPI-based payment app in India; Western Union and SWIFT are international money transfer systems, not UPI apps.
Q: What is a fintech company?
A: A fintech (financial technology) company uses technology to provide financial services such as payments, lending, wealth management and insurance.
Q: Which is the parent company of the fintech Paytm?
A: Paytm is operated by One97 Communications Ltd, a leading Indian fintech company.
Q: What is digital literacy?
A: Digital literacy is the ability to use digital technologies, devices and the internet to access information, communicate and conduct financial transactions.
Q: Which scheme was launched in 2017 to make rural citizens digitally literate?
A: The Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) was launched in 2017 to make rural citizens digitally literate.
Q: What is cryptocurrency?
A: Cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency that uses cryptography for security and operates on a decentralised network such as blockchain.
Q: Is Bitcoin considered legal tender in India?
A: No, Bitcoin is not legal tender in India; the RBI has not granted it legal tender status and has cautioned about its risks.
Q: What is the CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency) launched by RBI and when was its pilot started?
A: CBDC, called the Digital Rupee (e₹), is the RBI's digital currency; its pilot was launched in 2022.
Q: What is IMPS and when was it launched?
A: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) is a 24x7 instant interbank money transfer service launched by NPCI in 2010.
Q: Which institution regulates digital payment systems like UPI in India?
A: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates digital payment systems in India, while NPCI operates the UPI platform.

### Foreign Trade, FDI/FPI & International Bodies | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/foreign-trade-fdi-wto-imf-wb/
Summary: Important questions on foreign trade, FDI/FPI and international economic bodies for Indian economy competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
A: The WTO was established in 1995 as the successor to GATT.
Q: GATT was signed in which year?
A: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) was signed in 1947.
Q: Which principle of the WTO ensures that member countries grant equal treatment to all trading partners?
A: The Most Favoured Nation (MFN) principle ensures equal treatment for all trading partners.
Q: What is the headquarters of the WTO?
A: The WTO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland.
Q: Who established the IMF and World Bank at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944?
A: The IMF and the World Bank were established by 44 allied nations at the Bretton Woods Conference in July 1944.
Q: Which organization of the World Bank Group provides loans to private sector enterprises in developing countries?
A: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) provides loans to the private sector.
Q: Which institution of the World Bank Group provides concessional loans to the poorest countries?
A: The International Development Association (IDA) provides concessional loans to the poorest countries.
Q: What is the full form of IMF?
A: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund.
Q: Which international body provides temporary financial assistance to member countries facing BoP problems?
A: The IMF provides temporary financial assistance to member countries facing balance of payments problems.
Q: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established in which year?
A: The ADB was established in 1966 with headquarters in Manila, Philippines.
Q: Which new development bank was set up by the BRICS countries?
A: The New Development Bank (NDB) was set up by the BRICS countries in 2014.
Q: What is the headquarters of the New Development Bank (NDB)?
A: The NDB headquarters is in Shanghai, China.
Q: SAARC was founded in which year?
A: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in 1985.
Q: What is the difference between FDI and FPI?
A: FDI is direct investment in physical assets with management control, while FPI is portfolio investment in financial assets without management control.
Q: Which sector allows 100% FDI through the automatic route?
A: Many sectors such as single-brand retail, renewable energy and most manufacturing allow 100% FDI through the automatic route.
Q: In FDI policy, what is the 'automatic route'?
A: Under the automatic route, FDI is allowed without prior approval of the government or the RBI.
Q: In FDI policy, what is the 'approval route'?
A: Under the approval route, FDI requires prior approval from the government, usually through the concerned ministry.
Q: Which nodal agency is responsible for FDI policy formulation in India?
A: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for FDI policy.
Q: DPIIT comes under which ministry?
A: DPIIT functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Q: In which year was the 'Make in India' initiative launched?
A: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on 25 September 2014.
Q: The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is valid for which period?
A: The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is valid from 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2028.
Q: What is the major export destination of India as per recent trade data?
A: The United States has been India's largest export destination in recent years.
Q: Which country is the largest source of FDI inflows into India in recent years?
A: Singapore, followed by Mauritius and the USA, has been a major source of FDI inflows into India in recent years.
Q: What is a Free Trade Agreement (FTA)?
A: An FTA is an agreement between countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs on trade in goods and services.
Q: What is the difference between FTA and PTA?
A: A PTA (Preferential Trade Agreement) covers a limited set of goods with partial tariff cuts, while an FTA covers a wider range of goods and services with deeper liberalisation.
Q: Which of the following is a portfolio investment — FDI, FPI, ECB, or Export earnings?
A: FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment) is portfolio investment in financial assets.
Q: Which body regulates FPI in India?
A: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates Foreign Portfolio Investment.
Q: What is the FDI limit in the defence sector in India?
A: FDI up to 74% is allowed in the defence sector through the automatic route.
Q: What is the FDI limit in the insurance sector in India?
A: FDI up to 74% is allowed in the insurance sector in India.
Q: In which year was India admitted as a founding member of the WTO?
A: India was a founding member of the WTO when it came into effect on 1 January 1995.
Q: Which commodity is India's largest agricultural export?
A: Basmati rice and marine products are among India's largest agricultural exports.
Q: Which agreement replaced GATT as the global trade regulator?
A: The Marrakesh Agreement established the WTO in 1995, which replaced GATT.
Q: What is the major import item of India by value?
A: Crude petroleum is India's largest import item by value.
Q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the BRICS group?
A: The BRICS group consists of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa; countries like Japan are not members.
Q: Which international body adjudicates trade disputes between member countries?
A: The WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) adjudicates trade disputes between member countries.

### Green Revolution & Farm Subsidies | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/economics/indian-economy-sec/green-revolution-msp-pds-subsidies/
Summary: Important questions on the Green Revolution and farm subsidies for Indian economy competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: In which decade did the Green Revolution take place in India?
A: The Green Revolution in India took place mainly in the late 1960s.
Q: Who is known as the father of the Green Revolution?
A: Norman Borlaug, an American agronomist, is known as the father of the Green Revolution.
Q: Who is called the father of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is called the father of the Green Revolution in India.
Q: Which varieties of seeds were the main instrument of the Green Revolution?
A: High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds were the main instrument of the Green Revolution.
Q: Norman Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
A: Norman Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contributions to the Green Revolution.
Q: Which two states were the primary beneficiaries of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Punjab and Haryana were the primary beneficiaries of the Green Revolution in India.
Q: Which of the following was a key component of the Green Revolution package?
A: High yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation were key components of the Green Revolution package.
Q: Which revolution in India was aimed at increasing milk production?
A: The White Revolution, led by Dr. Verghese Kurien under Operation Flood, was aimed at increasing milk production.
Q: What is the Minimum Support Price (MSP)?
A: MSP is the minimum price announced by the government at which it purchases farmers' crops, protecting them from price fluctuations.
Q: Which agency is responsible for procuring food grains at MSP in India?
A: The Food Corporation of India (FCI), along with state agencies, procures food grains at MSP.
Q: On whose recommendation is the MSP fixed by the government of India?
A: MSP is fixed on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
Q: Which of the following is NOT a statutory or notified MSP crop?
A: Tea and vegetables are not notified MSP crops; MSP covers cereals, pulses, oilseeds, cotton, sugarcane and some commercial crops.
Q: What does PDS stand for in the context of food distribution in India?
A: PDS stands for the Public Distribution System, through which food grains and essential commodities are distributed at subsidised rates.
Q: Which system was introduced in India for the targeted distribution of food grains to the poor?
A: The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) was introduced in 1997 for the distribution of food grains to the poor at subsidised prices.
Q: The stock of food grains maintained by the government for emergency needs is called what?
A: The stock of food grains maintained by the government for emergency needs is called the buffer stock.
Q: In which year was the Food Corporation of India (FCI) established?
A: The Food Corporation of India was established in 1965.
Q: Which Act provides a legal right to subsidised food grains to eligible households in India?
A: The National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 provides a legal right to subsidised food grains to eligible households.
Q: As per the NFSA 2013, how much food grain is entitled to a priority household per person per month?
A: As per NFSA 2013, each member of a priority household is entitled to 5 kg of food grain per person per month at subsidised prices.
Q: What is the subsidised issue price of wheat under the NFSA 2013?
A: Under the NFSA 2013, the issue price of wheat is 2 rupees per kg.
Q: What is the subsidised issue price of rice under the NFSA 2013?
A: Under the NFSA 2013, the issue price of rice is 3 rupees per kg.
Q: Which of the following is a major subsidy given by the Government of India to farmers?
A: Fertiliser subsidy, food subsidy, power subsidy and irrigation subsidy are major subsidies provided to farmers in India.
Q: The fertiliser subsidy in India is mainly provided on which fertilisers?
A: The fertiliser subsidy in India is mainly provided on urea, DAP, potash and complex fertilisers, with urea being the most heavily subsidised.
Q: Which scheme provides income support of 6000 rupees per year to small and marginal farmers?
A: The PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) scheme provides 6000 rupees per year to eligible small and marginal farmers in three instalments.
Q: In which year was the PM-KISAN scheme launched?
A: The PM-KISAN scheme was launched in February 2019.
Q: What is meant by 'Evergreen Revolution'?
A: The Evergreen Revolution refers to a concept of sustainable agriculture that aims to increase productivity without harming the environment, as advocated by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan.
Q: Which of the following is a major drawback of the Green Revolution in India?
A: Regional disparity, overuse of chemicals, groundwater depletion and neglect of pulses and oilseeds are major drawbacks of the Green Revolution.
Q: The concept of the 'second Green Revolution' in India emphasizes which of the following?
A: The second Green Revolution emphasises sustainable agriculture, focus on dryland and rain-fed farming, pulses, oilseeds and balanced use of inputs.
Q: Which committee recommended that MSP should be at least 50 percent above the cost of production (A2+FL)?
A: The National Commission on Farmers headed by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan recommended that MSP should be at least 50 percent above the cost of production.
Q: What is the main objective of the buffer stock policy in India?
A: The buffer stock policy aims to maintain food security by ensuring availability of food grains for PDS and for stabilising prices during shortages.
Q: Which of the following is the largest component of the food subsidy bill of the Government of India?
A: The difference between the MSP/cost of procurement and the subsidised issue price under the NFSA is the largest component of the food subsidy bill.
Q: Which of the following programmes was started for the distribution of food to the poorest households at highly subsidised rates?
A: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) provides 35 kg of food grains per family per month at highly subsidised rates to the poorest households.
Q: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana, the issue price of wheat and rice is what?
A: Under AAY, wheat is issued at 2 rupees per kg and rice at 3 rupees per kg, matching the NFSA issue prices.
Q: Which of the following states has the highest coverage of the Public Distribution System in terms of ration card holders?
A: Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of ration card holders, followed by West Bengal and Bihar.
Q: What is the primary aim of the 'One Nation One Ration Card' scheme?
A: The One Nation One Ration Card scheme enables migrant workers and beneficiaries to access their food grains from any fair price shop across the country.
Q: Which of the following is TRUE about the Green Revolution?
A: The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains, especially in wheat, within a short span of time.

A: Yes. Every question and answer in this topic is bilingual, so you can practise in Assamese and English.
