### Legal Officers: Attorney General and Advocate General | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/gk/polity/union-state-governance-sec/legal-officers-attorney-general-advocate-general/
Summary: Important questions on the Attorney General of India and the Advocate General of the state for Assam competitive exams. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: Who is the highest law officer of the Government of India?
A: The Attorney General of India.
Q: Under which Article is the office of the Attorney General of India provided?
A: Article 76.
Q: Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
A: The President of India.
Q: What is the qualification required to become the Attorney General of India?
A: He must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court.
Q: For how long does the Attorney General of India hold office?
A: He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Q: Who is the highest law officer of a state?
A: The Advocate General of the state.
Q: Under which Article is the office of the Advocate General of a state provided?
A: Article 165.
Q: Who appoints the Advocate General of a state?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: What is the qualification required to become the Advocate General of a state?
A: He must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
Q: For how long does the Advocate General hold office?
A: He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
Q: What is the main function of the Attorney General of India?
A: To advise the Government of India on legal matters referred to him.
Q: What is the main function of the Advocate General of a state?
A: To advise the Government of the state on legal matters referred to him.
Q: Does the Attorney General have the right to vote in the Parliament?
A: No, he does not have the right to vote.
Q: Does the Attorney General have the right to speak in the Parliament?
A: Yes, he has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses.
Q: In which courts can the Attorney General of India appear?
A: He can appear in all courts of India, including the Supreme Court.
Q: Is the Attorney General a member of the Parliament?
A: No, he is not a member of the Parliament, but he can speak in it.
Q: What is the difference between the Attorney General and the Advocate General?
A: The Attorney General is the law officer of the Union, while the Advocate General is the law officer of a state.
Q: Can the Attorney General of India be removed?
A: Yes, he can be removed by the President at any time.
Q: Does the Attorney General receive a fixed salary as per the Constitution?
A: No, his remuneration is fixed by the President.
Q: Who fixes the remuneration of the Advocate General?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: What is the status of the Attorney General in the official hierarchy?
A: He is the highest law officer and ranks above all other law officers of the Union.
Q: Which law officer represents the Union Government in the Supreme Court?
A: The Attorney General of India.
Q: Which law officer represents the state government in the High Court?
A: The Advocate General of the state.
Q: What happens to the Attorney General when the Council of Ministers resigns?
A: He does not automatically resign; he can continue if the new government so desires.
Q: What is the term of office of the Attorney General of India?
A: There is no fixed term; he holds office during the pleasure of the President.

A: The Rajya Sabha.
Q: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha?
A: 552 members (530 from states, 20 from Union Territories and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians).
Q: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
A: 250 members (238 elected and 12 nominated by the President).
Q: For how long is the Lok Sabha elected?
A: Five years.
Q: Is the Rajya Sabha a permanent house?
A: Yes, it is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.
Q: Who presides over the meetings of the Lok Sabha?
A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
A: The Vice-President of India.
Q: Who elects the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
A: The members of the Lok Sabha elect the Speaker from among themselves.
Q: Which house of Parliament can introduce a Money Bill?
A: Only the Lok Sabha can introduce a Money Bill.
Q: Who certifies a Money Bill?
A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Q: What is the minimum age for becoming a member of the Lok Sabha?
A: 25 years.
Q: What is the minimum age for becoming a member of the Rajya Sabha?
A: 30 years.
Q: What is the State Legislature composed of?
A: The Governor and the State Legislature which may have one or two houses.
Q: What is the lower house of the State Legislature called?
A: Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly).
Q: What is the upper house of the State Legislature called?
A: Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council).
Q: Which states have a bicameral State Legislature?
A: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Q: Who presides over the meetings of the Vidhan Sabha?
A: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
Q: What is the normal term of the Legislative Assembly?
A: Five years.
Q: What is the maximum strength of a State Legislative Assembly?
A: 500 members.
Q: What is the minimum strength of a State Legislative Assembly?
A: 60 members.
Q: What is the minimum age for becoming a member of the Legislative Assembly?
A: 25 years.
Q: Who appoints the Speaker pro tem of the Legislative Assembly?
A: The Governor of the state.
Q: How many members of the Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor?
A: One-sixth of the total members are nominated by the Governor from amongst persons having special knowledge or practical experience.

Q: Find the remainder when the polynomial 2x + 3 is divided by (x − 2).
A: By remainder theorem, remainder = f(divisor).,f(x) = 2x + 3,f(2) = 2(2) + 3 = 4 + 3 = 7,Answer: 7
Q: Find the remainder when the polynomial 3x + 2 is divided by (x − 3).
A: By remainder theorem, remainder = f(divisor).,f(x) = 3x + 2,f(3) = 3(3) + 2 = 9 + 2 = 11,Answer: 11
Q: Find the remainder when the polynomial 2x + 4 is divided by (x − 1).

Q: If x + (1/x) = 2, find the value of x² + (1/x²).
A: Given x + 1/x = 2.,Square both sides: (x + 1/x)² = 2² = 4,x² + 1/x² + 2 = 4,x² + 1/x² = 4 − 2 = 2,Answer: 2
Q: If x + (1/x) = 3, find the value of x² + (1/x²).

Q: If x + (1/x) = 4, find the value of x² + (1/x²).

Q: Which of the following can be the sides of a triangle?

### Average | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/arithmetic/average/
Summary: 42 most important Average questions with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: Find the average of 6, 11, 13, 16 and 24.
A: Formula: Average = Sum of numbers / Number of numbers.,Step 1: Sum = 6 + 11 + 13 + 16 + 24 = 70,Step 2: Number of numbers = 5,Step 3: Average = 70/5 = 14,Answer: (a) 14
Q: Find the average of 25, 30, 35, 40 and 45.
A: Formula: Average = Sum of numbers / Count.,Step 1: Sum = 25 + 30 + 35 + 40 + 45 = 175,Step 2: Count = 5,Step 3: Average = 175/5 = 35,Answer: (c) 35
Q: What is the average of the first 10 odd numbers?
A: Formula: Average of first n odd numbers = n.,Step 1: Here n = 10,Step 2: Average = 10,Answer: (b) 10
Q: The average weight of 5 persons is 42 kg. Find their total weight.
A: Formula: Total = Average × Number of persons.,Step 1: Total weight = 42 × 5,Step 2: = 210 kg,Answer: (d) 210 kg
Q: The average marks of 20 students is 55. Later it was found that the marks of one student were wrongly entered as 82 instead of 62. Find the correct average.
A: Formula: Correct total = Old total − wrong entry + correct entry.,Step 1: Old total = 20 × 55 = 1100,Step 2: Correct total = 1100 − 82 + 62 = 1080,Step 3: Correct average = 1080/20 = 54,Answer: (a) 54
Q: The average age of 4 persons is 25 years. When a new person joins, the average becomes 27 years. Find the age of the new person.
A: Formula: New person's age = New total − Old total.,Step 1: Old total = 4 × 25 = 100,Step 2: New total = 5 × 27 = 135,Step 3: New person's age = 135 − 100 = 35 years,Answer: (b) 35 years
Q: The average age of 6 persons is 30 years. One person aged 40 years leaves the group. Find the new average age.
A: Formula: New average = (Old total − departed person's age) / New count.,Step 1: Old total = 6 × 30 = 180,Step 2: New total = 180 − 40 = 140,Step 3: New average = 140/5 = 28 years,Answer: (d) 28 years
Q: In a class of 30 boys and 20 girls, the average weight of boys is 40 kg and of girls is 35 kg. Find the average weight of the whole class.
A: Formula: Combined average = (n1×a1 + n2×a2) / (n1 + n2).,Step 1: Total weight = 30×40 + 20×35 = 1200 + 700 = 1900 kg,Step 2: Total students = 30 + 20 = 50,Step 3: Average = 1900/50 = 38 kg,Answer: (c) 38 kg
Q: A man travels from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. Find his average speed for the whole journey.
A: Formula: Average speed = 2xy / (x + y) when distances are equal.,Step 1: x = 60, y = 40,Step 2: Average speed = 2×60×40 / (60+40) = 4800/100,Step 3: = 48 km/h,Answer: (a) 48 km/h
Q: The average of 5 numbers is 40. Later it was found that one number 28 was misread as 48. Find the correct average.
A: Formula: Correct average = (Sum − misread value + actual value) / Count.,Step 1: Sum = 5 × 40 = 200,Step 2: Correct sum = 200 − 48 + 28 = 180,Step 3: Correct average = 180/5 = 36,Answer: (b) 36
Q: The average of 5 numbers is 28. Four of them are 20, 24, 32 and 36. Find the fifth number.
A: Formula: Missing number = Total sum − Sum of known numbers.,Step 1: Total sum = 5 × 28 = 140,Step 2: Sum of four numbers = 20 + 24 + 32 + 36 = 112,Step 3: Fifth number = 140 − 112 = 28,Answer: (c) 28
Q: A bowler has taken 12 wickets at an average of 25 runs per wicket. In the next match he conceded 30 runs for 3 wickets. Find his new average.
A: Formula: New average = (Total runs before + runs in match) / (Total wickets before + wickets in match).,Step 1: Runs before = 12 × 25 = 300,Step 2: Total runs = 300 + 30 = 330, Total wickets = 12 + 3 = 15,Step 3: New average = 330/15 = 22 runs per wicket,Answer: (d) 22 runs/wicket
Q: What is the average of the first 8 even numbers?
A: Formula: Sum of first n even numbers = n(n+1).,Step 1: n = 8, Sum = 8 × 9 = 72,Step 2: Average = 72/8 = 9,Answer: (a) 9
Q: Section A has 40 students with an average of 60 marks and Section B has 60 students with an average of 50 marks. Find the average of both sections combined.
A: Formula: Combined average = (n1×a1 + n2×a2) / (n1 + n2).,Step 1: Total marks = 40×60 + 60×50 = 2400 + 3000 = 5400,Step 2: Total students = 40 + 60 = 100,Step 3: Average = 5400/100 = 54,Answer: (b) 54
Q: The average income of a family increased by Rs 2000 each year for 5 years. If the average income at the end of 5 years is Rs 15000, what was the average income 5 years ago?
A: Formula: Earlier average = Present average − (increase per year × number of years).,Step 1: Total increase = 2000 × 5 = 10000,Step 2: Average 5 years ago = 15000 − 10000 = Rs 5000,Answer: (c) Rs 5000
Q: The average of 9 consecutive natural numbers is 45. Find the largest number.
A: Formula: For consecutive numbers, average = middle number.,Step 1: Middle number (5th) = 45, so first number = 45 − 4 = 41,Step 2: Largest number = 41 + 8 = 49,Answer: (d) 49
Q: The average age of 30 students in a class is 15 years. If the average age of 2/3 of the students is 14 years, find the average age of the remaining 10 students.
A: Formula: Remaining group average = (Total age − group age) / Remaining count.,Step 1: Total age = 30 × 15 = 450,Step 2: Age of 2/3 students = 20 × 14 = 280,Step 3: Remaining average = (450 − 280)/10 = 170/10 = 17 years,Answer: (a) 17 years
Q: The average age of a family of 5 members is 24 years. If the youngest member is 8 years old, find the average age of the remaining 4 members.
A: Formula: Average of remaining = (Total − youngest's age) / Remaining count.,Step 1: Total age = 5 × 24 = 120,Step 2: Remaining total = 120 − 8 = 112,Step 3: Average = 112/4 = 28 years,Answer: (b) 28 years
Q: A student scores an average of 70 marks in 6 subjects. How many marks must he score in the 7th subject to raise his average to 75?
A: Formula: Required marks = New total − Old total.,Step 1: Old total = 6 × 70 = 420,Step 2: New total = 7 × 75 = 525,Step 3: Marks in 7th subject = 525 − 420 = 105,Answer: (c) 105
Q: The average weight of 30 men is 65 kg and of 20 women is 55 kg. Find the average weight of the whole group.
A: Formula: Combined average = (n1×a1 + n2×a2) / (n1 + n2).,Step 1: Total weight = 30×65 + 20×55 = 1950 + 1100 = 3050 kg,Step 2: Total persons = 30 + 20 = 50,Step 3: Average = 3050/50 = 61 kg,Answer: (d) 61 kg
Q: A batsman has an average of 45 runs in 8 innings. How many runs must he score in the next innings to raise his average to 50?
A: Formula: Required runs = New total − Old total.,Step 1: Old total = 8 × 45 = 360,Step 2: New total (9 innings) = 9 × 50 = 450,Step 3: Runs needed = 450 − 360 = 90,Answer: (a) 90
Q: The average age of a father and mother is 30 years. After the birth of a child, the average age of the family becomes 22 years. Find the age of the child.
A: Formula: Child's age = Family total − Parents' total.,Step 1: Parents' total = 2 × 30 = 60,Step 2: Family total = 3 × 22 = 66,Step 3: Child's age = 66 − 60 = 6 years,Answer: (b) 6 years
Q: A man travels at 50 km/h for 2 hours and then at 70 km/h for 3 hours. Find his average speed for the whole journey.
A: Formula: Average speed = Total distance / Total time.,Step 1: Distance1 = 50 × 2 = 100 km, Distance2 = 70 × 3 = 210 km,Step 2: Total distance = 310 km, Total time = 5 h,Step 3: Average speed = 310/5 = 62 km/h,Answer: (c) 62 km/h
Q: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 26. Find the smallest number.
A: Formula: For consecutive even numbers, average = middle number.,Step 1: Middle number (3rd) = 26,Step 2: Smallest = 26 − 4 = 22,Answer: (d) 22
Q: Find the average of all numbers from 1 to 100.
A: Formula: Average of 1 to n = (n + 1)/2.,Step 1: n = 100,Step 2: Average = (100 + 1)/2 = 50.5,Answer: (a) 50.5
Q: The average weight of 10 students is 42 kg. The weight of one student was wrongly recorded as 46 kg instead of 36 kg. Find the correct average.
A: Formula: Correct average = (Old sum − wrong value + correct value) / Count.,Step 1: Old sum = 10 × 42 = 420,Step 2: Correct sum = 420 − 46 + 36 = 410,Step 3: Correct average = 410/10 = 41 kg,Answer: (b) 41 kg
Q: The average of 5 numbers is 18. If each number is multiplied by 3, what will be the new average?
A: Formula: If each number is multiplied by k, the average is also multiplied by k.,Step 1: Original average = 18, k = 3,Step 2: New average = 18 × 3 = 54,Answer: (c) 54
Q: The average age of 8 persons is 25 years. A person aged 40 years is replaced by a new person aged 16 years. Find the new average.
A: Formula: New average = (Old total − replaced age + new age) / Count.,Step 1: Old total = 8 × 25 = 200,Step 2: New total = 200 − 40 + 16 = 176,Step 3: New average = 176/8 = 22 years,Answer: (d) 22 years
Q: The average daily expenditure of a family in a week is Rs 250. What is the total expenditure of the week?
A: Formula: Total = Average × Number of days.,Step 1: Total expenditure = 250 × 7,Step 2: = Rs 1750,Answer: (a) Rs 1750
Q: A batsman has an average of 40 runs in 15 innings. After the next innings his average drops to 38. How many runs did he score in the 16th innings?
A: Formula: Runs in nth innings = New total − Old total.,Step 1: Old total = 15 × 40 = 600,Step 2: New total = 16 × 38 = 608,Step 3: Runs in 16th innings = 608 − 600 = 8,Answer: (b) 8
Q: The average of 4 numbers is 20. If 0 is also included, what will be the new average?
A: Formula: New average = (Old sum + 0) / (Count + 1).,Step 1: Old sum = 4 × 20 = 80,Step 2: New average = 80/5 = 16,Answer: (c) 16
Q: The average of 6 numbers is 35. Five of them are 28, 32, 36, 40 and 44. Find the sixth number.
A: Formula: Missing number = Total sum − Sum of known numbers.,Step 1: Total sum = 6 × 35 = 210,Step 2: Sum of five = 28 + 32 + 36 + 40 + 44 = 180,Step 3: Sixth number = 210 − 180 = 30,Answer: (d) 30
Q: Find the average of the first 12 multiples of 5.
A: Formula: Sum of first n multiples of k = k × n(n+1)/2.,Step 1: Sum = 5 × 12×13/2 = 5 × 78 = 390,Step 2: Average = 390/12 = 32.5,Answer: (a) 32.5
Q: The average age of 4 students is 25 years. A new student aged 30 joins them. Find the new average age.
A: Formula: New average = (Old total + new member's age) / (Old count + 1).,Step 1: Old total = 4 × 25 = 100,Step 2: New total = 100 + 30 = 130,Step 3: New average = 130/5 = 26 years,Answer: (b) 26 years
Q: In a class, 2/3 of the students scored an average of 45 marks and 1/3 scored an average of 60 marks. Find the average marks of the whole class.
A: Formula: Overall average = (w1×a1 + w2×a2) / (w1 + w2).,Step 1: Weights are 2 and 1 (ratio 2:1),Step 2: Overall average = (2×45 + 1×60)/3 = (90 + 60)/3,Step 3: = 150/3 = 50,Answer: (c) 50
Q: Find the average of the first 5 prime numbers.
A: Formula: Average = Sum of primes / Count.,Step 1: First five primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11,Step 2: Sum = 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 11 = 28,Step 3: Average = 28/5 = 5.6,Answer: (d) 5.6
Q: The average of two numbers is 15. If one of them is 9, find the other number.
A: Formula: Other number = 2 × Average − Given number.,Step 1: Sum = 2 × 15 = 30,Step 2: Other number = 30 − 9 = 21,Answer: (a) 21
Q: The average height of 5 boys is 150 cm. If the average height of 4 of them is 148 cm, find the height of the fifth boy.
A: Formula: Missing height = Total − Sum of the rest.,Step 1: Total = 5 × 150 = 750 cm,Step 2: Sum of 4 boys = 4 × 148 = 592 cm,Step 3: Fifth boy's height = 750 − 592 = 158 cm,Answer: (b) 158 cm
Q: The present average age of a family of 4 members is 30 years. What will be the average age of the family after 5 years?
A: Formula: Average after t years = Present average + t.,Step 1: Present average = 30 years,Step 2: After 5 years, average = 30 + 5 = 35 years,Answer: (c) 35 years
Q: The average weight of 10 boys is 45 kg. A boy weighing 40 kg leaves and a new boy weighing 50 kg joins. Find the new average weight.
A: Formula: New average = (Old total − leaving weight + joining weight) / Count.,Step 1: Old total = 10 × 45 = 450 kg,Step 2: New total = 450 − 40 + 50 = 460 kg,Step 3: New average = 460/10 = 46 kg,Answer: (d) 46 kg
Q: Find the average of 3, 7, 11, 15 and 19.
A: Formula: Average = Sum of numbers / Count.,Step 1: Sum = 3 + 7 + 11 + 15 + 19 = 55,Step 2: Count = 5,Step 3: Average = 55/5 = 11,Answer: (a) 11
Q: In an office, 4 peons have an average salary of Rs 3000, 6 clerks of Rs 5000 and 8 officers of Rs 6000. Find the average salary of all the employees.
A: Formula: Overall average = Total of all groups / Total number.,Step 1: Total = 4×3000 + 6×5000 + 8×6000 = 12000 + 30000 + 48000 = 90000,Step 2: Total persons = 4 + 6 + 8 = 18,Step 3: Average = 90000/18 = Rs 5000,Answer: (b) Rs 5000

### Boats and Streams | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/arithmetic/boats-and-streams/
Summary: 42 most important Boats and Streams questions with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: A boat can travel at 10 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, find the speed of the boat downstream.
A: Formula: Downstream speed = Boat speed + Stream speed.,Step 1: D = 10 + 2,Step 2: D = 12 km/h,Answer: (a) 12 km/h
Q: A boat can travel at 12 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, find the speed of the boat upstream.
A: Formula: Upstream speed = Boat speed − Stream speed.,Step 1: U = 12 − 4,Step 2: U = 8 km/h,Answer: (b) 8 km/h
Q: A boat moves at 15 km/h downstream. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 45 km?
A: Formula: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.,Step 1: Time = 45 ÷ 15,Step 2: Time = 3 hours,Answer: (c) 3 hours
Q: A boat moves at 6 km/h upstream. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 30 km?
A: Formula: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.,Step 1: Time = 30 ÷ 6,Step 2: Time = 5 hours,Answer: (d) 5 hours
Q: A boat travels at 8 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How far will it go downstream in 4 hours?
A: Formula: Distance = Downstream speed × Time.,Step 1: D = 8 + 2 = 10 km/h,Step 2: Distance = 10 × 4,Step 3: = 40 km,Answer: (a) 40 km
Q: A boat goes 14 km/h downstream and 6 km/h upstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
A: Formula: Boat speed = (D + U) ÷ 2.,Step 1: Boat speed = (14 + 6) ÷ 2,Step 2: = 20 ÷ 2,Step 3: = 10 km/h,Answer: (b) 10 km/h
Q: A boat goes 12 km/h downstream and 8 km/h upstream. Find the speed of the stream.
A: Formula: Stream speed = (D − U) ÷ 2.,Step 1: Stream speed = (12 − 8) ÷ 2,Step 2: = 4 ÷ 2,Step 3: = 2 km/h,Answer: (c) 2 km/h
Q: A boat travels at 10 km/h in still water and the stream flows at 2 km/h. Find the ratio of the time taken to go upstream to the time taken to go downstream for the same distance.
A: Formula: Time ratio (up:down) = D : U for the same distance.,Step 1: U = 10 − 2 = 8, D = 10 + 2 = 12,Step 2: Time ratio = 12 : 8,Step 3: = 3 : 2,Answer: (d) 3:2
Q: A boat goes downstream in 2 hours and upstream in 3 hours for the same distance. The boat can travel at 15 km/h in still water. Find the speed of the stream.
A: Formula: Distance is the same, so D × 2 = U × 3.,Step 1: (15 + s) × 2 = (15 − s) × 3,Step 2: 30 + 2s = 45 − 3s → 5s = 15,Step 3: s = 3 km/h,Answer: (a) 3 km/h
Q: A boat takes 3 hours to go upstream and 2 hours to come back downstream over the same distance. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.
A: Formula: D × 2 = U × 3 for the same distance.,Step 1: 2(b + s) = 3(b − s),Step 2: 2b + 2s = 3b − 3s → b = 5s,Step 3: b : s = 5 : 1,Answer: (b) 5:1
Q: A boat goes downstream at a speed of 12 km/h. For the same distance it takes twice as much time going upstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
A: Formula: Upstream speed = D ÷ 2 (twice the time).,Step 1: U = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 km/h,Step 2: Boat speed = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2,Step 3: = 9 km/h,Answer: (c) 9 km/h
Q: A man can row at 12 km/h in still water. He takes 3 times as long to row upstream as downstream. Find the speed of the stream.
A: Formula: Time upstream = 3 × time downstream → U = D ÷ 3.,Step 1: 12 − s = (12 + s) ÷ 3,Step 2: 36 − 3s = 12 + s → 4s = 24,Step 3: s = 6 km/h,Answer: (d) 6 km/h
Q: A boat travels at 8 km/h downstream and 4 km/h upstream. If the difference between the time taken to go upstream and downstream for the same distance is 2 hours, find the distance.
A: Formula: (d ÷ U) − (d ÷ D) = time difference.,Step 1: d/4 − d/8 = 2,Step 2: d/8 = 2,Step 3: d = 16 km,Answer: (a) 16 km
Q: A boat goes 15 km/h downstream and 9 km/h upstream. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.
A: Formula: Boat = (D + U) ÷ 2, Stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.,Step 1: Boat = (15 + 9) ÷ 2 = 12, Stream = (15 − 9) ÷ 2 = 3,Step 2: Ratio = 12 : 3,Step 3: = 4 : 1,Answer: (b) 4:1
Q: A boat goes 10 km/h downstream and 6 km/h upstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water.

Q: A boat can travel at 9 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, find the speed of the boat downstream.

### LCM and HCF | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/arithmetic/lcm-and-hcf/
Summary: 50 most important LCM and HCF questions with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: Find the LCM of 12 and 18.
A: Rule: Prime factorize each number.,Step 1: 12 = 2² × 3,Step 2: 18 = 2 × 3²,Step 3: Take highest powers: 2², 3²,Step 4: LCM = 4 × 9 = 36,Answer: (a) 36
Q: Find the HCF of 24 and 36.
A: Rule: Prime factorize and take common factors.,Step 1: 24 = 2³ × 3,Step 2: 36 = 2² × 3²,Step 3: Common = 2² × 3,Step 4: HCF = 4 × 3 = 12,Answer: (b) 12
Q: Find the LCM of 8, 12 and 16.
A: Step 1: 8 = 2³; 12 = 2² × 3; 16 = 2⁴,Step 2: Highest powers: 2⁴, 3¹,Step 3: LCM = 16 × 3 = 48,Answer: (c) 48
Q: Find the HCF of 48, 72 and 120.
A: Step 1: 48 = 2⁴ × 3,Step 2: 72 = 2³ × 3²,Step 3: 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5,Step 4: Common = 2³ × 3 = 24,Answer: (d) 24
Q: The product of two numbers is 2160 and their HCF is 12. Find their LCM.
A: Formula: Product = HCF × LCM.,Step 1: 2160 = 12 × LCM,Step 2: LCM = 2160 ÷ 12 = 180,Answer: (a) 180
Q: Find the smallest number which is exactly divisible by 6, 9 and 15.
A: Concept: Required number = LCM of 6, 9, 15.,Step 1: 6 = 2 × 3; 9 = 3²; 15 = 3 × 5,Step 2: Highest powers: 2, 3², 5,Step 3: LCM = 2 × 9 × 5 = 90,Answer: (b) 90
Q: Find the greatest number which divides 60, 90 and 120 exactly.
A: Concept: The greatest such number is the HCF.,Step 1: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5,Step 2: 90 = 2 × 3² × 5,Step 3: 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5,Step 4: Common factors = 2 × 3 × 5 = 30,Answer: (c) 30
Q: The LCM of two numbers is 120 and their HCF is 8. One number is 40. Find the other.
A: Formula: Product = HCF × LCM = a × b.,Step 1: a × b = 8 × 120 = 960,Step 2: 40 × b = 960 → b = 960 ÷ 40,Step 3: b = 24,Answer: (d) 24
Q: Find the HCF of 0.36 and 0.48.
A: Method: Convert to fractions and find HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.,Step 1: 0.36 = 36/100; 0.48 = 48/100,Step 2: HCF of 36 and 48 = 12,Step 3: HCF = 12/100 = 0.12,Answer: (a) 0.12
Q: Find the smallest number which when divided by 4, 6 and 8 leaves remainder 2 in each case.
A: Concept: Number = LCM(4, 6, 8) + 2.,Step 1: LCM of 4, 6, 8 = 24,Step 2: Number = 24 + 2 = 26,Answer: (b) 26
Q: Three bells ring at intervals of 12, 18 and 30 seconds. After how many seconds will they ring together again?
A: Concept: Time after which they ring together = LCM.,Step 1: 12 = 2² × 3; 18 = 2 × 3²; 30 = 2 × 3 × 5,Step 2: Highest powers: 2², 3², 5,Step 3: LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180,Answer: (c) 180 seconds
Q: Find the LCM of 14, 21 and 28.
A: Step 1: 14 = 2 × 7; 21 = 3 × 7; 28 = 2² × 7,Step 2: Highest powers: 2², 3, 7,Step 3: LCM = 4 × 3 × 7 = 84,Answer: (d) 84
Q: Find the HCF of 91, 104 and 130.
A: Step 1: 91 = 7 × 13,Step 2: 104 = 2³ × 13,Step 3: 130 = 2 × 5 × 13,Step 4: Common factor = 13,Answer: (a) 13
Q: Find the least number which when increased by 5 is exactly divisible by 16, 24 and 32.
A: Concept: Number + 5 = LCM(16, 24, 32).,Step 1: LCM of 16, 24, 32: 16 = 2⁴; 24 = 2³×3; 32 = 2⁵,Step 2: LCM = 2⁵ × 3 = 96,Step 3: Number = 96 − 5 = 91,Answer: (b) 91
Q: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:4 and their LCM is 84. Find the numbers.
A: Let the numbers be 3x and 4x.,Step 1: LCM of 3x and 4x = 12x,Step 2: 12x = 84 → x = 7,Step 3: Numbers = 3×7 = 21 and 4×7 = 28,Answer: (c) 21 and 28
Q: Find the greatest 3-digit number which is exactly divisible by 6, 8 and 12.
A: Concept: Largest 3-digit multiple of LCM(6, 8, 12).,Step 1: LCM of 6, 8, 12 = 24,Step 2: 999 ÷ 24 = 41 remainder 15,Step 3: Subtract remainder: 999 − 15 = 984,Answer: (d) 984
Q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 15 and 90. One number is 45. Find the other number.
A: Formula: a × b = HCF × LCM.,Step 1: a × b = 15 × 90 = 1350,Step 2: 45 × b = 1350 → b = 1350 ÷ 45,Step 3: b = 30,Answer: (a) 30
Q: Find the HCF of 75 and 125.
A: Step 1: 75 = 3 × 5²,Step 2: 125 = 5³,Step 3: Common = 5² = 25,Answer: (b) 25
Q: Find the least number of 4 digits which is exactly divisible by 15, 20 and 25.
A: Step 1: LCM of 15, 20, 25 = 300,Step 2: Smallest 4-digit number = 1000,Step 3: 1000 ÷ 300 = 3 remainder 100,Step 4: Next multiple: (3+1) × 300 = 1200,Answer: (c) 1200
Q: The product of two numbers is 1575 and their HCF is 15. Find their LCM.
A: Formula: LCM = Product ÷ HCF.,Step 1: LCM = 1575 ÷ 15,Step 2: = 105,Answer: (d) 105
Q: Find the greatest number that divides 76, 116 and 196 leaving remainder 1 in each case.
A: Method: Subtract the remainder from each number.,Step 1: 76−1 = 75; 116−1 = 115; 196−1 = 195,Step 2: 75 = 3 × 5²; 115 = 5 × 23; 195 = 3 × 5 × 13,Step 3: Common factor = 5,Answer: (a) 5
Q: Find the LCM of 18, 24 and 30.
A: Step 1: 18 = 2 × 3²; 24 = 2³ × 3; 30 = 2 × 3 × 5,Step 2: Highest powers: 2³, 3², 5,Step 3: LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360,Answer: (b) 360
Q: Find the HCF of 44 and 110 by the division method.
A: Method: Divide the larger by the smaller repeatedly.,Step 1: 110 ÷ 44 = 2 remainder 22,Step 2: 44 ÷ 22 = 2 remainder 0,Step 3: Last non-zero remainder = 22,Answer: (c) 22
Q: The ratio of two numbers is 4:5 and their HCF is 6. Find their LCM.
A: Let the numbers be 4x and 5x; HCF = x = 6.,Step 1: Numbers = 4×6 = 24 and 5×6 = 30,Step 2: LCM of 24 and 30 = 120,Answer: (d) 120
Q: Find the smallest number which is a perfect square and divisible by 8 and 12.
A: Step 1: LCM of 8 and 12 = 24,Step 2: 24 = 2³ × 3,Step 3: For a perfect square, exponent of 3 must be even → multiply by 3,Step 4: 24 × 6 = 144 (also 24 × 3 = 72, but 72 is not a square),Answer: (a) 144
Q: Find the HCF of 306 and 657 by Euclid's division algorithm.
A: Method: a = bq + r.,Step 1: 657 = 306 × 2 + 45,Step 2: 306 = 45 × 6 + 36,Step 3: 45 = 36 × 1 + 9,Step 4: 36 = 9 × 4 + 0,Step 5: Last non-zero remainder = 9,Answer: (b) 9
Q: Find the greatest number of 3 digits which when divided by 5, 7 and 9 leaves remainder 3 in each case.
A: Concept: Number = (multiple of LCM) + 3.,Step 1: LCM of 5, 7, 9 = 315,Step 2: 999 ÷ 315 = 3 remainder 54,Step 3: Largest multiple of 315 below 999 = 3 × 315 = 945,Step 4: Number = 945 + 3 = 948,Answer: (c) 948
Q: Find the HCF of 39, 65 and 91.
A: Step 1: 39 = 3 × 13,Step 2: 65 = 5 × 13,Step 3: 91 = 7 × 13,Step 4: Common factor = 13,Answer: (d) 13
Q: A rectangular room is 4 m 40 cm wide and 5 m 60 cm long. What is the side of the largest square tile that can exactly cover the floor?
A: Concept: The largest tile side = HCF of length and breadth (in cm).,Step 1: Length = 5 m 60 cm = 560 cm,Step 2: Breadth = 4 m 40 cm = 440 cm,Step 3: HCF of 560 and 440: 560 = 2⁴×5×7; 440 = 2³×5×11,Step 4: Common = 2³ × 5 = 40 cm,Answer: (a) 40 cm
Q: Find the smallest number which when divided by 3, 4, 5 leaves remainder 2, 3, 4 respectively.
A: Concept: Here differences 3−2=1, 4−3=1, 5−4=1 are equal.,Step 1: LCM of 3, 4, 5 = 60,Step 2: Number = LCM − common difference = 60 − 1,Step 3: = 59,Answer: (b) 59
Q: Find the HCF of 2, 3 and 5.
A: Step 1: 2, 3, 5 are all primes (co-prime).,Step 2: HCF of co-prime numbers = 1,Answer: (c) 1
Q: Two numbers are in the ratio 5:6 and their HCF is 4. Find their LCM.
A: Let numbers be 5x, 6x; HCF = x = 4.,Step 1: Numbers = 5×4 = 20 and 6×4 = 24,Step 2: LCM of 20 and 24 = 120,Answer: (d) 120
Q: Find the greatest number which divides 82, 102 and 122 leaving remainder 2 in each case.
A: Method: Subtract remainder 2 from each.,Step 1: 82−2 = 80; 102−2 = 100; 122−2 = 120,Step 2: HCF of 80, 100, 120: 80 = 2⁴×5; 100 = 2²×5²; 120 = 2³×3×5,Step 3: Common = 2² × 5 = 20,Answer: (a) 20
Q: Find the LCM of 4, 6, 10 and 15.
A: Step 1: 4 = 2²; 6 = 2×3; 10 = 2×5; 15 = 3×5,Step 2: Highest powers: 2², 3, 5,Step 3: LCM = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60,Answer: (b) 60
Q: The LCM of two numbers is 420 and their HCF is 14. If one number is 84, find the other.
A: Formula: a × b = HCF × LCM.,Step 1: a × b = 14 × 420 = 5880,Step 2: 84 × b = 5880 → b = 5880 ÷ 84,Step 3: b = 70,Answer: (c) 70
Q: Find the HCF of 144 and 180.
A: Step 1: 144 = 2⁴ × 3²,Step 2: 180 = 2² × 3² × 5,Step 3: Common = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36,Answer: (d) 36
Q: Find the least number which is exactly divisible by 14, 21 and 35.
A: Step 1: 14 = 2 × 7; 21 = 3 × 7; 35 = 5 × 7,Step 2: Highest powers: 2, 3, 5, 7,Step 3: LCM = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 210,Answer: (a) 210
Q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 6 and 84. If the numbers are in the ratio 2:3, find the numbers.
A: Let numbers be 2x and 3x; HCF = x = 6.,Step 1: Numbers = 2×6 = 12 and 3×6 = 18,Step 2: Verify: product = 12 × 18 = 216,Step 3: HCF × LCM = 6 × 84 = 504 ≠ 216 (inconsistent). But by ratio and HCF, numbers are 12 and 18.,Answer: (b) 12 and 18
Q: Find the greatest number that divides 58, 78 and 108 leaving remainder 3 in each case.
A: Method: Subtract remainder 3 from each.,Step 1: 58−3 = 55; 78−3 = 75; 108−3 = 105,Step 2: 55 = 5×11; 75 = 3×5²; 105 = 3×5×7,Step 3: Common factor = 5,Answer: (c) 5
Q: Find the HCF of 63 and 105.
A: Step 1: 63 = 3² × 7,Step 2: 105 = 3 × 5 × 7,Step 3: Common = 3 × 7 = 21,Answer: (d) 21
Q: Find the least number which when divided by 7, 9 and 11 leaves remainder 5 in each case.
A: Concept: Number = LCM(7, 9, 11) + 5.,Step 1: 7, 9, 11 are co-prime,Step 2: LCM = 7 × 9 × 11 = 693,Step 3: Number = 693 + 5 = 698,Answer: (a) 698
Q: Find the greatest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 8, 12 and 20.
A: Step 1: LCM of 8, 12, 20 = 120,Step 2: 9999 ÷ 120 = 83 remainder 39,Step 3: Subtract: 9999 − 39 = 9960,Answer: (b) 9960
Q: The product of two numbers is 2880 and their LCM is 480. Find their HCF.
A: Formula: HCF = Product ÷ LCM.,Step 1: HCF = 2880 ÷ 480,Step 2: = 6,Answer: (c) 6
Q: Find the HCF and LCM of 16, 24 and 36.
A: Step 1: 16 = 2⁴; 24 = 2³×3; 36 = 2²×3²,Step 2: HCF = common = 2² = 4,Step 3: LCM = highest powers = 2⁴ × 3² = 144,Answer: (d) HCF = 4, LCM = 144
Q: Find the smallest number divisible by all numbers from 1 to 10.
A: Concept: This is LCM of 1 to 10.,Step 1: Prime powers up to 10: 2³, 3², 5, 7,Step 2: LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 × 7,Step 3: = 2520,Answer: (a) 2520
Q: The sum of two numbers is 96 and their HCF is 12. If their LCM is 180, find the numbers.
A: Let numbers be 12a and 12b where a, b are co-prime.,Step 1: 12a + 12b = 96 → a + b = 8,Step 2: LCM = 12ab = 180 → ab = 15,Step 3: Solve a + b = 8, ab = 15 → a, b = 3, 5,Step 4: Numbers = 12×3 = 36 and 12×5 = 60,Answer: (b) 60 and 36
Q: Find the LCM of 27 and 45.
A: Step 1: 27 = 3³; 45 = 3² × 5,Step 2: Highest powers: 3³, 5,Step 3: LCM = 27 × 5 = 135,Answer: (c) 135
Q: Find the HCF of 66 and 121.
A: Step 1: 66 = 2 × 3 × 11,Step 2: 121 = 11²,Step 3: Common factor = 11,Answer: (d) 11
Q: Four numbers are 12, 18, 24 and 36. Find their LCM.
A: Step 1: 12 = 2²×3; 18 = 2×3²; 24 = 2³×3; 36 = 2²×3²,Step 2: Highest powers: 2³, 3²,Step 3: LCM = 8 × 9 = 72,Answer: (a) 72
Q: Find the greatest number that will divide 43, 91 and 183 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
A: Method: Find HCF of the differences.,Step 1: 91 − 43 = 48; 183 − 91 = 92; 183 − 43 = 140,Step 2: HCF of 48, 92, 140: 48 = 2⁴×3; 92 = 2²×23; 140 = 2²×5×7,Step 3: Common = 2² = 4,Answer: (b) 4

### Mixture and Alligation | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/arithmetic/mixture-and-alligation/
Summary: 42 most important Mixture and Alligation questions with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: A shopkeeper mixes two varieties of rice costing Rs 30 per kg and Rs 40 per kg. In what ratio must they be mixed so that the mixture costs Rs 36 per kg?
A: Formula: By alligation rule, ratio of cheaper:dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper).,Step 1: Cheaper = 30, dearer = 40, mean = 36.,Step 2: 40 − 36 = 4 and 36 − 30 = 6.,Step 3: Ratio = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3.,Answer: (a) 2 : 3
Q: Tea costing Rs 120 per kg and Rs 150 per kg are mixed to obtain a mixture worth Rs 138 per kg. Find the ratio in which they are mixed.
A: Formula: Cheaper:dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper).,Step 1: 150 − 138 = 12; 138 − 120 = 18.,Step 2: Ratio = 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.,Answer: (c) 2 : 3
Q: In what ratio should sugar at Rs 25 per kg be mixed with sugar at Rs 35 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs 30 per kg?
A: Formula: Cheaper:dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper).,Step 1: 35 − 30 = 5; 30 − 25 = 5.,Step 2: Ratio = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1.,Answer: (d) 1 : 1
Q: Coffee at Rs 80 per kg and Rs 100 per kg are mixed to get a mixture worth Rs 88 per kg. Using the alligation diagram, find the mixing ratio.
A: Formula: In the alligation diagram, cheaper(80) and dearer(100) go on the left, mean(88) in the centre.,Step 1: Right differences: 100 − 88 = 12 (for cheaper); 88 − 80 = 8 (for dearer).,Step 2: Cheaper : dearer = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.,Answer: (b) 3 : 2
Q: Two varieties of wheat costing Rs 20 per kg and Rs 25 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3 : 2. Find the cost price of the mixture per kg.
A: Formula: Mean price = (sum of price × quantity) / total quantity.,Step 1: Total value = 3 × 20 + 2 × 25 = 60 + 50 = 110.,Step 2: Total quantity = 3 + 2 = 5 kg.,Step 3: Mean = 110 / 5 = Rs 22 per kg.,Answer: (b) Rs 22 per kg
Q: Milk at Rs 30 per litre and Rs 36 per litre are mixed in the ratio 2 : 1. Find the mean price of the mixture.
A: Formula: Mean price = total cost / total quantity.,Step 1: Total cost = 2 × 30 + 1 × 36 = 60 + 36 = 96.,Step 2: Total quantity = 2 + 1 = 3 litres.,Step 3: Mean = 96 / 3 = Rs 32 per litre.,Answer: (a) Rs 32 per litre
Q: Rice at Rs 40 per kg is mixed with rice at Rs 50 per kg in the ratio 1 : 3. What is the cost price of the mixture per kg?
A: Formula: Mean price = total cost / total quantity.,Step 1: Total cost = 1 × 40 + 3 × 50 = 40 + 150 = 190.,Step 2: Total quantity = 1 + 3 = 4 kg.,Step 3: Mean = 190 / 4 = Rs 47.50 per kg.,Answer: (c) Rs 47.50 per kg
Q: Tea at Rs 100 per kg and Rs 120 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3 : 1. Using the alligation rule, find the mean price of the mixture.
A: Formula: Let mean price be M; cheaper:dearer = (120 − M) : (M − 100) = 3 : 1.,Step 1: (120 − M) / (M − 100) = 3 / 1.,Step 2: 120 − M = 3M − 300 → 4M = 420 → M = 105.,Answer: (d) Rs 105 per kg
Q: A vessel contains 60 litres of milk and water in the ratio 5 : 1. If 10 litres of water is added, find the new ratio of milk to water.
A: Step 1: Milk = 5/6 × 60 = 50 litres; water = 1/6 × 60 = 10 litres.,Step 2: After adding 10 litres water, water = 20 litres.,Step 3: New ratio = 50 : 20 = 5 : 2.,Answer: (a) 5 : 2
Q: A container has 40 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 3 : 2. If 10 litres of milk is added, what will be the new ratio of milk to water?
A: Step 1: Milk = 3/5 × 40 = 24 litres; water = 2/5 × 40 = 16 litres.,Step 2: After adding 10 litres milk, milk = 34 litres.,Step 3: New ratio = 34 : 16 = 17 : 8.,Answer: (c) 17 : 8
Q: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. If 10 litres of water is added, find the new ratio.
A: Step 1: Milk = 7/10 × 80 = 56 litres; water = 3/10 × 80 = 24 litres.,Step 2: After adding 10 litres water, water = 34 litres.,Step 3: New ratio = 56 : 34 = 28 : 17.,Answer: (b) 28 : 17
Q: A vessel contains 45 litres of milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. If 5 litres of milk is added, find the new ratio of milk to water.
A: Step 1: Milk = 4/5 × 45 = 36 litres; water = 1/5 × 45 = 9 litres.,Step 2: After adding 5 litres milk, milk = 41 litres.,Step 3: New ratio = 41 : 9.,Answer: (d) 41 : 9
Q: A 30-litre mixture of milk and water contains 10% water. How many litres of water must be added so that the new mixture contains 25% water?
A: Step 1: Milk = 90% of 30 = 27 litres; water = 3 litres.,Step 2: In the new mixture milk = 75%, so total = 27 / 0.75 = 36 litres.,Step 3: Water added = 36 − 30 = 6 litres.,Answer: (b) 6 litres
Q: A vessel contains 40 litres of milk containing 20% water. How many litres of water should be added so that the mixture contains 36% water?
A: Step 1: Milk = 80% of 40 = 32 litres; water = 8 litres.,Step 2: In new mixture milk = 64%, so total = 32 / 0.64 = 50 litres.,Step 3: Water added = 50 − 40 = 10 litres.,Answer: (d) 10 litres
Q: A container has 24 litres of milk and water in the ratio 5 : 1. How much water must be added so that the ratio becomes 5 : 2?
A: Step 1: Milk = 5/6 × 24 = 20 litres; water = 1/6 × 24 = 4 litres.,Step 2: For ratio 5 : 2, required water = 2/5 × 20 = 8 litres.,Step 3: Water to add = 8 − 4 = 4 litres.,Answer: (a) 4 litres
Q: A vessel contains 25 litres of milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How much water should be added so that the ratio becomes 5 : 3?
A: Step 1: Milk = 4/5 × 25 = 20 litres; water = 1/5 × 25 = 5 litres.,Step 2: For ratio 5 : 3, required water = 3/5 × 20 = 12 litres.,Step 3: Water to add = 12 − 5 = 7 litres.,Answer: (c) 7 litres
Q: A vessel contains 100 litres of pure milk. 10 litres is withdrawn and replaced with water, and the process is repeated once more. Find the final ratio of milk to water.
A: Formula: Milk left = total × (1 − x/T)ⁿ, where x is withdrawn, T is total, n is number of times.,Step 1: Milk left = 100 × (1 − 10/100)² = 100 × (0.9)².,Step 2: = 100 × 0.81 = 81 litres.,Step 3: Water = 100 − 81 = 19 litres. Ratio = 81 : 19.,Answer: (a) 81 : 19
Q: A vessel contains 40 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 8 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced with water, find the new ratio of milk to water.
A: Step 1: Initial milk = 3/4 × 40 = 30 litres; water = 10 litres.,Step 2: In 8 litres removed, milk removed = 8 × 30/40 = 6 litres, water removed = 2 litres.,Step 3: Milk = 30 − 6 = 24 litres; water = 10 − 2 + 8 = 16 litres.,Step 4: New ratio = 24 : 16 = 3 : 2.,Answer: (c) 3 : 2
Q: A vessel contains 60 litres of pure milk. 15 litres is drawn out and replaced by water. The process is repeated once more. Find the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture.
A: Formula: Milk left = total × (1 − x/T)ⁿ.,Step 1: Milk left = 60 × (1 − 15/60)² = 60 × (0.75)².,Step 2: = 60 × 0.5625 = 33.75 litres.,Step 3: Water = 60 − 33.75 = 26.25 litres. Ratio = 33.75 : 26.25 = 9 : 7.,Answer: (b) 9 : 7
Q: A can contains 80 litres of pure milk. 20 litres of milk is removed and replaced with water. Find the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture.
A: Step 1: Milk left = 80 − 20 = 60 litres.,Step 2: Water = 20 litres.,Step 3: Ratio = 60 : 20 = 3 : 1.,Answer: (d) 3 : 1
Q: Vessel A contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1, and vessel B contains them in the ratio 1 : 1. Equal quantities from both vessels are mixed. Find the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture.
A: Formula: Milk in A = 3/4, water = 1/4; in B, milk = 1/2, water = 1/2.,Step 1: Total milk = 3/4 + 1/2 = 5/4.,Step 2: Total water = 1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4.,Step 3: Ratio = 5/4 : 3/4 = 5 : 3.,Answer: (a) 5 : 3
Q: Vessel A has milk and water in the ratio 5 : 2, while vessel B has them in the ratio 3 : 2. Equal quantities of the two mixtures are mixed together. Find the ratio of milk to water in the resulting mixture.
A: Step 1: Milk in A = 5/7, water = 2/7; milk in B = 3/5, water = 2/5.,Step 2: Total milk = 5/7 + 3/5 = 25/35 + 21/35 = 46/35.,Step 3: Total water = 2/7 + 2/5 = 10/35 + 14/35 = 24/35.,Step 4: Ratio = 46 : 24 = 23 : 12.,Answer: (b) 23 : 12
Q: Vessel A contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 5, and vessel B contains them in the ratio 4 : 3. They are mixed in the ratio 2 : 1 (A : B). Find the ratio of milk to water in the mixture.
A: Step 1: Milk = 2 × (7/12) + 1 × (4/7) = 14/12 + 4/7 = 7/6 + 4/7 = 73/42.,Step 2: Water = 2 × (5/12) + 1 × (3/7) = 10/12 + 3/7 = 5/6 + 3/7 = 53/42.,Step 3: Ratio = 73 : 53.,Answer: (d) 73 : 53
Q: Vessel A has milk and water in the ratio 9 : 4, and vessel B has them in the ratio 3 : 2. Equal quantities are mixed. Find the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture.
A: Step 1: Milk = 9/13 + 3/5 = 45/65 + 39/65 = 84/65.,Step 2: Water = 4/13 + 2/5 = 20/65 + 26/65 = 46/65.,Step 3: Ratio = 84 : 46 = 42 : 23.,Answer: (c) 42 : 23
Q: A shopkeeper mixes sugar at Rs 27 per kg with sugar at Rs 33 per kg and sells the mixture at Rs 36 per kg, gaining 20%. Find the ratio of the two varieties in the mixture.
A: Formula: Cost price of mixture = SP / (1 + profit%).,Step 1: CP of mixture = 36 / 1.20 = Rs 30 per kg.,Step 2: Cheaper:dearer = (33 − 30) : (30 − 27) = 3 : 3.,Step 3: Ratio = 1 : 1.,Answer: (a) 1 : 1
Q: A trader mixes tea at Rs 150 per kg with tea at Rs 170 per kg and sells the mixture at Rs 193.20 per kg, making a profit of 15%. Find the ratio of the two varieties.
A: Step 1: CP of mixture = 193.20 / 1.15 = Rs 168 per kg.,Step 2: Cheaper:dearer = (170 − 168) : (168 − 150) = 2 : 18.,Step 3: Ratio = 1 : 9.,Answer: (d) 1 : 9
Q: A merchant mixes wheat at Rs 18 per kg with wheat at Rs 24 per kg and sells the mixture at Rs 24.75 per kg, gaining 10%. Find the ratio of the two types of wheat.
A: Step 1: CP of mixture = 24.75 / 1.10 = Rs 22.50 per kg.,Step 2: Cheaper:dearer = (24 − 22.5) : (22.5 − 18) = 1.5 : 4.5.,Step 3: Ratio = 1 : 3.,Answer: (c) 1 : 3
Q: A grocer mixes dal at Rs 32 per kg with dal at Rs 40 per kg and sells the mixture at Rs 43.20 per kg, gaining 20%. Find the mixing ratio.
A: Step 1: CP of mixture = 43.20 / 1.20 = Rs 36 per kg.,Step 2: Cheaper:dearer = (40 − 36) : (36 − 32) = 4 : 4.,Step 3: Ratio = 1 : 1.,Answer: (b) 1 : 1
Q: A shopkeeper mixes rice at Rs 25 per kg with rice at Rs 35 per kg. The mixture is worth Rs 30 per kg. If the total quantity is 90 kg, how much of the cheaper rice is used?
A: Step 1: Cheaper:dearer = (35 − 30) : (30 − 25) = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1.,Step 2: Cheaper share = 1/2 × 90 = 45 kg.,Answer: (a) 45 kg
Q: Two varieties of oil costing Rs 20 per litre and Rs 30 per litre are mixed so that the mixture costs Rs 26 per litre. If the total quantity is 120 litres, find the quantity of the cheaper oil.

Q: Wheat at Rs 15 per kg is mixed with wheat at Rs 20 per kg to form a mixture worth Rs 17 per kg. If 100 kg of the mixture is made, how much wheat at Rs 15 per kg is used?
A: Step 1: Cheaper:dearer = (20 − 17) : (17 − 15) = 3 : 2.,Step 2: Cheaper share = 3/5 × 100 = 60 kg.,Answer: (d) 60 kg
Q: Milk at Rs 50 per litre is mixed with milk at Rs 60 per litre to get a mixture worth Rs 56 per litre. If the total mixture is 80 litres, find the quantity of milk at Rs 50 per litre.
A: Step 1: Cheaper:dearer = (60 − 56) : (56 − 50) = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3.,Step 2: Cheaper share = 2/5 × 80 = 32 litres.,Answer: (b) 32 litres
Q: In what ratio must a goldsmith mix gold of 22 carats with gold of 18 carats to obtain gold of 20 carats?
A: Formula: Cheaper:dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper).,Step 1: (22 − 20) : (20 − 18) = 2 : 2.,Step 2: Ratio = 1 : 1.,Answer: (a) 1 : 1
Q: In what ratio must gold of 24 carats be mixed with gold of 16 carats so that the mixture is 18 carats?

Q: Two alloys of copper and zinc are in the ratios 5 : 1 and 2 : 3. Equal quantities of these alloys are melted together. Find the ratio of copper to zinc in the new alloy.
A: Step 1: Copper = 5/6 + 2/5 = 25/30 + 12/30 = 37/30.,Step 2: Zinc = 1/6 + 3/5 = 5/30 + 18/30 = 23/30.,Step 3: Ratio = 37 : 23.,Answer: (c) 37 : 23
Q: A 45 g gold ornament contains gold and copper in the ratio 4 : 1. How many grams of copper must be added so that the ratio becomes 3 : 1?
A: Step 1: Gold = 4/5 × 45 = 36 g; copper = 1/5 × 45 = 9 g.,Step 2: For ratio 3 : 1, copper = 36/3 = 12 g.,Step 3: Copper to add = 12 − 9 = 3 g.,Answer: (b) 3 g
Q: A chemist mixes a 20% salt solution with a 40% salt solution to obtain a 30% salt solution. Find the ratio in which the two solutions are mixed.
A: Formula: Cheaper:dearer = (dearer% − mean%) : (mean% − cheaper%).,Step 1: (40 − 30) : (30 − 20) = 10 : 10.,Step 2: Ratio = 1 : 1.,Answer: (a) 1 : 1
Q: In what ratio must a 10% sugar solution be mixed with a 25% sugar solution so that the resulting mixture contains 20% sugar?
A: Step 1: Cheaper:dearer = (25 − 20) : (20 − 10) = 5 : 10.,Step 2: Ratio = 1 : 2.,Answer: (b) 1 : 2
Q: A 50-litre solution contains 12% salt. How many litres of water must be added so that the solution contains 8% salt?
A: Step 1: Salt = 12% of 50 = 6 litres.,Step 2: For 8% salt, total = 6 / 0.08 = 75 litres.,Step 3: Water added = 75 − 50 = 25 litres.,Answer: (d) 25 litres

Q: A container has 45 litres of milk and water in the ratio 5 : 4. How many litres of milk must be added so that the ratio becomes 3 : 2?

Q: Find the sum of the first 50 natural numbers.
A: Formula: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2,Here n = 50.,Step 1: Substitute n = 50 → 50(50+1)/2,Step 2: = 50 × 51 / 2,Step 3: = 2550 / 2 = 1275,Answer: (a) 1275
Q: Find the sum of all odd numbers from 1 to 99.
A: Formula: Sum of first n odd numbers = n²,Step 1: Find n. Odd numbers from 1 to 99 form the sequence 1, 3, 5, ..., 99.,Step 2: General term = 2n-1. Set 2n-1 = 99 → n = 50.,Step 3: Sum = n² = 50² = 2500,Answer: (b) 2500
Q: Find the sum of the first 40 even numbers.
A: Formula: Sum of first n even numbers = n(n+1),Here n = 40.,Step 1: Substitute n = 40 → 40(40+1),Step 2: = 40 × 41,Step 3: = 1640,Answer: (c) 1640
Q: Find the sum of the squares of the first 15 natural numbers.
A: Formula: 1²+2²+...+n² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6,Here n = 15.,Step 1: = 15 × 16 × 31 / 6,Step 2: = (15/6) × 16 × 31 = 2.5 × 496,Step 3: = 1240,Answer: (d) 1240
Q: Find the sum of the cubes of the first 10 natural numbers.
A: Formula: 1³+2³+...+n³ = [n(n+1)/2]²,Here n = 10.,Step 1: n(n+1)/2 = 10 × 11 / 2 = 55,Step 2: Square it → 55² = 3025,Answer: (a) 3025
Q: Find the HCF of 36, 60 and 72.
A: Method: Prime factorization.,Step 1: 36 = 2² × 3², 60 = 2² × 3 × 5, 72 = 2³ × 3²,Step 2: Common primes with smallest power: 2² and 3¹,Step 3: HCF = 2² × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12,Answer: (b) 12
Q: Find the LCM of 12, 15 and 20.
A: Method: Prime factorization.,Step 1: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 20 = 2² × 5,Step 2: Take each prime with the highest power: 2², 3, 5,Step 3: LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 4 × 15 = 60,Answer: (c) 60
Q: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 60, find the other.
A: Formula: First × Second = HCF × LCM,Step 1: Let the other number be x.,Step 2: 60 × x = 12 × 360,Step 3: x = (12 × 360) / 60,Step 4: x = 4320 / 60 = 72,Answer: (d) 72
Q: Find the greatest number which divides 425, 460 and 490 leaving the remainder 5 in each case.
A: Step 1: Subtract remainder from each: 425-5=420, 460-5=455, 490-5=485,Step 2: Find HCF of 420, 455, 485.,Step 3: 420 = 2²×3×5×7, 455 = 5×7×13, 485 = 5×97,Step 4: Common factors = 5. So HCF = 5.,Answer: (a) 5
Q: Find the smallest number which is exactly divisible by 24, 36 and 48.

Q: Is 58437 divisible by 9? Justify.
A: Rule: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.,Step 1: Sum of digits = 5+8+4+3+7 = 27,Step 2: 27 is divisible by 9.,Step 3: Hence 58437 is divisible by 9.,Answer: (c) Yes (quotient = 6493)
Q: Check whether 918273 is divisible by 11.
A: Rule: A number is divisible by 11 if (sum of digits at odd places) - (sum of digits at even places) is 0 or a multiple of 11.,Step 1: Odd places (from right): 3+2+1 = 6; Even places: 7+8+9 = 24,Step 2: Difference = 24 - 6 = 18,Step 3: 18 is not a multiple of 11.,Answer: (d) Not divisible by 11

Q: A man buys 12 pens at Rs 5 each and sells them at Rs 6 each. Find the profit percent.
A: Formula: Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100,Step 1: CP = 12 × 5 = 60; SP = 12 × 6 = 72,Step 2: Profit = SP - CP = 72 - 60 = 12,Step 3: Profit% = (12/60) × 100 = 20%,Answer: (d) 20%
Q: Find the simple interest on Rs 2000 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
A: Formula: SI = (P × R × T)/100,Step 1: P=2000, R=5, T=3,Step 2: SI = (2000 × 5 × 3)/100,Step 3: = 30000/100 = 300,Answer: (a) Rs 300
Q: Find the value of 3.5 × 3.5 - 2.5 × 2.5 using a² - b².
A: Formula: a² - b² = (a+b)(a-b),Step 1: a = 3.5, b = 2.5,Step 2: = (3.5+2.5)(3.5-2.5),Step 3: = 6 × 1 = 6,Answer: (b) 6
Q: The cost of 7 kg of rice is Rs 245. Find the cost of 12 kg.
A: Step 1: Cost of 1 kg = 245/7 = 35,Step 2: Cost of 12 kg = 12 × 35 = 420,Answer: (c) Rs 420
Q: Find the number of divisors of 100.
A: Formula: Number of factors = (p+1)(q+1),Step 1: 100 = 2² × 5²,Step 2: Factors = (2+1)(2+1) = 3 × 3,Step 3: = 9,Answer: (d) 9
Q: Find the smallest 4-digit number that is a perfect square.
A: Step 1: Smallest 4-digit = 1000. √1000 ≈ 31.6.,Step 2: Next integer = 32. 32² = 1024.,Step 3: So 1024 is the smallest 4-digit perfect square.,Answer: (a) 1024
Q: Find the value of 10 ÷ 5 + 3 × 2 - 1.
A: Step 1: Division: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 → 2 + 3 × 2 - 1,Step 2: Multiplication: 3 × 2 = 6 → 2 + 6 - 1,Step 3: Left to right: 2 + 6 = 8; 8 - 1 = 7,Answer: (b) 7
Q: Find the number of odd numbers from 1 to 50.
A: Step 1: Odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, ..., 49,Step 2: General term = 2n-1. Set 2n-1 = 49 → n = 25.,Answer: (c) 25

Q: A invests Rs 5000 and B invests Rs 7000 in a business. The total profit at the end of the year is Rs 6000. Find A's share of profit.
A: Formula: Profit shared in ratio of (capital × time).,Step 1: Capital ratio = 5000 : 7000 = 5 : 7,Step 2: Total parts = 5 + 7 = 12,Step 3: A's share = (5/12) × 6000 = 2500,Answer: (a) Rs 2500
Q: A invests Rs 8000 and B invests Rs 12000 in a business. The total profit is Rs 10000. Find B's share of profit.

Q: A starts a business with Rs 12000. B joins after 6 months. Their profit ratio is 2 : 1. Find B's capital.

A: Step 1: Savings = 100% − 70% = 30%,Step 2: 30% of 30000 = (30/100) × 30000,Step 3: = 9000,Answer: (c) Rs 9000
Q: What is 60% of 80% of 250?
A: Step 1: 80% of 250 = (80/100) × 250 = 200,Step 2: 60% of 200 = (60/100) × 200,Step 3: = 120,Answer: (d) 120
Q: The population of a village is 5000. It increases by 10% per year. Find the population after one year.
A: Step 1: Increase = 10% of 5000 = 500,Step 2: New population = 5000 + 500 = 5500,Answer: (a) 5500
Q: Find the number which is 40% less than 300.
A: Step 1: 40% of 300 = (40/100) × 300 = 120,Step 2: Number = 300 − 120 = 180,Answer: (b) 180
Q: In an election, a candidate got 55% of the total votes and won by 200 votes. Find the total number of votes.
A: Concept: Winning margin = 55% − 45% = 10%.,Step 1: 10% of total = 200,Step 2: Total = 200 × (100/10),Step 3: = 2000,Answer: (c) 2000
Q: A shopkeeper marks an item at Rs 250 and gives a discount of 20%. Find the selling price.
A: Step 1: Discount = 20% of 250 = (20/100) × 250 = 50,Step 2: Selling price = 250 − 50 = 200,Answer: (d) Rs 200
Q: What percent of 5 kg is 750 g?
A: Concept: Convert to same unit.,Step 1: 5 kg = 5000 g,Step 2: Percentage = (750/5000) × 100,Step 3: = 15%,Answer: (a) 15%
Q: The value of a machine depreciates by 10% per year. If its present value is Rs 50000, find its value after one year.
A: Step 1: Depreciation = 10% of 50000 = 5000,Step 2: New value = 50000 − 5000 = 45000,Answer: (b) Rs 45000
Q: If A's salary is 25% less than B's, then B's salary is what percent more than A's?
A: Let B = 100, then A = 75.,Step 1: Difference = 100 − 75 = 25,Step 2: Percentage more than A = (25/75) × 100,Step 3: = 33 1/3%,Answer: (c) 33 1/3%
Q: Find 2/5 as a percentage.
A: Formula: (2/5) × 100.,Step 1: 200/5,Step 2: = 40%,Answer: (d) 40%
Q: The price of rice increases by 20%. By what percent should consumption be reduced to keep expenditure the same?
A: Formula: Reduction% = (R/(100+R)) × 100.,Step 1: R = 20,Step 2: Reduction% = (20/120) × 100,Step 3: = 16 2/3%,Answer: (a) 16 2/3%
Q: Find 0.25% of 5000.
A: Step 1: 0.25% of 5000 = (0.25/100) × 5000,Step 2: = 0.25 × 50 = 12.5,Answer: (b) 12.5
Q: A student scored 75% marks. If he scored 450 marks, find the total marks.
A: Let total be T.,Step 1: 75% of T = 450,Step 2: T = 450 × (100/75),Step 3: T = 600,Answer: (c) 600
Q: The ratio of boys to girls in a school is 3:2. If 60% of the students are boys, what is the total number of students if there are 720 boys?
A: Let total be T.,Step 1: 60% of T = 720,Step 2: T = 720 × (100/60),Step 3: T = 1200,Answer: (d) 1200
Q: What is the percentage change when a number increases from 50 to 75?
A: Formula: (Change/Original) × 100.,Step 1: Change = 75 − 50 = 25,Step 2: (25/50) × 100,Step 3: = 50%,Answer: (a) 50%
Q: If 40% of a number is 80 more than 25% of the same number, find the number.
A: Let the number be x.,Step 1: 40% of x − 25% of x = 80,Step 2: 15% of x = 80 → (15/100)x = 80,Step 3: x = 80 × (100/15) = 533 1/3,Answer: (b) 533 1/3
Q: Find 5/8 as a percentage.
A: Formula: (5/8) × 100.,Step 1: 500/8,Step 2: = 62.5%,Answer: (c) 62.5%
Q: The value of an article increases by 10% every year. If its present value is Rs 4000, find its value after 2 years.
A: Formula: Final = P(1 + r/100)².,Step 1: Final = 4000 × (110/100)²,Step 2: = 4000 × 1.1 × 1.1,Step 3: = 4000 × 1.21 = 4840,Answer: (d) Rs 4840
Q: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3:1. What percent is water?
A: Concept: Total parts = 3 + 1 = 4.,Step 1: Water fraction = 1/4,Step 2: Percentage = (1/4) × 100 = 25%,Answer: (a) 25%
Q: A number is 200. Another number is 20% less than it. Find the other number.
A: Step 1: 20% of 200 = (20/100) × 200 = 40,Step 2: Other number = 200 − 40 = 160,Answer: (b) 160

### Pipes and Cisterns | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/arithmetic/pipes-and-cisterns/
Summary: 42 most important Pipes and Cisterns questions with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: A pipe can fill a cistern in 6 hours. What fraction of the cistern will be filled in 2 hours?
A: Formula: Fraction filled in Y hours = Y ÷ X.,Step 1: Filled in 1 hour = 1/6 of the cistern.,Step 2: Filled in 2 hours = 2 × 1/6 = 2/6 = 1/3.,Answer: (a) 1/3
Q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours. What part of the tank is filled in 5 hours?
A: Formula: Fraction filled in Y hours = Y ÷ X.,Step 1: In 1 hour, 1/8 of the tank is filled.,Step 2: In 5 hours, 5 × 1/8 = 5/8 is filled.,Answer: (b) 5/8
Q: A pipe fills a cistern in 10 hours. What fraction of the cistern is filled in 3 hours?
A: Formula: Fraction filled in Y hours = Y ÷ X.,Step 1: In 1 hour, 1/10 of the cistern is filled.,Step 2: In 3 hours, 3 × 1/10 = 3/10 is filled.,Answer: (c) 3/10
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 12 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. In how much time will the cistern be filled if both pipes are opened together?
A: Formula: 1/A + 1/B = 1/T.,Step 1: A's rate = 1/12, B's rate = 1/6.,Step 2: 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/12 + 2/12 = 3/12 = 1/4.,Step 3: T = 4 hours.,Answer: (d) 4 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and pipe B in 15 hours. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
A: Formula: 1/T = 1/A + 1/B.,Step 1: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6.,Step 2: T = 6 hours.,Answer: (a) 6 hours
Q: Two pipes fill a cistern in 20 hours and 30 hours respectively. Working together, in what time will they fill the cistern?
A: Formula: 1/T = 1/20 + 1/30.,Step 1: 1/20 + 1/30 = 3/60 + 2/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.,Step 2: T = 12 hours.,Answer: (b) 12 hours
Q: A pipe can fill a cistern in 6 hours, while a leak can empty it in 12 hours. If both are opened together, in what time will the cistern be filled?
A: Formula: Net rate = fill rate − empty rate.,Step 1: Fill rate = 1/6, empty rate = 1/12.,Step 2: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/12 = 2/12 − 1/12 = 1/12.,Step 3: Time = 12 hours.,Answer: (c) 12 hours
Q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and an emptying pipe drains it in 24 hours. Both are opened together. Find the time to fill the tank.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/8 − 1/24.,Step 1: 1/8 − 1/24 = 3/24 − 1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12.,Step 2: Time = 12 hours.,Answer: (d) 12 hours
Q: A filling pipe can fill a cistern in 4 hours and a draining pipe can empty it in 12 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the cistern take to be filled?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12.,Step 1: 1/4 − 1/12 = 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6.,Step 2: Time = 6 hours.,Answer: (a) 6 hours
Q: Pipes A and B fill a cistern in 12 hours and 8 hours respectively, while pipe C empties it in 24 hours. All three are opened together. Find the time to fill the cistern.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/A + 1/B − 1/C.,Step 1: 1/12 + 1/8 − 1/24 = 2/24 + 3/24 − 1/24 = 4/24 = 1/6.,Step 2: Time = 6 hours.,Answer: (b) 6 hours
Q: A fills a tank in 30 hours, B in 20 hours and C (a waste pipe) empties it in 60 hours. All three are opened together. Find the time to fill the tank.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/30 + 1/20 − 1/60.,Step 1: 1/30 + 1/20 − 1/60 = 2/60 + 3/60 − 1/60 = 4/60 = 1/15.,Step 2: Time = 15 hours.,Answer: (c) 15 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 15 hours, pipe B in 10 hours and pipe C empties it in 6 hours. All three are opened together. What will happen to the cistern?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/15 + 1/10 − 1/6.,Step 1: 1/15 + 1/10 − 1/6 = 2/30 + 3/30 − 5/30 = 0.,Step 2: Net rate is 0, so the water level never rises.,Answer: (d) The cistern will never be filled
Q: Two pipes together fill a cistern in 4 hours. One pipe alone can fill it in 6 hours. Find the time in which the other pipe alone can fill the cistern.
A: Formula: 1/B = 1/T − 1/A.,Step 1: 1/B = 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12.,Step 2: B alone = 12 hours.,Answer: (a) 12 hours
Q: Two pipes together fill a tank in 6 hours. If one pipe can fill it in 10 hours, how long will the other pipe take to fill it alone?
A: Formula: 1/B = 1/6 − 1/10.,Step 1: 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15.,Step 2: B alone = 15 hours.,Answer: (b) 15 hours
Q: Two pipes together fill a cistern in 8 hours. One pipe alone fills it in 12 hours. Find the time taken by the other pipe alone.
A: Formula: 1/B = 1/8 − 1/12.,Step 1: 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24.,Step 2: B alone = 24 hours.,Answer: (c) 24 hours
Q: A pipe fills a cistern in 4 hours and another pipe empties it in 6 hours. Starting from an empty cistern, if both are opened together, how long will it take to fill?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6.,Step 1: 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12.,Step 2: Time = 12 hours.,Answer: (d) 12 hours
Q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another empties it in 4 hours. If the tank is full and both pipes are opened, in how much time will the tank be emptied?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 (emptying).,Step 1: Empty pipe is faster, so the tank empties.,Step 2: Time to empty = 1 ÷ (1/12) = 12 hours.,Answer: (a) 12 hours
Q: A pipe fills a cistern in 10 hours and another empties it in 15 hours. From an empty cistern, if both are opened together, how long will it take to fill?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/10 − 1/15.,Step 1: 1/10 − 1/15 = 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30.,Step 2: Time = 30 hours.,Answer: (b) 30 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours, pipe B in 12 hours and waste pipe C empties it in 8 hours. All three are opened together. Find the time to fill the tank.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/6 + 1/12 − 1/8.,Step 1: 1/6 + 1/12 − 1/8 = 4/24 + 2/24 − 3/24 = 3/24 = 1/8.,Step 2: Time = 8 hours.,Answer: (c) 8 hours
Q: A fills a cistern in 15 hours, B in 30 hours and C empties it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in what time will the cistern be filled?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/15 + 1/30 − 1/20.,Step 1: 1/15 + 1/30 − 1/20 = 4/60 + 2/60 − 3/60 = 3/60 = 1/20.,Step 2: Time = 20 hours.,Answer: (d) 20 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 8 hours, pipe B in 8 hours and waste pipe C empties it in 12 hours. All opened together, find the time to fill the cistern.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/8 + 1/8 − 1/12.,Step 1: 1/8 + 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 + 3/24 − 2/24 = 4/24 = 1/6.,Step 2: Time = 6 hours.,Answer: (a) 6 hours
Q: A cistern has a capacity of 600 litres. A pipe fills it at the rate of 20 litres per minute. In how many minutes will the cistern be full?
A: Formula: Time = Capacity ÷ Rate.,Step 1: Time = 600 ÷ 20.,Step 2: = 30 minutes.,Answer: (b) 30 minutes
Q: A tank of capacity 720 litres is filled by a pipe in 6 hours and emptied by another pipe in 8 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
A: Formula: Fill rate = 720/6 = 120 L/h, empty rate = 720/8 = 90 L/h.,Step 1: Net rate = 120 − 90 = 30 L/h.,Step 2: Time = 720 ÷ 30 = 24 hours.,Answer: (c) 24 hours
Q: A cistern of capacity 480 litres is filled by two pipes together in 4 hours. If one pipe alone fills it in 12 hours, find the rate of the other pipe in litres per hour.
A: Formula: Combined rate = 480/4 = 120 L/h.,Step 1: Pipe A rate = 480/12 = 40 L/h.,Step 2: Other pipe = 120 − 40 = 80 L/h.,Answer: (d) 80 L/h
Q: A pipe fills a cistern in 6 hours, but due to a leak in the bottom it takes 8 hours. Find the time in which the leak alone can empty the full cistern.
A: Formula: Leak rate = Fill rate − Net rate.,Step 1: 1/6 − 1/8 = 4/24 − 3/24 = 1/24.,Step 2: Leak alone empties in 24 hours.,Answer: (a) 24 hours
Q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours, but because of a leak it takes 12 hours to fill. How long will the leak alone take to empty the full tank?
A: Formula: Leak rate = 1/8 − 1/12.,Step 1: 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24.,Step 2: Leak alone empties in 24 hours.,Answer: (b) 24 hours
Q: A pipe fills a cistern in 4 hours, but due to a leak it takes 5 hours. In how much time will the leak empty the full cistern?
A: Formula: Leak rate = 1/4 − 1/5.,Step 1: 1/4 − 1/5 = 5/20 − 4/20 = 1/20.,Step 2: Leak alone empties in 20 hours.,Answer: (c) 20 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 8 hours and pipe B empties it in 12 hours. If the cistern is half full and both pipes are opened, how long will it take to become full?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24.,Step 1: Half tank = 1/2 of the work.,Step 2: Time = (1/2) ÷ (1/24) = 12 hours.,Answer: (d) 12 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and pipe B in 15 hours. They are opened alternately, one at a time, each for 1 hour, starting with A. Find the time to fill the tank.
A: Step 1: Work in 2 hours (A then B) = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6.,Step 2: In 12 hours (6 cycles) = 6 × 1/6 = 1 full tank.,Answer: (a) 12 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 9 hours and pipe B in 18 hours. If the cistern is half full and both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill?
A: Formula: Combined rate = 1/9 + 1/18 = 3/18 = 1/6.,Step 1: Work needed = 1/2 tank.,Step 2: Time = (1/2) ÷ (1/6) = 3 hours.,Answer: (b) 3 hours
Q: The efficiencies of two pipes A and B are in the ratio 3 : 2. If A alone fills a cistern in 8 hours, how long will B alone take to fill it?
A: Formula: Time is inversely proportional to efficiency.,Step 1: Time of B = Time of A × (3/2).,Step 2: = 8 × 3/2 = 12 hours.,Answer: (c) 12 hours
Q: The times taken by pipes A and B to fill a tank are in the ratio 4 : 5. Together they fill the tank in 20 hours. Find the time taken by B alone.
A: Step 1: Let A = 4x, B = 5x hours.,Step 2: 1/4x + 1/5x = 1/20 gives 9/20x = 1/20, so x = 9.,Step 3: B alone = 5 × 9 = 45 hours.,Answer: (d) 45 hours
Q: The efficiencies of pipes A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. Together they fill a cistern in 12 hours. Find the time taken by the faster pipe alone.
A: Step 1: Rates 3k + 4k = 7k = 1/12, so k = 1/84.,Step 2: B (faster) rate = 4/84 = 1/21.,Step 3: B alone = 21 hours.,Answer: (a) 21 hours
Q: Pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 6 hours and 12 hours respectively. Both are opened together. After 2 hours, B is closed. Find the total time to fill the cistern.
A: Step 1: Work in first 2 hours = 2 × (1/6 + 1/12) = 2 × 1/4 = 1/2.,Step 2: Remaining 1/2 by A at 1/6 per hour = 3 hours.,Step 3: Total = 2 + 3 = 5 hours.,Answer: (b) 5 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours and pipe B in 24 hours. Both are opened together and after 3 hours pipe B is closed. Find the total time taken to fill the tank.
A: Step 1: Work in first 3 hours = 3 × (1/8 + 1/24) = 3 × 1/6 = 1/2.,Step 2: Remaining 1/2 by A at 1/8 per hour = 4 hours.,Step 3: Total = 3 + 4 = 7 hours.,Answer: (c) 7 hours
Q: Pipe A fills a cistern in 12 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. Both are opened together. After 2 hours, A is closed. Find the total time to fill the cistern.
A: Step 1: Work in first 2 hours = 2 × (1/12 + 1/6) = 2 × 1/4 = 1/2.,Step 2: Remaining 1/2 by B at 1/6 per hour = 3 hours.,Step 3: Total = 2 + 3 = 5 hours.,Answer: (d) 5 hours
Q: Pipe A fills 1/6 of a cistern in 1 hour and pipe B empties 1/12 of it in 1 hour. If both are opened together, in how many hours will the cistern be full?
A: Formula: Net rate per hour = 1/6 − 1/12 = 1/12.,Step 1: Net work per hour = 1/12 of the cistern.,Step 2: Time = 1 ÷ (1/12) = 12 hours.,Answer: (a) 12 hours
Q: Pipe A fills 1/4 of a tank in an hour and pipe B empties 1/12 of it in an hour. Both are opened together. Find the time to fill the tank.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6.,Step 1: Net work per hour = 1/6 of the tank.,Step 2: Time = 6 hours.,Answer: (b) 6 hours
Q: Pipe A fills 1/8 of a cistern per hour, pipe B empties 1/24 per hour and pipe C fills 1/6 per hour. All three are opened together. Find the time to fill the cistern.
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/8 − 1/24 + 1/6.,Step 1: 1/8 − 1/24 + 1/6 = 3/24 − 1/24 + 4/24 = 6/24 = 1/4.,Step 2: Time = 4 hours.,Answer: (c) 4 hours
Q: A leak can empty a full cistern in 12 hours. A filling pipe can fill it in 6 hours. If the cistern is empty and both are opened together, how long will it take to fill?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/12 = 1/12.,Step 1: Fill rate = 1/6, leak rate = 1/12.,Step 2: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/12 = 1/12.,Step 3: Time = 12 hours.,Answer: (d) 12 hours
Q: A leak empties a full tank in 10 hours and a pipe fills it in 5 hours. From an empty tank, if both are opened together, how long will it take to fill?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10.,Step 1: Net rate = 2/10 − 1/10 = 1/10.,Step 2: Time = 10 hours.,Answer: (a) 10 hours
Q: A leak empties a full cistern in 8 hours and a pipe fills it in 4 hours. If the cistern is empty and both are opened together, in what time will it be full?
A: Formula: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/8 = 1/8.,Step 1: Net rate = 2/8 − 1/8 = 1/8.,Step 2: Time = 8 hours.,Answer: (b) 8 hours
