### Statistics | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/math/statistics-and-data-interpretation/statistics/
Summary: 50 most important Statistics questions covering 25 different types (each type max 2 questions) with full step-by-step solutions for Assam competitive exams. Useful for APSC, ADRE 2.0, Assam Police, SSC and Railway exams in Assam.
Q: Find the mean of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
A: Mean = (sum of values)/(number of values),= (2+4+6+8+10)/5 = 30/5 = 6,Answer: 6
Q: Find the mean of the data set: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.
A: Mean = (5+10+15+20+25)/5 = 75/5 = 15,Answer: 15
Q: Find the median of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
A: For odd number of values, median is the middle value.,The 3rd value (middle) = 6,Answer: 6
Q: Find the median of the data set: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.
A: The middle (3rd) value = 30,Answer: 30
Q: Find the median of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8.
A: For even number of values, median = average of the two middle values.,Middle values are 4 and 6.,Median = (4+6)/2 = 5,Answer: 5
Q: Find the median of the data set: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.
A: Middle values are 30 and 40.,Median = (30+40)/2 = 35,Answer: 35
Q: Find the mode of the data set: 1, 2, 2, 3, 4.
A: Mode is the value that appears most frequently.,The value 2 appears twice, the maximum.,Answer: 2
Q: Find the mode of the data set: 5, 5, 6, 7, 8.
A: The value 5 appears twice, the maximum.,Answer: 5
Q: Find the range of the data set: 2, 5, 8, 11, 13.
A: Range = maximum value − minimum value.,Maximum = 13, minimum = 2.,Range = 13 − 2 = 11,Answer: 11
Q: Find the range of the data set: 5, 10, 20, 35, 50.
A: Range = 50 − 5 = 45,Answer: 45
Q: The mean of 5 numbers is 20. Four of the numbers are 10, 15, 25 and 30. Find the fifth number.
A: Sum of 5 numbers = 20 × 5 = 100.,Sum of given four = 10+15+25+30 = 80.,Fifth number = 100 − 80 = 20,Answer: 20
Q: The mean of 5 numbers is 15. Four of the numbers are 12, 14, 16 and 18. Find the fifth number.
A: Sum of 5 numbers = 15 × 5 = 75.,Sum of given four = 12+14+16+18 = 60.,Fifth number = 75 − 60 = 15,Answer: 15
Q: The mean of 20 numbers is 40 and the mean of 30 numbers is 50. Find the combined mean.
A: Combined mean = (n1×m1 + n2×m2)/(n1 + n2),= (20×40 + 30×50)/(20+30),= (800 + 1500)/50 = 2300/50 = 46,Answer: 46
Q: The mean of 10 numbers is 30 and the mean of 20 numbers is 45. Find the combined mean.
A: Combined mean = (10×30 + 20×45)/(10+20),= (300 + 900)/30 = 1200/30 = 40,Answer: 40
Q: Find the mean of the first 5 natural numbers.
A: Mean of first n natural numbers = (n + 1)/2,= (5 + 1)/2 = 6/2 = 3,Answer: 3
Q: Find the mean of the first 10 natural numbers.
A: Mean = (10 + 1)/2 = 11/2 = 5.5,Answer: 5.5
Q: The marks 10, 20, 30, 40 have frequencies 2, 4, 3, 1 respectively. Find the mean marks.
A: Mean = Σ(f×x)/Σf,Σ(f×x) = 10×2 + 20×4 + 30×3 + 40×1 = 20+80+90+40 = 230,Σf = 2+4+3+1 = 10,Mean = 230/10 = 23,Answer: 23
Q: The marks 10, 20, 30, 40 have frequencies 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively. Find the mean marks.
A: Σ(f×x) = 10×1 + 20×2 + 30×3 + 40×4 = 10+40+90+160 = 300,Σf = 1+2+3+4 = 10,Mean = 300/10 = 30,Answer: 30
Q: The values 1, 2, 3, 4 have frequencies 2, 5, 3, 1 respectively. Find the mode.
A: Mode is the value with the highest frequency.,Value 2 has frequency 5, the highest.,Answer: 2
Q: The values 5, 10, 15, 20 have frequencies 3, 6, 4, 1 respectively. Find the mode.
A: Value 10 has frequency 6, the highest.,Answer: 10
Q: The mean of a data set is 25 and the number of observations is 10. Find the sum of all observations.
A: Sum = mean × number of observations,= 25 × 10 = 250,Answer: 250
Q: The mean of a data set is 15 and the number of observations is 8. Find the sum of all observations.
A: Sum = 15 × 8 = 120,Answer: 120
Q: A coin is tossed once. What is the probability of getting a head?
A: Total outcomes = 2 (Head, Tail).,Favourable = 1 (Head).,P(Head) = 1/2,Answer: 1/2
Q: A coin is tossed once. What is the probability of getting a tail?
A: Total outcomes = 2.,Favourable = 1 (Tail).,P(Tail) = 1/2,Answer: 1/2
Q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
A: Total outcomes = 6.,Even numbers: 2, 4, 6 → 3 favourable outcomes.,P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2,Answer: 1/2
Q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a multiple of 3?
A: Total outcomes = 6.,Multiples of 3: 3, 6 → 2 favourable outcomes.,P(multiple of 3) = 2/6 = 1/3,Answer: 1/3
Q: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king?
A: Total cards = 52, kings = 4.,P(king) = 4/52 = 1/13,Answer: 1/13
Q: A card is drawn from a pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a heart?
A: Total cards = 52, hearts = 13.,P(heart) = 13/52 = 1/4,Answer: 1/4
Q: A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
A: Total balls = 3 + 2 = 5.,Red balls = 3.,P(red) = 3/5,Answer: 3/5
Q: A bag contains 4 red and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is blue?
A: Total balls = 4 + 5 = 9.,Blue balls = 5.,P(blue) = 5/9,Answer: 5/9
Q: Find the standard deviation of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
A: Mean = (2+4+6+8+10)/5 = 6.,Deviations: −4, −2, 0, 2, 4.,Variance = (16+4+0+4+16)/5 = 40/5 = 8.,SD = √8 = 2√2,Answer: 2√2
Q: Find the standard deviation of the data set: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
A: Mean = (2+3+4+5+6)/5 = 4.,Deviations: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2.,Variance = (4+1+0+1+4)/5 = 10/5 = 2.,SD = √2,Answer: √2
Q: Find the variance of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
A: Mean = 6.,Deviations: −4, −2, 0, 2, 4.,Variance = (16+4+0+4+16)/5 = 40/5 = 8,Answer: 8
Q: Find the variance of the data set: 1, 3, 5, 7.
A: Mean = (1+3+5+7)/4 = 4.,Deviations: −3, −1, 1, 3.,Variance = (9+1+1+9)/4 = 20/4 = 5,Answer: 5
Q: Find the mean deviation of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8.
A: Mean = (2+4+6+8)/4 = 5.,Deviations: |2−5|, |4−5|, |6−5|, |8−5| = 3, 1, 1, 3.,MD = (3+1+1+3)/4 = 8/4 = 2,Answer: 2
Q: Find the mean deviation of the data set: 2, 3, 4.
A: Mean = (2+3+4)/3 = 3.,Deviations: |2−3|, |3−3|, |4−3| = 1, 0, 1.,MD = (1+0+1)/3 = 2/3,Answer: 2/3
Q: Find the geometric mean of the numbers 4 and 16.
A: GM = √(a × b),= √(4 × 16) = √64 = 8,Answer: 8
Q: Find the geometric mean of the numbers 9 and 25.
A: GM = √(9 × 25) = √225 = 15,Answer: 15
Q: Find the harmonic mean of the numbers 5 and 20.
A: HM = 2ab/(a + b),= 2 × 5 × 20/(5 + 20),= 200/25 = 8,Answer: 8
Q: Find the harmonic mean of the numbers 4 and 6.
A: HM = 2ab/(a + b),= 2 × 4 × 6/(4 + 6),= 48/10 = 4.8,Answer: 4.8
Q: A student scores 70 in a test of weight 2 and 80 in a test of weight 3. Find the weighted mean.
A: Weighted mean = Σ(w×x)/Σw,= (70×2 + 80×3)/(2+3),= (140 + 240)/5 = 380/5 = 76,Answer: 76
Q: A student scores 50 in a test of weight 1 and 60 in a test of weight 4. Find the weighted mean.
A: Weighted mean = (50×1 + 60×4)/(1+4),= (50 + 240)/5 = 290/5 = 58,Answer: 58
Q: Find the first quartile (Q1) of the data set: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
A: Q1 is the median of the lower half.,Lower half: 1, 2, 3, 4.,Q1 = (2 + 3)/2 = 2.5,Answer: 2.5
Q: Find the third quartile (Q3) of the data set: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
A: Q3 is the median of the upper half.,Upper half: 5, 6, 7, 8.,Q3 = (6 + 7)/2 = 6.5,Answer: 6.5
Q: The values 10, 20, 30, 40 have frequencies 4, 5, 6, 5 respectively. Find the median.
A: Total frequency = 4+5+6+5 = 20.,Cumulative frequencies: 4, 9, 15, 20.,Median position = 20/2 = 10th value.,The 10th value lies in the class 30 (cumulative 9 to 15).,Answer: 30
Q: The values 5, 10, 15, 20 have frequencies 6, 8, 6, 5 respectively. Find the median.
A: Total frequency = 6+8+6+5 = 25.,Cumulative frequencies: 6, 14, 20, 25.,Median position = (25+1)/2 = 13th value.,The 13th value lies in the class 10.,Answer: 10
Q: In a data set of the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 20, find the value of the 75th percentile.
A: Position of P75 = (75/100) × 20 = 15th value.,The 15th value in 1,2,...,20 is 15.,Answer: 15
Q: In a data set of the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 10, find the value of the 90th percentile.
A: Position of P90 = (90/100) × 10 = 9th value.,The 9th value in 1,2,...,10 is 9.,Answer: 9
Q: Find the mean of the first 10 even numbers (2, 4, 6, ..., 20).
A: Mean of first n even numbers = n + 1.,= 10 + 1 = 11,Answer: 11
Q: Find the mean of the first 10 odd numbers (1, 3, 5, ..., 19).
A: Mean of first n odd numbers = n.,= 10,Answer: 10

URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/reasoning/analytical-critical-reasoning/cause-effect/

### Complex Puzzles Test (Assam Competitive Exams) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/reasoning/analytical-critical-reasoning/complex-puzzles/
Summary: Solve floor, box and scheduling puzzles using positional, relational and calendar clues. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: Six persons A, B, C, D, E, F live on six different floors of a building (ground = 1st). A lives on the top floor. F lives two floors below A. Who lives on the floor immediately above D if D lives on the 2nd floor?
A: D
Q: Five people P, Q, R, S, T live on five floors of a building. P lives on the top floor. Q lives immediately below P. R lives immediately above S. If S lives on the 2nd floor from bottom, who lives on the bottom floor?
A: A
Q: Seven persons live in a seven-storey building (ground to 6th floor). Three persons live above C. How many persons live below C?
A: A
Q: In a five-floor building, A lives on the 3rd floor. B lives two floors above A. C lives immediately below B. Which floor does C live on?
A: B
Q: Six friends live on six floors. Two persons live between A and B. A lives on the ground floor. B lives above A. How many floors are above B?
A: C
Q: Seven persons live on seven floors of a building. P lives on the 4th floor from the bottom. Q lives immediately above P. How many persons live below Q?
A: A
Q: Four people A, B, C, D live on four floors of a building. A lives on the top floor. C lives below B. D lives above C but below B. Who lives on the ground floor?
A: B
Q: Eight people live on eight floors. X lives on the 7th floor. Y lives three floors below X. Z lives immediately above Y. Which floor does Z live on?
A: B
Q: Six persons live on six floors. M lives on the 2nd floor. N lives three floors above M. O lives immediately below N. P lives immediately above M. Who lives on the top (6th) floor?
A: D
Q: Five people live on five floors of a building. A lives above B but below C. D lives above C. E lives below B. Who lives on the top floor?
A: D
Q: A six-storey building has one person per floor. K lives on an odd-numbered floor above the 2nd floor. L lives immediately below K. If K does not live on the 5th floor, which floor does K live on?
A: A
Q: Seven persons A to G live on seven floors. B lives immediately below A. C lives immediately above A. If A lives on the 4th floor, how many persons live above C?
A: A
Q: Six boxes A, B, C, D, E, F are stacked one above another. Box A is at the bottom. Box C is immediately above A. Box E is immediately below A. Which box is exactly in the middle of the stack of six?
A: A
Q: Five boxes P, Q, R, S, T are stacked. P is at the top. Q is immediately below P. R is immediately above S. T is at the bottom. Which box is immediately above T?
A: D
Q: Seven boxes are stacked. Box X is the 3rd from the top. Box Y is immediately below X. How many boxes are above Y?
A: B
Q: Five boxes are stacked one above another. Box A is two places above box B. Box C is immediately below box B. If box A is 2nd from the top, what is the position of box C from the bottom?
A: A
Q: Eight boxes are stacked. Box P is at the top. Box Q is at the bottom. Box R is exactly in the middle. How many boxes are between R and Q?
A: A
Q: Six boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R are stacked. N is immediately above P. R is immediately below P. Which two boxes are adjacent to each other if the stack from top is M, N, P, R, O, Q?
A: B
Q: Five boxes A, B, C, D, E are stacked. Two boxes are between A and B. A is at the top. How many boxes are above B?
A: B
Q: Seven boxes are stacked. Box G is 4th from the bottom. Box H is immediately above G. How many boxes are above H?
A: A
Q: Six boxes are stacked. Box X is at the bottom. Box Z is two places above box X. Box Y is immediately above box Z. Which box is 3rd from the top?
A: A
Q: Four boxes P, Q, R, S are stacked. Q is above P. R is above Q. S is at the bottom. Which box is at the top?
A: C
Q: Six lectures A, B, C, D, E, F are scheduled on six days from Monday to Saturday, one per day. A is on Monday. B is two days after A. Which day is lecture B on?
A: A
Q: Seven employees work on seven days from Monday to Sunday. P works on Monday. Q works on the 4th day after P. R works immediately after Q. Which day does R work?
A: A
Q: Five subjects are taught from Monday to Friday. Maths is on Monday. Science is two days after Maths. English is immediately after Science. Which day is English taught?
A: C

### Drawing Inferences (Assam Competitive Exams) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/reasoning/analytical-critical-reasoning/drawing-inferences/
Summary: A short passage or set of statements is given. Choose the inference that can most safely/logically be drawn from it. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: The literacy rate of Assam has risen from 63.31 percent in 2001 to 72.19 percent in 2011, but the female literacy rate still lags behind the male literacy rate. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above passage?
A: B
Q: Every year during the monsoon, several districts of Assam experience floods, and large areas of standing crops are submerged. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above statement?
A: C
Q: A large number of young people from rural Assam migrate to cities such as Guwahati and Delhi every year in search of employment. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above passage?
A: B
Q: The Superintendent of Police said that most road accidents in the district occur at night because of speeding and poor lighting. Which of the following is implied by the above statement?
A: C
Q: A study found that villages that have anganwadi centres with regular health check-up camps report fewer cases of child malnutrition. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above passage?
A: A
Q: Tea garden workers in Assam often suffer from seasonal income gaps, because they are paid only for the days they work and work is not available throughout the year. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above statement?
A: D
Q: In a panchayat meeting, the members decided to spend the annual development fund on repairing the village road instead of building a new community hall. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above information?
A: A
Q: Many shopkeepers in Guwahati now display QR codes at their counters, and customers increasingly pay by scanning them instead of using cash. Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the above passage?
A: B

Q: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing North. B sits to the immediate right of A. C sits to the immediate left of A. Who sits in the middle if there are exactly three people to the left of C?

A: 42. (Differences increase by 2 each time: +4, +6, +8, +10, +12)

A: 243. (Each number is multiplied by 3)

### Biology - Ecology Question Bank (300 Questions, Bilingual English & Assamese) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/science/biology/ecology/
Summary: Biology - Ecology Question Bank (300 Questions, Bilingual English & Assamese) - practice questions with answers for competitive exams in Assam. Practice for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, DME, SSC and Railway exams.
Q: What is an ecosystem?
A: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with their non-living physical environment as a system.
Q: Who coined the term ecosystem?
A: The term ecosystem was coined by the British ecologist A. G. Tansley.
Q: What are the two main components of an ecosystem?
A: The two main components are the abiotic (non-living) and biotic (living) components.
Q: What is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
A: Abiotic components are the non-living physical and chemical factors such as soil, water, air, temperature and sunlight.
Q: What is a biotic component of an ecosystem?
A: Biotic components are the living organisms such as producers, consumers and decomposers.
Q: Which organisms are called producers in an ecosystem?
A: Green plants and other autotrophs that make their own food through photosynthesis are called producers.
Q: What are autotrophs?
A: Autotrophs are organisms that produce their own food from inorganic substances using energy from sunlight or chemicals.
Q: What are heterotrophs?
A: Heterotrophs are organisms that cannot make their own food and depend on other organisms for nutrition.
Q: What are decomposers?
A: Decomposers are organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil.
Q: What is a habitat?
A: A habitat is the natural environment where an organism lives and grows.
Q: What is a niche?
A: A niche is the functional role and position of an organism within its ecosystem.
Q: What is the term for all populations of different species living together in one area?
A: A community is all populations of different species living and interacting in one area.
Q: What is a population in ecology?
A: A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in a specific area at a given time.
Q: What is the biosphere?
A: The biosphere is the part of the Earth where life exists, including land, water and atmosphere.
Q: What is biomass?
A: Biomass is the total mass of living organisms present in a given area or ecosystem.
Q: What is meant by productivity of an ecosystem?
A: Productivity is the rate at which biomass is produced in an ecosystem.
Q: What is primary productivity?
A: Primary productivity is the rate at which producers convert solar energy into chemical energy.
Q: What is a food web?
A: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains in an ecosystem.
Q: What are the major functions of an ecosystem?
A: The major functions are energy flow, nutrient cycling and ecological regulation.
Q: What is ecological succession?
A: Ecological succession is the gradual process of change in the species composition of an ecosystem over time.
Q: What is primary succession?
A: Primary succession is succession that begins in an area with no soil or previous life, such as bare rock.
Q: What is secondary succession?
A: Secondary succession is succession that occurs in an area where a disturbance destroyed an existing community but left the soil intact.
Q: What is the climax community?
A: The climax community is the final, stable community in an ecological succession that is in balance with the environment.
Q: What is stratification in an ecosystem?
A: Stratification is the vertical layering of different plant species in a forest, such as canopy, understory and ground layers.
Q: What is an ecotone?
A: An ecotone is a transition zone between two adjacent ecosystems or biomes.

A: Yes. All 300 Biology - Ecology Question Bank (300 Questions, Bilingual English & Assamese) questions, answers and explanations on axomexam.in are completely free. No login or subscription is required.

### Biology - Genetics Question Bank (300 Questions, Bilingual English & Assamese) | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/topic/science/biology/genetics/
Summary: Biology - Genetics Question Bank (300 Questions, Bilingual English & Assamese) - practice questions with answers for competitive exams in Assam. Relevant for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, DHS, SSC, Railway and other government exams.
Q: Who is regarded as the father of genetics?
A: Gregor Johann Mendel
Q: On which plant did Mendel perform his famous breeding experiments?
A: Garden pea (Pisum sativum)
Q: How many pairs of contrasting characters did Mendel study in pea plants?
A: Seven pairs
Q: Mendel's first law of inheritance is known as the law of what?
A: Law of Segregation
Q: Mendel's second law of inheritance is known as the law of what?
A: Law of Independent Assortment
Q: The law of dominance was given by whom?
A: Gregor Mendel
Q: In a monohybrid cross, what is the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation?
A: 3:1
Q: In a monohybrid cross, what is the genotypic ratio in the F2 generation?
A: 1:2:1
Q: In a dihybrid cross, what is the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation?
A: 9:3:3:1
Q: A cross between two individuals involving only one pair of contrasting characters is called what?
A: Monohybrid cross
Q: A cross involving two pairs of contrasting characters is called what?
A: Dihybrid cross
Q: What is the physical appearance or observable trait of an organism called?
A: Phenotype
Q: What is the genetic constitution of an organism called?
A: Genotype
Q: What are the alternative forms of a gene called?
A: Alleles
Q: An organism having two identical alleles for a trait is called what?
A: Homozygous
Q: An organism having two different alleles for a trait is called what?
A: Heterozygous
Q: Which trait expresses itself and hides the other in the F1 generation?
A: Dominant trait
Q: A trait that remains hidden in the presence of a dominant allele is called what?
A: Recessive trait
Q: What is the cross between an F1 hybrid and its recessive parent called?
A: Test cross
Q: What is the diagram used to determine the possible genotypes of offspring called?
A: Punnett square
Q: Which law of Mendel states that the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation?
A: Law of Segregation
Q: Which law of Mendel states that alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation?
A: Law of Independent Assortment
Q: What phenotypic ratio is seen in the F2 generation of incomplete dominance?
A: 1:2:1
Q: Incomplete dominance was first discovered in which plant?
A: Mirabilis jalapa (four o'clock plant)
Q: The phenomenon in which both alleles express themselves equally in a heterozygote is called what?
A: Codominance

A: Staphylococcus

A: Diplococcus

A: Phototrophic or photosynthetic bacteria

Q: What is a wave?
A: A disturbance that transfers energy through a medium.
Q: What do waves transfer?
A: Energy
Q: What is amplitude?
A: Maximum displacement of particles from their mean position.

A: Distance between two successive similar points on a wave.
Q: What is frequency?
A: Number of waves passing a point per second.

A: Hertz (Hz)
Q: What is the period of a wave?
A: Time taken to complete one full cycle.
Q: What is the relation between frequency and period?
A: f = 1/T
Q: What is the formula for wave speed?
A: v = f x wavelength
Q: What is a longitudinal wave?
A: A wave in which particles vibrate parallel to the direction of propagation.
Q: What is a transverse wave?
A: A wave in which particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation.
Q: What is a compression?
A: A region where particles of the medium are close together.
Q: What is a rarefaction?
A: A region where particles of the medium are spread apart.
Q: What is a crest?
A: The highest point of a transverse wave.
Q: What is a trough?
A: The lowest point of a transverse wave.
Q: What is a medium?
A: The substance through which a wave travels.
Q: Does a wave transfer matter?
A: No, it transfers only energy.
Q: What is a mechanical wave?
A: A wave that requires a medium to travel.
Q: What is an electromagnetic wave?
A: A wave that does not require a medium to travel.
Q: In which unit is wavelength measured?
A: Meter (m)
Q: In which unit is frequency measured?
A: Hertz (Hz)
Q: What is oscillation?
A: One complete to-and-fro motion of a particle.

A: A cycle
Q: What is the number of waves per second called?
A: Frequency
Q: What is the time taken for one cycle called?

A: Calorie or Joule.
Q: What is one calorie?
A: It is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of water by 1 degree Celsius.
Q: What does the temperature of a body measure?
A: It measures the degree of hotness or coldness of the body.
Q: What does a thermometer measure?
A: It measures temperature.
Q: What is the triple point of water?
A: It is 273.16 K, where solid, liquid and vapour coexist in equilibrium.
Q: What is the unit of temperature on the Celsius scale?
A: Degree Celsius.
Q: What is the SI unit of heat energy?
A: Joule.

### Analytical and Critical Reasoning Practice for ADRE and APSC | axomexam
URL: https://axomexam.in/category/reasoning/analytical-critical-reasoning/
Summary: Practice analytical and critical reasoning for ADRE, APSC, Assam Police, SSC and Railway. Seating arrangement, puzzles, statement and assumption, conclusion, assertion and reason.
Q: Are puzzles and seating arrangement important for ADRE?
A: Yes. Analytical reasoning, including seating arrangement and puzzles, carries good weight and also appears in the Assam Police and APSC papers.
Q: How do I improve in statement and conclusion questions?
A: Decide clearly what the statement guarantees. A conclusion that needs extra information beyond the statement is not valid.
Q: What is the difference between assumption and conclusion?
A: An assumption is an unstated idea the speaker takes for granted, while a conclusion is the logical result that follows from the given information.
Q: How much time should I spend on one puzzle?
A: If a puzzle is not opening up within about a minute and a half, mark the possibilities and move on. Return to it after finishing the easier questions.
